title: Cat on the Rooftop
place: Teen Teen Hall, 24, Daehak-ro 10-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: The Painters
overview: The Painters is a non-verbal performance built on an unusual combination: dance, comedy, and live art-making on stage. Projection mapping adds a layer of moving imagery over the painting itself, so every scene doubles as a visual show. Signature acts include light carving (sculpting images out of light), four-panel action painting, dust drawing with its trademark reveal, high-speed drawing, marbling painted on water, and glow-in-the-dark drawing. Because the show has no dialogue, it works equally well for visitors who speak no Korean.
fee: VIP 70,000 won · R 60,000 won · S 50,000 won
hours: 14:00 / 17:00 / 20:00 · Schedule may change depending on the producer

title: There Are Machines Inside Animals
overview: A hands-on children's exhibition at the National Institute of Ecology's Ecorium, revealing the mechanical principles hidden in how animals move. Kids guess how each creature works, then test their theory through interactive displays.
place: Ecorium Special Exhibition Hall, National Institute of Ecology
fee: Adults 5,000 won · Youth 3,000 won · Children 2,000 won

title: Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony at Gyeongbokgung Palace
overview: The sumungun were the soldiers who held the gates of the Joseon palaces, and this reenactment has run at Gyeongbokgung since 2002. It was reconstructed from a record in the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty describing the gate-guard system introduced in 1469, and the costumes and weapons are reproductions of early-Joseon military kit. The ceremony proper runs at 10:00 and 14:00 in the plaza in front of Heungnyemun Gate; a separate gate-sentry ceremony runs at Gwanghwamun at 11:00 and 13:00, and there is an open guard drill at 09:35 and 13:35. All of it is free and outside the ticket gate, so you can watch without paying palace admission. Cancelled in heavy rain and on Tuesdays, when the palace closes.
place: Heungnyemun Gate Plaza and Gwanghwamun, Gyeongbokgung Palace
hours: Guard changing 10:00 and 14:00 · Gate sentry ceremony 11:00 and 13:00 · Open drill 09:35 and 13:35
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service, Royal Palaces and Tombs Center

title: At That Time, Byeonhongrye
place: Haddangse Theater, B1, 5-7 Seongbuk-ro, Seongbuk-gu, Seoul

title: JUST MALE FRIEND, FEMALE FRIEND
titleFull: JUST MALE FRIEND, FEMALE FRIEND(남사친 여사친)
place: 4F, Sewoo Art Center Hall 2, 49, Daehak-ro 12-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Sound Park Festival
overview: A free outdoor music festival running since 2016, pairing top Korean acts with the region's best local musicians in full-band live sets. Held on the outdoor stage of the Kimdaejung Convention Center alongside the Gwangju beer fest.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gwangju

title: Step It Up
place: Myungbo Art Hall, 47, Daon Hall, Mareunnae-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul

title: Art Gwangju 24 International Art Fair
overview: The Honam region's largest art fair, with 113 Korean and international gallery booths plus special exhibitions, artist talks, hands-on programs, and docent tours for first-time collectors.

title: Ganghwa Yango Ice Fishing Festival
titleFull: Ganghwa Yango Ice Fishing Festival (강화 양오 빙어축제)
overview: The Ganghwa Yango Ice Fishing Festival offers ice sledding, smelt fishing, smelt net fishing experience, making it perfect to enjoy with family. Visitors can also enjoy a variety of foods, including fried smelt fish.

title: Seocheon Maryangjin Port Sunset & Sunrise Festival
overview: Maryangjin is one of the rare west-coast spots where you can watch both the year's last sunset and the New Year's first sunrise over water, and this year-end gathering marks both with wish-making events at the port.

title: Hahoe Byeolsingut Tallori
titleFull: Hahoe Byeolsingut Tallori (Mask Dance Drama of Hahoe) (하회별신굿탈놀이 상설공연)
place: Hahoe Village Mask Dance Theater , 3-15 Hahoejongga-gil, Pungcheon-myeon, Andong-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do

title: Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony
titleFull: Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (수문장 교대의식)
overview: In the Joseon dynasty, the royal guards of the palace were gatekeepers who were responsible for guarding the the main gates of Gyeongbokgung Palace as well as the main gates of the city such as Heunginjimun Gate and Sungnyemun Gate. The royal guards worked in shift duties and were in charge of opening and closing Gwanghwamun Gate. Before the royal guard system was enforced in 1469, the palace gates were protected by soldiers of the central army. The Palace Royal Guard Changing Ceremony held at Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Gwanghwamun area reenacts the guard-changing procedure that took place during the Joseon dynasty, along with the reproduction of costumes and weapons, based on historical records.
place: Gyeongbokgung Palace Heungnyemun Gate and Gwanghwamun Gate areas
hours: [Royal Guard Changing Ceremony] 10:00, 14:00 [Ceremony of Guarding Gwanghwamun Gate] 11:00, 13:00 [Public Training of the Royal Guard Soldiers] 09:35, 13:35 * Schedule is subject to change; refer to the official website for details.* Events may be canceled in the case of rain.

title: Taekwon Beat Final
place: Taekwondowon T1 Arena, 1482, Museol-ro, Seolcheon-myeon, Muju-gun, Jeonbuk-do

title: Goods Is Good V.2
overview: A four-day showcase where creators and companies in video, illustration, and story content sell character goods and share the stories behind them — run by the organizers of the Seoul Illustration Fair.

title: The Barber of Seville
titleFull: The Barber of Seville(대학로 세비야의 이발사)
place: NOL Uniplex Theater 3, 64 Daehak-ro 12-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: 3rd Gangneung International Art Festival (GIAF25)
overview: A month-long art festival threading contemporary works through Gangneung's old spaces — the station, warehouses, the old government office, even a former clinic — around stories passed down through the UNESCO-listed Gangneung Danoje rites.

title: Jindo Miracle Sea Road Festival
titleFull: Jindo Miracle Sea Road Festival (진도신비의바닷길 축제)
addr: 74 Sinbiuibadat-gil, Jindo-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Jindo Island holds the Miracle Sea Road Festival in time for the path’s emergence from the sea. During the hour in which the path remains above sea level, visitors can walk across the middle of the sea and collect seafood such as abalone and octopus using their bare hands. The festival also showcases intangible cultural heritage performances and activities, including Jindo Arirang, Ganggangsullae (Circle Dance), Namdo Deullorae (Farmers’ Song of Jeollanam-do), and Jindo Ssitgimgut (Purification Ritual of Jindo). People from all over the world gather in the global zone for a global music trip, a global Ssireum (Traditional Korean Wrestling) competition, and an EDM night show. ◎ Jindo Sea RoadEvery year, the sea road appears during low tide and lasts for an hour a day but only for a few days. The path that stretches about 2km out to sea is referred to as Korea’s Miracle of Moses.

title: Daegu Yangnyeongsi Herbal Medicine Festival
overview: Daegu Yangnyeongsi Herbal Medicine Festival, held in the 366-year-old Daegu Yangnyeongsi, offers a rich experience of traditional herbal medicine culture. Visitors can enjoy free consultations with herbal medicine doctors, herbal foot baths, and unique programs such as Joseon Gutpan: Herbal Club and Zombie Street.
sponsor: Daegu Metropolitan City, Daegu Jung-gu District Office

title: Gochang Blue Farm Lavender Festival
titleFull: Gochang Blue Farm Lavender Festival (고창청농원 라벤더 축제)
overview: Gochang Blue Farm, located in Gocheong-gun, is a stay farm featuring seasonal gardens. Lavender and Hydrangeas bloom in spring and summer, while pink muhly grass adorns the farm in October. Spanning over 16,000 square meters, the Lavender Garden offers various photo zones, allowing visitors to capture memorable shots, especially the hanok building with lavender in the background adds an extra touch of charm. Visitors can also enjoy strolling through the bamboo and pine forest behind the lavender garden or relax at the hanok café. The farm is pet-friendly, making it an ideal destination to visit with your pet, family, or a date.
fee: 5,000 won (Free for elementary school kids and younger)

title: Future Ground
overview: An XR-sports playground where your body is the controller: dodge lasers in X-RUNNER, play virtual football in XR KICKER, and watch your drawings come alive — 16 interactive attractions in one venue.
place: Lotte Mall Gimpo Airport, 1F exhibition hall

title: Treadmill
place: Link Arts Center DREAM 1, 123 Dongsung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Paradise
place: Link Arts Center DREAM 3, 123 Dongsung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Marie Curie
place: Kwanglim Arts Center BBCH Hall, 33 Nonhyeon-ro 163-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul

title: Gwangju Design Biennale
addr: 111 Biennale-ro, Buk-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Gwangju Design Biennale is the world’s first design biennale and currently Asia’s only design biennale. With exhibitions centered on the concept of design, the biennale combines the industrial aspect of design with cultural elements.
fee: [On-site Admission] Adults 16,000 won / [Advance Reservation] Adults 13,000 won · Refer to the official website for information on discounted tickets
hours: 10:00-18:00(Last admission 17:00) / Closed on Mondays · It will operate as usual on September 1 and October 6, 2025

title: 6th Blue Sky Day Celebration
overview: A clean-air awareness festival at Seoul Plaza for the UN's International Day of Clean Air, with quiz shows, kids' speech contests, live music, and eco-friendly hands-on booths run by the environment ministry.

title: Ostrich Boys
place: Daehak-ro TOM Hall 1, 85 Daehak-ro 8ga-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Goesan Red Pepper Festival
overview: The Goesan Red Pepper Festival celebrates Goesan’s specialty red peppers and other agricultural products, offering a variety of experiences and food. Held at the Goesan Organic Expo Plaza, the festival features creative pepper-themed programs, the Organic Goesan Singing Contest, and the Hot Chimac Festival.
fee: Free (Fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Hwadojin Festival
overview: Incheon's oldest military-camp festival, now in its 36th year, reenacting the history of Hwadojin — the Joseon fort built against 19th-century foreign incursions. Costumed processions and appointment ceremonies anchor three days of performances, traditional military experiences, and night markets around Dongincheon Station and Hwadojin Park.
place: Dongincheon Station north plaza and Hwadojin Park

title: Chuncheon Forest Recreation Camp Festa & Dog-Cat Games
overview: A campground culture festa in the cypress forests of Chuncheon, 40 minutes from Seoul: live acts, slime and wood-fired pizza workshops, perfume-making, and pet-friendly events alongside glamping under the stars.

title: Seoul Africa Festival
overview: Korea's largest festival dedicated to African culture, running since 2016 with embassies and communities: music and dance stages, an Asia-Africa talent award, a fashion show of African brands, food booths, and hands-on programs at DDP.
sponsor: Africa Insight · African Diplomatic Corps in Korea · Seoul Design Foundation

title: Sanjicheon Festival
overview: A stream-side festival in downtown Jeju City along the Sanjicheon, the old lifeline of the walled town. It opens with the UNESCO-listed Chilmeoridang Yeongdeunggut shamanic rite, then runs traditional pole fishing, straw-boat making, a song contest, and family programs along the waterway.

title: 2025 Yeongdong World Traditional Music & Arts Expo
titleFull: 2025 Yeongdong World Traditional Music & Arts Expo (2025 영동세계국악엑스포)
overview: The Yeongdong World Traditional Music & Arts Expo showcases the industrial values of Gugak, traditional Korean music, sharing its joy and connecting diverse people, cultures, and regions. It features various exhibitions, traditional performances, and hands-on experience programs.
place:
Main event: Yeongdong Rainbow Healing Tourist Site
Side events: Yeongdong Korean Classical Music Experience Village
fee: [On-site] Adults 10,000 won / Teenagers 7,000 won / Children 5,000 won · [Advance reservation] Adults 5,000 won / Teenagers 4,000 won / Children 2,000 won

title: Eunpyeong Youth Festival
overview: A mystery-themed youth festival at Gupabal: solve the case of the mascot's stolen beanie through storytelling missions, with pop-up booths, western-styled duel shows, circus and music stages, and food trucks.

title: Sejong Hangeul Sulsul Festival
overview: A downtown festival pairing Sejong's brewing industry with Hangeul culture — fitting for the city named after the king who created the alphabet. Local breweries pour tastings alongside food booths, concerts, busking, and pop-up stores around the traditional market.
place: Sejong Traditional Market and Jochiwon Station plaza

title: Songdo Tribowl Jazz Festival
overview: Jazz fills the waterfront around Songdo's sculptural Tribowl building, indoors and out, with the lit-up architecture as backdrop. Now in its 11th year and a fixture for Incheon's jazz crowd. Free.

title: Jamunbak Cultural Festival
overview: The Jamunbak Festival is a celebration of the artistic life of Seoulites. At the foot of Bukhansan Mountain, the festival features exhibitions, performances, forums, workshops, and field trips that bring together artists of different generations and citizens of Seoul—who have long led Korea’s artistic culture—to reflect on and propose new directions for their own artistic lives. The festival aims to create a platform where emerging artists experimenting with new aesthetics, mid-career artists who form the backbone of Korean art, collectors, critics, students, and the general public can all engage in dialogue together.

title: Wiliams: Wiliam and Wiliam's Williams
titleFull: Wiliams: Wiliam and Wiliam's Williams(윌리엄과 윌리엄의 윌리엄들)
place: NOL Seogyeong Square Scone Hall 2, 148 Dongsung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Almond
place: NOL Uniflex Theater, 64 Daehak-ro 12-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Seongnam Festival
overview: A tech-arts festival branded 'T.A.G. Seongnam' — Technology, Arts, Game — from the city behind Pangyo's game industry: large-scale projection mapping on natural landscapes, AI sound, AR, and drones across Bundang Central Park and the Tancheon stream.
place: Bundang Central Park and citywide venues

title: Paju Folk Festival
overview: An evening folk-music festival at the Imjingak Peace Nuri open-air stage near the DMZ, asking 'What is folk?' — revisiting the genre that shaped Korean protest and campus music, with stages spilling into the plaza. Free.

title: Entertech Seoul 2025
overview: A global entertainment-technology festival at DDP hosted by the Seoul city government: K-pop meets XR, virtual idols, and games, with Korean entertainment companies and startups staging tech-driven shows over three days. Free.
place: DDP Art Hall and Eoullim Plaza

title: Goyang Autumn Flower Festival
overview: An autumn flower show at Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang, one of the largest artificial lake parks in Asia and about 40 minutes northwest of central Seoul. The planting is arranged as much for sitting among as for looking at — the point is an afternoon in the park rather than a horticultural exhibition. Free. Not to be confused with the much larger International Horticulture Goyang Korea, which runs in spring at the same venue.

title: Rachmaninoff
place: YES 24 Stage Hall 1, 21 Daehak-ro 12-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Hwaseong Urban-Rural Harmony Festival
overview: A city-meets-countryside festival by Hwaseong's agricultural technology center: kimchi-making and Chuseok songpyeon workshops, farm experience booths run by local grower groups, kids' art contests, and a trusted local-produce market.

title: Yongsan Youth Festival
overview: The Youngsan Youth Festival, a wellness-themed event, invites both youths and residents to take the initiative for their well-being by achieving a balanced state of mental, physical, and social health. During the festival, visitors can enjoy dance performances, shows by popular singers, magic shows, traditional Korean music ensembles, and a commemorative ceremony featuring congratulatory remarks.

title: 14th Gangnam Beautiful Architecture Exhibition
overview: Gangnam's annual architecture showcase, presenting 15 award winners among 289 buildings that shape the district's skyline — with a symposium, silk-screen workshops, winner building tours, and open-office visits to the architects behind them.

title: Gray House
place: YES24 Art One, 83 Daehak-ro 12-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Drone Soccer World Cup Jeonju 2025
overview: The first Drone Soccer World Cup, held in the plaza outside Jeonju World Cup Stadium over four days in September 2025, marking ten years since the sport was invented — in Jeonju. Drone soccer is played with caged drones that score by flying through a hoop, and national teams came from around the world to compete. Alongside the tournament ran a crashing competition, a super-pilot selection event, an international drone industry symposium, performances, and drone try-out sessions for visitors. Free.
sponsor: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport · Jeonbuk State · Jeonju City · FIDA

title: Jeonju International Short Film Festival
titleFull: Jeonju International Short Film Festival (제8회 전주국제단편영화제)
overview: The Jeonju International Short Film Festival highlights the potential and experimental spirit of short films while exploring new possibilities of cinema through them. Throughout the festival, both Korean and international short films are screened, including award-winning works from competitions, along with an opening ceremony and performances, also offering opportunities to interact with audiences.
fee: Opening ceremony 8,000 won / Movie screening 5,000 won

title: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish Fulfillment Festival
titleFull: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish Fulfillment Festival (경산 갓바위소원성취축제)
overview: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish Fulfillment Festival is a healing and participatory festival that blends traditional culture with modern performances. Various events and hands-on activities are offered during the festival, including tea ceremony programs, temple stay, wish pagoda stacking, meditation, and yoga. Visitors can also explore various regional products such as fresh Wachon plums and enjoy opening performances.
place: Gatbawi Parking Lot, Wachon-myeon Sports Complex
hours: Gatbawi Parking Lot (September 26 - 28) 10:00-18:00 · Wachon-myeon Sports Complex (September 26 - 27) 10:00-21:00

title: DDP Autumn Festival: Design Lounge
overview: For three days, giant drawing walls rise around DDP's silver curves and everyone becomes the artist — a participatory coloring festival where thousands of small brush strokes accumulate into one autumn artwork. Free.

title: Gyeonggi Content Festival 2025
overview: A culture-tech festival at Suwon Convention Center: immersive storytelling exhibitions, XR and AI experiences, webtoon and game showcases, and the K-Culture Trend 2026 forum — open to the public for the first time after a B2B-only debut. Free.

title: Jungnang Yongma Waterfall Festival
overview: An autumn-night neighborhood arts festival beneath Yongma Falls — one of Asia's tallest artificial waterfalls — with an open-air film night, a residents' talent concours, family bounce zones, and evening stages.
sponsor: Jungnang Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Guri Cosmos Festival
overview: The capital region's signature autumn flower festival since 2001, drawing over 300,000 visitors to vast cosmos fields along the Han River in Guri, with concerts, food streets, and family programs among the blooms. Free.

title: Goyang Street Arts Festival
overview: Goyang Street Arts Festival provides festival-goers with a chance to see various performances all in one place. From street performances to citizen participation programs, there is plenty to see and enjoy at this street festival.
place: Areas of Ilsan Lake Park and Ilsan Culture Plaza

title: Hyo Culture Ppuri Festival
overview: Held at the nation’s only filial duty-themed park, the Ppuri Park, the Daejeon K-Hyo Festa is a traditional cultural event dedicated to finding the roots of the ancestry of unique family clans and learning traditional filial piety. The festival features various experiences related to surnames and filial duty, along with popular flea markets and food zones. In 2022, it received a Special Award at the Korea Festival Contents Awards.

title: Seoul Hanok Week 2025
overview: Ten days of hanok culture across Bukchon, Seochon, and the Songhyeon green — exhibitions, lectures, tours, and performances in Seoul's public hanok, themed this year around the garden: the outdoor spaces that complete traditional Korean houses. Some 90 organizations and 50 venues take part.
place: Bukchon Culture Center and hanok venues

title: Seongbuk Street Culture Festival (Dada Festa)
overview: A 200-meter street festival by Seokgwan Elementary bringing together the district's universities, young artists, residents, and immigrant communities — global food and performances, an art market of local creators, and shop-collab flea markets.

title: Geumhogang River Wind Song Festival
overview: Daegu Buk-gu's riverside festival on the Geumho: six themed zones covering music, healing, food, and water sports, with a river song contest, mass dance performances, themed playgrounds, and an 80-years-of-liberation photo exhibition — run as a low-waste festival.

title: Gangbuk Youth Festival (Gangchu)
overview: A retro-themed youth festival at Sungshin Women's University's Mia campus: a retro game playground, teen-planned stages with an original theme song, dance competitions, a mascot contest, and guest sets by Korean pop vocalists.
place: Sungshin Women's University Unjeong Green Campus

title: Hwabuk Port Culture Festival
overview: A resident-led festival at Hwabuk Port, the old gateway harbor of Jeju, using the neighborhood's maritime history as its stage — performances and hands-on programs by the water.

title: National Intangible Heritage Center Outing
overview: A theatrical tour of the National Intangible Heritage Center in Jeonju: five costumed master characters guide visitors through exhibitions, quizzes, and digital experiences, ending with a performance or a craft workshop.

title: Dogok Metasequoia Road Festa
overview: Season two of a street festa under the metasequoia canopy along Yangjaecheon: a 30-team flea market with social-economy makers, food street, one-day classes, an outdoor library, and evening concerts by Korean pop vocalists.

title: Yeonnam-dong Community Festival
overview: A neighborhood festival in Yeonnam — the cafe quarter beside Hongdae — with music and dance stages, family hands-on booths, and markets run by local artists and shopkeepers along the back streets.

title: Hanwha Seoul International Fireworks Festival
titleFull: Hanwha Seoul International Fireworks Festival (한화와 함께하는 서울세계불꽃축제)
overview: Hanwha Seoul International Fireworks Festival, a large festival in Korea, is an annual event organized by Hanwha Group since 2000. Every year, major fireworks teams are invited to perform fireworks displays and to light up the night sky of Yeouido. The event is also filled with various subsidiary events during the daytime.
fee: Free (Fees may apply to select seating)

title: Jinju Traditional Crafts Biennale
overview: Jinju Traditional Crafts Biennale explores the relationship between nature and humankind. The materials used in the craft—wood, earth, and metal—are drawn from nature and reborn through human hands and senses. By reflecting on this relationship, it reconnects the memories of tradition and modernity, time and place.
place: Jinju Station in Railway Cultural Park

title: Special Weekends at Yangju Gwanaji
overview: Weekend heritage programs at the old Yangju government office site: traditional games, hanbok and craft workshops, guided history tours including independence-movement stories, and traditional performance stages for families.

title: Changdeokgung Palace Herbal Tea House
overview: The old royal pharmacy inside Changdeokgung — where court physicians once kept the palace's medicinal herbs — reopens as a tea house, serving herbal infusions reinterpreted from the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty in the original building.

title: Baekdudaegan Bongja Festival
overview: A native-flower festival at the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum in Bonghwa, built from blooms grown by local farms with local artists and merchants. This edition, 'Flowers, longing for stars', carries a message about living together through climate change.

title: Taebaek Festival
overview: The 44th citizens' festival of Taebaek, the old coal-mining boomtown in the Gangwon highlands, themed on the flavors and spirit of its 1980s heyday — concerts, hands-on programs, and neighborhood stages around Hwangji Pond, the source of the Nakdong River.
place: Taebaek Culture Plaza and Hwangji Pond

title: Jeonju International Hanji Industry Fair
overview: A fair celebrating Jeonju hanji — the city's thousand-year tradition of mulberry paper — running since 1997, with a national hanji craft competition and exhibitions reinterpreting the paper's industrial and cultural uses.

title: Hadong Bukcheon Cosmos & Buckwheat Flower Festival
overview: Cosmos and white buckwheat blossoms blanket the farm valley of Bukcheon in Hadong each autumn — a rural landscape festival grown from a farming cooperative, with flower fields, country food, and harvest-season markets. Entry 2,000 won.

title: Iksan Mahan Culture Festival
overview: A history festival celebrating Iksan's roots in Mahan — the ancient confederacy that preceded the Baekje kingdom — with performances and programs asserting the city's place as Korea's center of Mahan heritage.

title: Seoul Light Hangang Bitseom Festival
overview: Korea's largest light, laser, and media-art festival, rotating across the Han River's islands. The 2025 edition, 'Spectra of Light', turned Ttukseom Hangang Park into ten nights of laser-art installations, a citizen 'Light Run', and lectures bridging art and technology. Free.

title: Seodaemun Heritage Night Tour
overview: A night festival at Independence Park, where Korea's independence history is layered thick: Dongnimmun Arch, Seodaemun Prison History Hall, and the Provisional Government Memorial host literary-themed programs weaving together the writers and works of the independence era.

title: Wonju Pet Culture Festival: Animal University
overview: A pet festival built on a university theme — owners enroll in one of three 'departments' for themed games, national dog-sports demonstrations, a pet orchestra performance, a senior-model-and-rescue-dog walking show, and behavior classes.

title: Korea Drama Festival 2025
overview: A K-drama festival against the backdrop of Jinju Fortress and the Nam River: a red-carpet event and drama awards with hallyu stars, forums with actors, writers, and directors, an OST music festa, and recreated drama-set experiences.

title: World Flower & Culture Festival: Play at the Lake
overview: A night-tourism flower festival at Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang, layering world cultures and K-culture programming over the city's famous flower exhibition grounds.
place: Goyang Flower Exhibition Hall, Ilsan Lake Park

title: Gumi Industrial Complex Festival
overview: A culture-tech festival inside the Bang-rim factory of Gumi's national industrial complex, reinterpreting the city's industrial heritage through art: exhibitions and workshops by day, performances and media shows by night.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gyeongsangbuk-do · Gumi City

title: Tree Hundred Festival Uljin
overview: A recovery-and-healing festival born from the great 2022 Uljin forest fire: music and comedy stages plus hands-on programs that thank the volunteers of the disaster response and turn attention to forest regeneration.

title: Pocheon Hantangang World Drone Festival
overview: Korea's largest drone festival at the Hantangang Eco Landscape Complex: a 6,000-drone light show — the country's biggest — with artist collaboration stages, the world's first high-speed drone racing over a river gorge, drone soccer, a world food festival, and camping festa.

title: Tamna Culture Festival
overview: The Tamna Cultural Festival is a celebration of Jeju’s unique cultural heritage, including folklore, mythology, history, and daily life. The festival’s highlight is the 1.7 km street parade with over 1,500 participants, showcasing active community involvement. The event also features high-quality performances that attract many visitors.
place: Areas of Jeju Island, including Tapdonghaebyeon Seaside Stage and Tamna Culture Plaza

title: Yangyang Songi Mushroom Festival
overview: Yangyang's autumn celebration of songi (pine mushroom) — Korea's most prized fungus. Buy same-day harvested mushrooms at source, join a mushroom treasure hunt, and eat through the songi gourmet garden, with night concerts on the Namdaecheon riverside.
fee: Free entry (treasure hunt 30,000 won · gourmet garden 15,000–20,000 won)

title: K-Wave Dance Festival 2025
overview: Around 100 overseas dance fans travel to Korea on their own initiative to perform K-dance on the floating-island stage of Banpo Hangang Park, joined by influencers, professional companies, and open citizen programs — 17 Korean regions and 193 countries connected by dance.

title: Hanbok Love Incheon Citizens' Festival
overview: A hanbok festival on the lawn of Incheon City Hall: traditional and modern hanbok fashion shows — including one for pets — plus traditional performances and try-on programs promoting Korea's national dress.

title: UNICA Korea International Film Festival 2025
overview: Two days of screenings from UNICA — the international non-commercial film federation founded on UNESCO principles in 1931 — showing films chosen for beauty and humanity over violence and sensation, at CGV Gyeongsan. Free.

title: Seoul Living Arts Festival
overview: Five hundred citizen artists take the stages of Nodeul Island for Seoul's flagship amateur-arts festival — proof that the city's arts scene runs deeper than professionals — with an artist-farmer night market and family programs across the island.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government · Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Pocheon Youth Festival
overview: Pocheon's sixth youth festival, planned by a young residents' committee: opening performances, experience booths, busking, and headline concerts at the city stadium under the slogan 'Resonance — the next hour is ours'.

title: RUCKUS: the SKOOL
place: Guri Art Hall , 453 Achasan-ro, Guri-si, Gyeonggi-do

title: Green Chips Festival
overview: Seoul's sustainability festival in the Yeonnam-Yeonhui neighborhoods, styled as a walkable 'Green Chips Town': sustainable-design brand pop-ups, a village-hotel concept space, and shop-in-shop collaborations with local stores make eco-living browsable like a stroll.
place: News Museum Yeonnam and neighborhood venues

title: Gwangju Seochang Silver Grass Festival
overview: A riverside healing festival among the natural eulalia (silver grass) fields of the Yeongsan River — sunset walks through the reeds, performances, hands-on programs, and even a national spacing-out contest, in the city's only rural-scenery quarter.
place: Yeongsan River bike path center area

title: Nowon Moonlight Walk Light Sculpture Festival
overview: A month-long public-art light festival drawing over a million visitors a year: 2km of the Danghyeoncheon stream becomes an open-air museum of some 30 light sculptures and media artworks by 18 Korean and international teams, this year themed 'everyone's moon'. Free, nightly.

title: Pocheon Sanjeong Lake Silver Grass Festival
overview: The 28th silver-grass festival at Sanjeong Lake, marking the lake's 100th year: eulalia fields on Myeongseongsan mountain in full autumn color, craft and letter-to-the-future programs by day, and floating fireworks theater, lantern displays, and silent disco by night.
place: Sanjeong Lake and Myeongseongsan grass fields

title: Gyeongsan Jujube Festival & Farm Fair
overview: Gyeongsan grows 30 percent of Korea's jujubes, and its harvest fair sells the new crop alongside jujube foods, a national nongak (farmers' music) festival, and full days of stages and family programs.

title: Cheongdo World Comedy Art Festival
overview: Korea's comedy festival in Cheongdo — 'the sacred ground of Korean comedy' — with top comedians, an acrobatic hip-hop troupe from abroad, magic shows, and trot-star stages, held jointly with the Cheongdo Bansi Persimmon Festival. Free.

title: Hwasun Dolmen Autumn Flower Festival
overview: Cosmos, chrysanthemums, and sunflowers bloom across the UNESCO World Heritage dolmen fields of Hwasun — Bronze Age tombs and autumn flowers in one frame, with prehistoric-themed programs and local signature snacks. Entry 5,000 won, refunded in local gift certificates.

title: Cheongdo Bansi Persimmon Festival
overview: A harvest festival for Cheongdo's seedless bansi persimmon: sales halls of the prized fruit, persimmon playgrounds and food zones, persimmon-dye workshops and picking experiences, plus band stages — held alongside the comedy festival. Free.

title: Jeonpo Coffee Festival
overview: Busan's first coffee festival, born after the New York Times named Jeonpo Cafe Street a place to visit in 2017. Local and guest roasters — including barista booths from Japan and Taiwan — fill the cafe alleys with tastings, performances, and events.
place: Jeonpo Cafe Street and side alleys

title: October Festa in Gwangalli
titleFull: October Festa in Gwangalli (옥토버페스타 인 광안리)
overview: The festival takes place at Gwangalli Beach in Suyeong-gu, Busan, featuring a variety of programs that highlight the regional characteristics and lifestyle of Suyeong-gu. Visitors can enjoy workshops, exhibitions and sales from local cafes & bakeries, hands-on activities, cultural events, and performances.

title: Suncheon Naganeupseong Folk Culture Festival
overview: A folk festival inside Naganeupseong — the 600-year-old walled town where residents still live within Joseon-era ramparts and thatched houses. Daily life of the dynasty is reenacted where it actually happened.

title: Oeam Village Straw & Grass Culture Festival
overview: A farming-culture festival in Oeam Folk Village — a living 600-year-old hamlet of stone walls and thatched roofs. Straw craft, cauldron-rice cooking in old manor houses, traditional funeral-bier processions, and thatch-laying demonstrations keep vanishing folkways in practice.

title: Global Content Festival in Suncheon
overview: A content-industry festival on Suncheon's Ocheon Green Plaza — 'All Content Garden' — mixing public festivities (drone shows, anime OST concerts, sing-alongs) with business markets and animation awards connecting creators, companies, and students.

title: Nowon Book Festival
overview: An open-air library along the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail — the old railway turned linear park — running weekend evenings for weeks under the theme 'romance guaranteed': books among the trees, author concerts, and performances where trains once ran.

title: Jongno K Festival
overview: Jongno's brand festival since 2016, celebrating its 10th year by growing from a hanbok festival into a full traditional-arts celebration on Gwanghwamun Square — fashion shows, exhibitions, and hands-on programs over a ten-day festival week.

title: Culture Month National Festival (Seogwipo)
overview: Korea's national Culture Month event, hosted by a different city each October since 1990 — the 2025 edition landed in Seogwipo, running with the Chilsimni Festival: concerts, food, markets, and a theme performance drawing on Jeju's creation goddess Seolmundae Halmang around Cheonjiyeon Falls.
place: Cheonjiyeon Falls area and old downtown
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Seogwipo City

title: Sim Hun Sangnok Culture Festival
overview: Dangjin's literary festival, held since 1977 for Sim Hun — resistance poet, novelist of 'Sangnoksu' (The Evergreens), and film director — carrying his rural-enlightenment spirit through programs where literature and culture meet.

title: Mokpo Heritage Night Tour
overview: A hundred-year time trip through Mokpo's modern-history quarter — one of Korea's densest concentrations of early-1900s port architecture — with night lighting, performances, and programs among the colonial-era buildings.

title: Gwanak Kang Gam-chan Festival
overview: The Gwanak Gang Gam-chan Festival is a historical and cultural event held to honor the patriotic spirit of General Gang Gam-chan, a famous general from the Goryeo Dynasty. The festival is known for its impressive night events, fitting for the location named after a falling star, and features a variety of parades and performances. ◎ Gang Gam-chan and Nakseongdae General Gang Gam-chan of Goryeo is said to have been born at the place where the fourth star of the Big Dipper fell. This place is called Nakseongdae, which means “the place where the star fell.”

title: Yuseong Chrysanthemum Festival
overview: Yurim Park at peak chrysanthemum season: flower sculptures, fragrance, and evening performances in Daejeon's hot-spring district. Free, open late.

title: Seoriji Family Adventure Festival
overview: A family festival at Seoriji Eco Park in Daegu styled as an 'adventure forest' — visitors become heroes on a quest through nature-themed challenges and hands-on programs.

title: Seongju Gayasan Golden Fields Grasshopper Festival
overview: A farm-country festival in the clean valleys below Gayasan: catch grasshoppers in the rice paddies, dig sweet potatoes, fish for apples and catfish — childhood nostalgia for adults, first-time farm play for kids.

title: Heo Jun Festival
overview: A festival honoring Heo Jun — Joseon's greatest physician, whose 25-volume medical encyclopedia Donguibogam (1610) is inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World — held in the Seoul district where he was born and wrote it. Since 2023 it fills the Seoul Botanic Park lawn with traditional-medicine experiences and performances.

title: Guri Light Festival
overview: Jangja Lake Park glows through late autumn with light sculptures and photo zones built on the lake's dragon legend and winter fairy tales, plus weekend programs — LED jwibulnori spinning, face painting, bubbles — and lakeside concerts.

title: Mungyeong Apple Festival
overview: Mungyeong's mountain-grown Gamhong apples — averaging 16.5 brix, among Korea's sweetest — star in a harvest festival at the foot of Mungyeong Saejae pass, with tastings, sales, and events in the historic gateway park.

title: Korea Forest Expo 2025
overview: A national forestry expo at Gonjiam Ceramic Park with 50 institutions and 100 companies: forest-tech exhibitions, a national forest-interpretation contest, carbon-zero camping, and family programs on climate and green living.

title: Dongincheon Romance Festival
overview: A nostalgia festival on Dongincheon Station's north plaza revisiting the district's boom years: a two-day 'romance market' with the area's traditional markets, busking, retro cinema with the old Mirim Theater, and folk and pop concerts by veteran singers.

title: Gimpo La Veniche Festival
overview: A festival at La Veniche, Gimpo's Venice-styled canal town: busking from boats on the water, Venetian mask photo zones, citizen programs, a headline concert, and a fireworks finale over the canal.
place: La Veniche canal and Hangang Central Park

title: Gimhae Music Festival 'Salmon'
overview: A citizen-run forest music festival since 2006, named for the salmon returning to its home stream — as Gimhae-raised musicians come home to play. Jazz and rock band stages with markets, food, and workshops in Gaya Theme Park.
fee: Free with reservation (park admission on site)

title: Incheon Living Culture Festival
overview: One hundred amateur culture clubs from across Incheon share performances, crafts, and exhibitions in Wolmi Park for a single day — a citizen-made festival about culture as everyday life.
sponsor: Incheon Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Bbang Bbang Day Cheonan
overview: The bread festival of Cheonan — a city proud of its bakery culture — gathering fresh-baked breads and desserts in one big 'bread market' at the stadium plaza, with performances and family programs. Come hungry.
sponsor: Cheonan City · Korea Bakers Association Cheonan

title: Pyeongtaek Wonpyeong Naru Silver Grass Festival
overview: An urban silver-grass festival on the reed fields below Gunmun Bridge in Pyeongtaek — sunset light through the eulalia, evening strolls, and hands-on programs in the heart of the city.

title: Whole Family Book Festival
overview: The Seoul education office's reading festival since 2013, in the garden of Jeongdok Library in Bukchon: family reading awards, performances, creative book-linked crafts, and traditional culture programs run with local bookstores and school reading clubs.

title: The Film Delivery Man
place: Eunpyeong Culture & Arts Center Grand Theater, 16 Nokbeon-ro, Eunpyeong-gu, Seoul / Incheon Art Platform Theater C, 3 Jemullyang-ro 218beon-gil, Jemulpo-gu, Incheon

title: Seoul Silver Grass Festival
overview: Haneul (Sky) Park — a 98m hill built on Seoul's former landfill and reborn as an eco-park for the 2002 World Cup — waves with vast eulalia grass fields every October. The festival opens the park late for sunset and night walks through the silver grass with the city skyline beyond. One of Seoul's defining autumn scenes.

title: Daegu Dong-gu Harmony Festival (Dududadong)
overview: The autumn finale of Dong-gu's seasonal festival series: a sports day, national trot singing contest, harmony concert, pop-up playground, lifelong-learning fair, and laser survival games at Yulha Sports Park.

title: Guro Youth Festival
overview: A tenth-anniversary youth festival planned and run by Guro's teen council 'Greennarae', themed 'Own Game, Own GURO': sports reimagined as festival games, club performances, a career fair, science fair, and a K-pop guest stage.

title: Hanbok Culture Week
overview: Korea's national hanbok week, held every third week of October with 330 participating venues nationwide: fashion shows, performances, and try-on programs under the banner 'Modern Hanbokpan', with satellite events in Hong Kong, New York, and Berlin.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Seomjinggang Interntional Experimental Arts Festvial
overview: The Seomjinggang International Experimental Arts Festival is a traditional art festival that takes place in Gokseong, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City . The festival invites over 100 artists from around the world, and "seeks to explore the philosophical, ecological, and artistic meanings and values encapsulated by the river."

title: Yesan Jangteo Three Kingdoms Festival
titleFull: Yesan Jangteo Three Kingdoms Festival (예산장터 삼국축제)
overview: The Yesan Jangteo Three Kingdoms Festival revolves around three themes: chrysanthemums, Korean rice soup, and noodles. Visitors can enjoy a variety of foods and experience the culture unique to Yesan Market.

title: Jeongdong Culture Festival
overview: A street festival on Jeongdong-gil — the stone-wall lane by Deoksugung Palace that was the diplomatic quarter of the Korean Empire. Street performances, retro arcades, pump-organ playing, and caricature booths along one of Seoul's most beloved walks.

title: Ganggyeong Jeotgal Festival
overview: Ganggyeong was once one of Joseon's three great markets, and its salted-seafood (jeotgal) trade survives as Korea's largest — this riverside festival celebrates that pungent heritage with tastings, kimchi-making with fresh jeotgal, and themed riverside lounges on the Geumgang.

title: Namdo Film Festival Season 2: Gwangyang
overview: A traveling film festival touring Jeonnam's 22 cities and counties — season two lands in Gwangyang, the city of light and steel, for five days of competition and open-air screenings in plazas, museums, and even container docks.

title: La La La Festival
overview: Busan Geumjeong's coffee-and-bread festival on the Oncheoncheon stream below Pusan National University station — 'Drink the coffee! Eat the bread! Enjoy the culture!' — with local roasters, bakeries, and stages.

title: Gwangmyeong Cave Light Festival
overview: A light festival at Gwangmyeong Cave — the abandoned gold mine turned culture space — themed on the whale as a messenger of hope and climate awareness, pairing cave light art with an eco-consumption campaign.

title: Garak Oktoberfest Gourmet Night
overview: A rooftop Oktoberfest on the sky garden of Garak Market — Korea's largest wholesale food market: 20 craft breweries, barbecue and camping vibes, market-fresh cooking pop-ups, and chef battles featuring Culinary Class Wars alumni.

title: Iksan Ten Million Chrysanthemum Festival
overview: Korea's biggest chrysanthemum festival: ten million blooms shaped into giant sculptures — phoenixes, Baekje gates, dragons — plus the country's largest chrysanthemum garden, bonsai exhibitions, music fountains, and night lighting.

title: Danyang Ondal Culture Festival
overview: Korea's only Goguryeo-kingdom festival, built on the legend of General Ondal and Princess Pyeonggang at Danyang's riverside drama-set park: period costume experiences, a recreated Goguryeo market street, and free entry to the Ondal filming location during the festival.

title: Hapcheon Hwangto Hanwoo Festival
overview: Hapcheon's red-clay-raised hanwoo beef gets a three-day showcase — 'Come! Try! Taste! Buy!' — with grill zones, performances, and county food at the sports park.

title: Jeonju Bibimbap Festival
overview: The Jeonju Bibimbap Festival celebrates the taste and charm of one of Korea's representative foods in the city of it's origin, Jeonju. The city has been recognized by UNESCO as a City of Gastronomy, and the festival promotes this branding. Visitors to the festival can enjoy a variety of immersive programs, including hadns-on activities and performances centered on Jeonju bibimbap.

title: Music Performers Festival 2025
overview: Jeju musicians and mainstream Korean artists share a seaside stage at Tapdong Beach Theater — a festival by the musicians' union where live performance meets the ocean horizon. Free, evenings.

title: Jeonnam World Gimbap Festival
overview: A festival for Korea's favorite seaweed roll in the province that grows most of the country's gim: specialty gimbap from all 22 Jeonnam counties, cooking competitions, live auctions, art-gimbap making, and multicultural gimbap workshops in Mokpo.
place: Mokpo Culture & Arts Center outdoor stage

title: Yongmaru Forest Trail Festival
overview: Nine weekend days of healing along the Gyeongui Line Forest Trail in Yongsan: busking, one-day classes, street performances, and pop-up markets with local merchants under the slogan 'my healing oasis in the city'.

title: Yangyang Salmon Festival
overview: Every autumn salmon return up the Namdaecheon to spawn, and Yangyang celebrates with Korea's famous bare-hand salmon catching, salmon cooking shows, ecology programs, and riverside night stages. A living nature lesson for kids and a feast for adults.

title: Jeju Reading Festival
overview: Jeju's largest book festival at Udang Library: author lectures, character-costume parades, book-themed AI chats, reading clinics, and family programs under the year's theme 'utterly fallen for books'.

title: Gijang Conger Eel Festival in Chiram
overview: The 19th sea-eel festival in the fishing village of Chiram, Busan: free conger-eel bibimbap tastings, bare-hand eel catching, quiz shows, a national song contest, and fireworks over the autumn sea.

title: Korea Chrysanthemum Grand Festival (Hampyeong)
overview: Hampyeong's signature autumn show — 'Magic Chrysanthemum Land': carousel, ferris wheel, and giant cups built entirely of chrysanthemums across the Expo Park, with food streets under the fragrance.

title: Tripitaka Koreana Cultural Festival
overview: The Tripitaka Koreana Cultural Festival showcases the cultural values of  Tripitaka Koreana combined with vibrant content featuring splendid autumn flowers. Visitors can enjoy fall flowers and take part in various hands-on activities.
place: Theme Park of the Tripitaka Koreana
fee: Free (Fee applies for hands-on experience programs)

title: Yeongdeungpo Seonyudo Garden Festival
overview: Autumn on Seonyudo — the water-plant island park in the Han River rebuilt from an old filtration plant: book festival, flea market, yoga and birdwatching walks, ballet and gugak performances among the ivy-covered structures.

title: Goyang Animal-Assisted Healing Festival
overview: A pet culture festival on Ilsan Culture Plaza themed on animal-assisted healing: pet fashion show, mini sports day, agility demos, free animal registration, behavior classes, therapy zones, and a pet run across seven themed sectors.

title: Gangjin Bay Dancing Reeds Festival
overview: Sunset over the reed beds of Gangjin Bay Eco Park — home to 1,572 recorded species — with boardwalk ecology walks, performances against the estuary light, and children's nature programs.

title: Jeongeupsa Culture Festival
overview: Jeongeup's flagship festival since 1990, honoring the devoted wife of 'Jeongeupsa' — the only surviving Baekje-era song in Korean — with performances and programs at the culture park named for her.

title: Bohyeonsa Temple Millennium Culture Festival
overview: A temple festival at thousand-year-old Bohyeonsa near Gangneung: mountain-spirit rites, tea ceremonies for the temple's three great masters, healing temple concerts, Korean and Chinese tea tastings, ceramics exhibitions, and temple-food showcases.

title: Pohang Steel Art Festival 2025
overview: The steel city's signature art festival: sculptures and installations exploring iron as material and metaphor, made with artists, steel companies, and steelworkers at the Dongbin Culture Warehouse 1969 on the harbor.

title: Black Music Festival
overview: The Black Music Festival feature performances across various genres, including hip hop, R&B, soul form both local artists and international artists. Along with performances, visitors can enjoy various cultural events and hands-on experience programs.

title: Byeolgil Market
overview: A neighborhood culture market on the street from Gileum Station to Mia Elementary: less-waste market with local shops, a youth start-up market, art market, and jazz, dance, and magic stages — building a walkable family street.

title: Cheongnamdae Autumn Festival
overview: Autumn at Cheongnamdae — the former presidential villa on Daecheong Lake, opened to the public in 2003: foliage walks, chrysanthemum bonsai exhibitions, daily music performances, and a winery corner on the lakeside grounds.

title: 7th Black Music Festival (BMF)
overview: Hip-hop, R&B, and soul on a former US Army base: Camp Red Cloud in Uijeongbu, used by the military for 70 years, hosts top Korean and international acts as the city reclaims the space for culture.

title: Yeosu Dongdong Drum Festival
overview: A drum festival rooted in the Goryeo-era song 'Dongdong' and General Yu Tak, Yeosu's forgotten defender: a citizen drum parade through the streets, drum competitions, EDM and guest stages at the old naval shipyard site.
place: Seonso shipyard site and Yonggi Park

title: Incheon Wondosa Rite & Nakseom Festival
overview: A revival of the Joseon-era Wondosa rite, in which Incheon's magistrate honored the spirits of the West Sea islands on Nakseom Island each spring and autumn — reenacted with a procession and village festival in Michuhol.

title: Sea in the City Festival (Noryangjin)
overview: The capital's biggest seafood festival at Noryangjin Fish Market: tuna-cutting shows, auctioneer experiences, grilled-fish streets, shrimp-net fishing for kids, K-trot concerts, and direct-from-the-boat markets from fishing co-ops nationwide.
place: Noryangjin Fish Market and sports fields

title: WOW Let's Play! Yangpyeong Festa
overview: The Yangpyeong education campus becomes one big playground: booknic picnics, campus-wide treasure hunts and stamp rallies, a five-senses play zone, future-tech studio, and eco-craft workshops for families. Free.

title: Yangcheon Family Street Festival
overview: A 900-meter stretch by Sinjeongnegeori Station becomes a family commons for a day — generations sharing each other's culture through stages, booths, and street programs.

title: 20th Humanities Week
overview: Korea's national humanities week — 29 universities and institutes sharing research with the public through lectures, exhibitions, performances, and field trips, themed 'connecting again: region and community through the humanities'.
place: National Research Foundation, Daejeon and venues nationwide

title: Urban Forest Art Healing: Garden of Quiet Breath
Fraternité
place: Link Arts Center DREAM Theater 3, 123 Dongsung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Incheon Global Education Fair
overview: An open education festival at Songdo Convensia: world-culture booths run by foreign embassies, 80 exhibition booths on Incheon's future industries — aviation, robotics, metaverse — a Hyundai future-mobility hall, and student stages.

title: Gangneung Noodle Festival
overview: Gangneung may be Korea's best noodle city — jang-kalguksu, buckwheat makguksu, potato-dumpling soup — and this festival on Wolhwa Street serves them all at 5,000 won a bowl, mapping the city's famous and hidden noodle houses.

title: Hongcheon Apple Festival
overview: Apples from Hongcheon's high valleys — Hongro, Arisu, Sinano Gold, Envy, Fuji — sold at source in the Tori Forest park, with stages, events, and autumn programs.

title: Wolchulsan Chrysanthemum Festival
overview: Chrysanthemum sculptures and photo zones fill Gichan Land at the foot of Wolchulsan — the jagged 'Matterhorn of the south' — for a fragrant, free autumn stroll in Yeongam.

title: Yanggu Punchbowl Siraegi & Apple Festival
overview: A harvest festival in the Punchbowl — the famous crater-like basin near the DMZ in Yanggu — celebrating its two specialties: siraegi (dried radish greens) and highland apples, with markets and programs at the healing house grounds.

title: Cheonhamu-Bbong
place: Daehak-ro Ieum Center Ieum Hall, 112 Daehak-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Busan Mackerel Festival
overview: Songdo Beach — Korea's first public beach — hosts this tribute to the national fish since 2008. Busan lands 90 percent of Korea's mackerel, and the festival leans in: bare-hand mackerel catching, surprise auctions, kayak fishing games, paper-boat races, and a big seafood market by the cable car.

title: Beauty Some Suwon 2025
overview: A K-beauty expo at Suwon Convention Center covering cosmetics, derma and aesthetics, hair and nail, fragrance, inner beauty, and beauty devices — with an AI beauty-tech hall, export fairs, and hands-on citizen programs. Free with pre-registration.

title: Suncheon Food & Art Festival
overview: Suncheon closes its central boulevard for a festival where local-ingredient street food meets hands-on art: snack stalls, street performances, and street art down the middle of the road.

title: Buyeo Chrysanthemum Festival
overview: Ten days of chrysanthemums at Gungnamji — Korea's oldest artificial pond, built by Baekje kings — with flower sculptures found only here: the Great Gilt-bronze Incense Burner and Sabi Gate rendered entirely in blooms, across six themed zones. Free, open to 21:00.

title: Yeongnam-Honam Traditional Market Expo
overview: Traditional-market merchants from Busan and Jeonnam — Korea's historically rival southeast and southwest — trade specialties side by side at Busan Citizens Park, with quiz shows, merchant talent stages, and market troupe performances.

title: Icheon Ginseng Festival
overview: The Icheon Ginseng Festival has been held annually since 2015 to promote the benefits and value of the locally grown ginseng. The festival features sales as well as events.
place: Donggyeonggi Ginseng Farmers Association Icheon Ginseng Sales Center

title: Jeonju Makgeolli Festival
overview: Jeonju's rice-wine festival: classic makgeolli with its perfect companions — yukjeon, samhap, pajeon — alongside fruit makgeolli and cocktail shows for younger drinkers, moju-brewing workshops, and fusion-gugak-to-EDM stages.

title: Dronebot Festival
overview: A civil-military drone festival at Ganapri Airfield co-hosted by Gyeonggi Province, Yangju City, and the ROK Ground Operations Command: army dronebot combat-system demos, US Forces Korea equipment displays, drone-robot company exhibitions, competitions, and military culture shows.
sponsor: Gyeonggi Province · Yangju City · ROK Ground Operations Command

title: Treasure Hunt Festival: Find the Gold Bars!
overview: Iksan — home of Korea's only jewelry industrial complex — turns a persistent local legend into a festival: two tons of gold bars said to be buried under a colonial-era farm warehouse. AR and RPG technology transform the heritage village into a treasure-hunt stage.

title: Gangdong Book Festival
overview: The 16th reading festival of Gangdong, marking the opening of the new Gangdong Central Library under the theme 'THE LIBRARY: 도서관+': announcer-hosted lectures and piano-accompanied readings, publisher booths, and library goods.
place: Gangdong Central Library and Dunchon Park

title: Gimpo Marine Corps Culture Festival
overview: A Marine Corps culture festival at Gimpo's warship park: equipment displays and rides, the Blue Dragon unit departure ceremony, honor guard and military band shows, and army-style food — the ROK Marines up close.
place: Gimpo Warship Park and Daemyeong Port

title: Downtown Night Tour: The Season for Jeju Island Nights
titleFull: Downtown Night Tour: The Season for Jeju Island Nights (원도심 야간여행 ‘섬夜시즌’ 운영)
overview: The festival features various performances and events, making it perfect for enjoying Jeju's autumn ambiance with family, friends, or loved ones. It also features the Season Night Walk, allowing participants to momentarily set aside their daily busyness and connect with nature in the serene night. The course takes visitors along landmarks by the night sea.

title: National Agricultural Museum Festival: Rest, Stay
overview: The National Agricultural Museum's harvest-season festival: a silent-disco DJ party in the botanical garden, artist performances, classical concerts, perfume workshops, and treasure hunts — plus its autumn special exhibitions.

title: Ginkgo Tree Road Street Arts Festival
overview: Asan's famous ginkgo avenue at golden peak becomes a circus carnival: non-verbal street performances — circus, mime, juggling, percussion — with kids' circus workshops and local produce markets under the yellow canopy.

title: Unjeong Lake Park Fireworks Festival
overview: Paju's resident-founded fireworks festival, in its seventh year: a headline fireworks show over Unjeong Lake with light installations and local performances through the afternoon and evening.

title: Ansan Science Valley (ASV) Science Festival
overview: Ansan's brand science festival at Hanyang University ERICA: robots, space engineering, and future-tech exhibitions from the science valley's institutes and companies, fused with performances and hands-on booths that make it all approachable.

title: Busan Jung-gu Pet Festival
overview: Busan Jung-gu Pet Festival is a pet cultural event featuring various programs such as walking programs, health consultations, and behavior training programs that pets and their owners can participate in together. The event aims to spread the culture of responsible pet ownership and revitalize the local pet industry.

title: Busan Street Festa in Gwangbok
titleFull: Busan Street Festa in Gwangbok (부산 스트릿 페스타 인 광복)
overview: The Busan Street Festa in Gwangbok transforms everyday urban spaces into a festival stage through various programs such as music, dance, performance shows, local flea markets, and parades that unfold throughout the streets.

title: 14th Asian Bird Fair (Seosan)
overview: Asia's largest bird-watching gathering lands at Seosan Birdland by the Cheonsuman Bay — one of the world's great migratory stopovers. Bird groups and eco-tourism operators from across Asia gather for a weekend of watching, talks, and exhibitions.

title: Anseong Fitting Festival: Tok-Tok Sweet
overview: The 27th arts festival of Anseong's artist federation at the Yongseol lake stage: K-pop cover dance, kids' dance time, magic shows, musical gala, busking, an art market, and bounce zones — a generation-bridging family day out.

title: Real Treasure Festival
overview: A smartphone-based spy adventure at the old Gyeonggi provincial office: participants become secret agents solving missions through the historic building — CODENAME: H, spy hunter games, a mystery theme park, and an alien-capture operation. Free with reservation.

title: Gourmet Eat Gangnam
titleFull: Gourmet Eat Gangnam (제2회 고메 잇 강남)
overview: Marking its second anniversary, this year's Gourmet Eat Gangnam highlights the theme of gourmet festival, featuring a chef cooking show with 100 different menu items. The event takes place from November 4 to 16 at the plaza in front of COEX’s East Gate. As an F&B festival at the heart of the city, it offers visitors the opportunity to enjoy delicious food and drinks while engaging in a variety of activities.

title: Gwangju Women's Film Festival
overview: An annual film festival amplifying women filmmakers: screenings with workshops, seminars, and panel talks that push both craft conversation and gender equality in Korean cinema.

title: Hadong Byeolmat (Star Taste) Festival
overview: A food festival rediscovering Hadong's own flavors: the Seomjin River corbicula soup made famous by K-dramas, the clear chicken harvest soup farmers ate at threshing time, and a hundred local tastes with riverside stages.

title: Jukbyeon Port Seafood Festival
overview: Uljin's harbor festival at Jukbyeon Port: bare-hand fish catching, seafood butchering shows, mulhoe performances, on-the-spot auctions, and a fishing-boat parade against the East Sea, with trot stars at the opening concert.

title: Yeongdo Bridge Festival
overview: A festival celebrating Busan's beloved bascule bridge and the island district it connects: a 43-meter runway stage hosts the Yeongdo Dynamic Dancing Festival, with exhibitions and experiences linking the island's history, sea, and people.

title: 19th Jeonbuk Youth Film Festival
overview: A film festival of works made by teenagers — national and Jeonbuk sections with screenings, awards, and director talks under the slogan 'awkward is okay', in Jeonju's cinema district.

title: Yanggang Island Arts Festival
overview: Yangpyeong's brand arts festival by the river, this year centered on gugak — traditional Korean music meeting contemporary staging — with performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs in the county's riverside parkland.

title: Incheon Airport Sky Festival
overview: The world's only airport mega-festival, running since 2004 and rebranded for its 20th edition at the Inspire Resort: two days of K-pop headliners (past lineups include Highlight, Crush, Heize, Sung Si-kyung) plus K-drama and craft culture zones. Free.

title: Yeosu Night Sea Fireworks Festival
overview: Fireworks over the water that inspired Korea's most famous night-sea ballad: music-synchronized shows above Jangundo Island off Yi Sun-sin Square, with performances along the old harbor. Free — arrive early; the waterfront fills fast.
place: Yi Sun-sin Square and harbor waters

title: Incheon Local Festa
titleFull: Incheon Local Festa (Jemulpo Wave Market) (인천 로컬 페스타 (제물포 웨이브 마켓))
overview: Jaemulpo Wave Market is a special festival where one can explore the many different local brands in Incheon. Approximately 70 Incheon-based brands are participating to promote handmade products, home decor items, lifestyle  goods and more. During the festival period, Jemulpo Wave Vintage Market also takes place with 20 vintage sellers showcasing timeless products. Entertaining events are also planned, such as a DJ show, vintage auction, beer drinking contest, and more.

title: Changwon Industrial Complex Culture Festival
overview: A culture festival for the workers and neighbors of Changwon's industrial complex: opening performances, concerts, an exhibition of the complex's transformation, content booths, and a workers' singing contest — industry read through culture.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Changwon City

title: Open Port Dog Library
overview: A book-and-dog festival on Incheon's 1883 Open Port Plaza: reading lounges where dogs are welcome, a free-run and agility course, walking-training and grooming classes, pet tarot and crafts, and a local pet-goods market.

title: Dongmyeong Coffee Walk
overview: Gwangju's cafe-quarter festival in Dongmyeong-dong: tasting passports with flavor voting ('Just Award'), a cafe-tour-plus-exhibition walk, local makers' market, ateliers, and lounge stages across the neighborhood by the Asia Culture Center.

title: Hangang & Mountains Trekking (2nd)
overview: Seoul's citizen trekking series pairing river and mountain courses with themed rounds — family, couples, singles, dog-walking, fashion — up to 600 walkers per round with course events along the way.

title: Gyeonggi Kimchi Festa
overview: A kimchi expo ahead of kimjang season: a national kimchi competition, make-your-own workshops, a communal kimjang for sharing, ingredient markets, and master-artisan kimchi exhibitions at Suwon Convention Center.

title: Gyeongbuk Apple Fair (Seoul)
overview: Fourteen apple-growing counties of Gyeongbuk bring the new harvest to Seoul Plaza: premium apple exhibitions, sculpture displays, tastings of every major variety, and direct sales at grower prices for three days.

title: Donggwol Night Tour
overview: A night program through Changgyeonggung and the UNESCO-listed Changdeokgung rear garden — together once called Donggwol, the East Palace: an immersive 60-minute tour guided by a court painter character, then 40 minutes free in the moonlit Secret Garden. Four sessions nightly, 50 people each.

title: Muan YD Festival
overview: A youth festival at Namak Central Park in Muan — 'where my dream comes true' — positioning the provincial-capital town as a youth culture hub with stages, programs, and community events.

title: Korea Sool Grand Festival
overview: Korea's largest traditional-liquor festival at the aT Center: hundreds of brewers from every province pouring makgeolli, yakju, and distilled spirits for tasting and direct purchase, with pairing programs and events. Entry 10,000 won.
sponsor: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

title: Busan Fireworks Festival
overview: Busan Fireworks Festival takes place every autumn along Gwangalli Beach. The festival’s diverse programs of cultural events, high-tech laser light shows, and myriad of unique and colorful fireworks make this one of the area’s most popular festivals, drawing crowds of over 1 million visitors each year. Although most people flock to the beach for a closer view of the festivities, nearby Hwangnyeongsan Mountain, Dongbaekseom Island, and Igidae Coastal Park also offer great views of the fireworks.

title: Sunchang Korea Tteokbokki Festa
overview: K-food's favorite street dish meets Korea's fermentation capital: tteokbokki recipes built on Sunchang's famous gochujang, with tastings, exhibitions, photo zones, and family programs in the home of traditional pastes.

title: Autumn, to Myeongdong
overview: A neighborhood autumn event at the 'Jaemiro' plaza by Myeongdong Station: performances, a toy flea market whose proceeds partly fund toys for children in need, and prize events along Seoul's comic street.
place: Jaemiro Sangsang Plaza, Myeongdong Station exit 3

title: Bangbae Cafe Alley Festa
overview: A revival festival for Bangbae's cafe alley — the original hangout street of 1980s Seoul youth culture — under the slogan 'the alley itself is a cafe': merchant-led programs, performances, and markets reconnecting generations to the district.

title: Starlight Tavern: Soyang
overview: A night festival in the hanok village of Soyang, Wanju: traditional-house taverns serving local food and black-persimmon makgeolli, talks, live music, and the Starlight K-Contest among the wooden courtyards of Oseong Hanok Village.
place: Oseong Hanok Village and Soyang Gotaek

title: Hongseong Baekban Festa
overview: A home-style-table festival at Gwangcheon Culture Market — famous for gim and jeotgal — serving local-ingredient baekban spreads and global gimbap, with seaweed-roasting, cooking classes, and market events under the theme 'a full Gwangcheon table'.

title: E-World Illumination
overview: E-World Illumination is a lighting festival that decorates E-World and 83 Tower with ten million lights. Visitors can also take memorable photos at romantic and attractive photo zones that light up the evening.
fee: Paid; refer to the website for details

title: Hologram Expo: HOLO WAVE
overview: Jeonbuk's hologram-industry expo at Wonkwang University: graphic-art displays, technology and product exhibitions, hands-on hologram experiences, a future-tech forum on AI and XR, and hologram performances. Free.

title: 46th Seoul Dance Festival
overview: Korea's flagship contemporary dance festival at the Arko Arts Theater, this year exploring the 'omnivore' era — connection over fusion, individuality intact — through premieres and competition stages by the national dance association.

title: Korea AI Education Festival
overview: A national AI-education festival at KINTEX running since 2015: exhibitions, hands-on zones, and lectures that make AI learning approachable for students, teachers, and families. Free.
sponsor: Ministry of Science and ICT · Ministry of Education

title: Early Early Christmas
overview: Hwasun's head start on the holidays: a Christmas market and marching-band parade, night market, classic carousel, and family programs filling Namsan Park before December even arrives.

title: The Souvenir Fair
titleFull: The Souvenir Fair (2025 대한민국 관광기념품 박람회)
overview: The Souvenir Fair brings together various companies and local governments to showcase a variety of souvenirs, both traditional and trendy. Visitors can freely explore the exhibition space, enjoy souvenir shopping, and take part in various programs. Highlights of the fair include an exhibition of competition-winning works, a zone featuring outstanding local souvenirs, and a special exhibition of overseas souvenirs.
place: Art Hall 1, 2  of Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Sangsang Platform Sool Sool Festa
overview: A traditional-liquor festival in Incheon's open-port warehouse venue: 32 breweries pouring Korean sool, makgeolli-brewing and cocktail classes, soap-making from brewing lees, busking and DJ parties, plus a camping pop-up and local-food market.

title: Korea Kimjang Grand Festival
overview: A national celebration of kimjang — Korea's UNESCO-listed communal kimchi-making culture — at the aT Center: master-kimchi sales halls, ingredient markets, discounts, performances, and hands-on booths as the winter kimchi season opens.

title: Dan-Dan-Dan Festival
overview: Gangneung's winter tradition festival at the Danoje education hall — 'our one and only finest festival': gugak-crossover headliners, a children's traditional performance day, regional troupes, and the Yeongsanhong concert with pansori and street-dance stars.

title: Christmas Village Busan
overview: A month-long Santa village across the grounds of the Busan Cinema Center: some 150 local and popular brands, world street food and Christmas menus, gift and lifestyle shops, and pop-ups under the world's largest cantilever roof — Korea's biggest Christmas market.

title: Hampyeong Winter Light Festival
overview: Hampyeong keeps its chrysanthemum-festival sculptures lit through winter: large light installations, media-art projections, and evening programs across the Expo Park and town streets. Free, evenings.
place: Hampyeong Expo Park and town center

title: K-Rice Festa: Our Rice, Our Sool
Haeundae Light Festival
overview: The Haeundae Light Festival features light sculptures, media art exhibitions, and various performances, creating healing spaces and urban art spaces in the city center.

title: Game Playground Pop-up
overview: Six Busan game studios open their titles for public play in a pop-up at Gwangalli: story-and-art booths with playable zones, stamp tours with prizes, and special game events — indie Korean gaming made approachable.

title: Kimjang Together at Jeolla Gamyeong
overview: The old provincial seat of Jeonju revives the communal kimjang: visitors make kimchi together — later delivered to neighbors in need — with performances and traditional games recreating the warmth of village kimchi season.

title: Gwanak Starlight Walk
overview: Gwanak Starlight Walk is a signature winter festival of Gwanak-gu in Seoul. It's a lighting festival where visitors can enjoy beautiful light installation along Byeolbitnaerincheon Stream. The event area spans 300-meters from Sillimgyo Bridge to Bongnimgyo Bridge. The diverse lighting artworks created by ten different Korean artist teams come together to create a space where stories of individuals all become one as a community. Various hands-on programs offer visitors a chance to see and enjoy the sights and sounds of the city throughout the festival period.

title: Ulsan Culture Expo
overview: A culture expo tracing Ulsan's 6,000-year creative lineage — from the newly UNESCO-listed Bangucheon petroglyphs, called the origin of Korean art, to today's citizen arts scene — with participatory programs by local artists at UECO.

title: Lighting Festival at The Garden of Morning Calm
titleFull: Lighting Festival at The Garden of Morning Calm (아침고요수목원 오색별빛정원전)
overview: Held at the Garden of Morning Calm, the Lighting Festival was the first light festival in Korea to combine the natural surroundings with lights, covering 330 thousand square meters. Held from December to March, the environmental-friendly LED lights shine throughout the garden.
fee: Adults 11,000 won · Teenagers 8,500 won · Children 7,500 won

title: Ulsan Night, Christmas Market
titleFull: Ulsan Night, Christmas Market (울산의 밤, 크리스마스 마켓)
overview: Ulsan's Night, Christmas Market is an end of the year festival held in the heart of Ulsan, presenting a special evening with beautiful lights and decorations. Around 40 participating local vendors come together to showcase handcrafted products and delicious foods. Moreover, busking performances, Santa's present giveaway, balloon event, and more are prepared to create a family-friendly atmosphere and x_heighten the holiday mood.

title: Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival
overview: Busan's main winter illumination, running along Gwangbok-ro in the old town from a countdown switch-on in early December through to late February. During the festival there is busking by Busan musicians, and public switch-on events where visitors light the trees themselves. Free, and directly connected to the Day 1 route in our Busan guide — Gwangbok-ro runs alongside BIFF Square and Gukje Market, so the illuminations are a natural way to end an afternoon in the old town.

title: Yuseong Hot Springs Christmas Festival
overview: Daejeon's hot-spring district opens the holidays with a tree-lighting and drone light show, 30 market and experience booths, a vin-chaud lounge, bubble and acoustic stages, instant-photo booths, and a carousel in Yurim Park.

title: Buan Snow Mullet Festival
overview: A winter seafood festival in Buan for seol-sungeo — 'snow mullet', at its fattest and sweetest in the cold months — with tastings, market food, fishing-village programs, and local performances.

title: Yangpyeong Ice & Trout Festival
overview: Winter fishing at Sumi Village — a presidential-award-winning farm-stay village east of Seoul: smelt netting, bare-hand trout catching, ice-fishing spots, plus pizza and steamed-bun making, succulent crafts, and ATV rides.

title: Good Neighbors World Play Festival
overview: A children's-rights NGO festival where kids play traditional games from around the world — earning a world-education certificate — with magic, bubble shows, and balloon art at Pohang's sports center.

title: Busan International Children's Book Fair
overview: Korea's first international children's book fair at BEXCO — a picture-book platform gathering publishers, authors, and illustrators from across Asia, and a book festival for kids (elementary age and under enter free).

title: Seoul Lantern Festival
overview: Seoul's signature lantern festival since 2009: glowing sculpture installations along the Cheonggyecheon stream from Cheonggye Plaza, this year themed 'my light, our dream, Seoul's magic'. Free, nightly till 23:00 — one of the city's classic winter walks.

title: Winter Lights of Cheonggyecheon
overview: Cheonggye Plaza's 11th winter light garden: a golden cake tree centerpiece with fairies, teddy bears, mini trains, and media art along the stream — themed 'a winter where everyone comes together in golden warmth'. Free, evenings through New Year's Eve.

title: Gwanghwamun Market
overview: Gwanghwamun Market takes place along with the Seoul Lantern Festival to support local small businesses and promote Seoul night tourism. The market features local store owners and businesses that exhibit and sell seasonal decor, handcrafted items, and winter snacks.

title: Seoul Light Gwanghwamun
overview: Media-art projections on and around Gwanghwamun — the spot where electric light first entered Korea — themed 'Gwanghwa, Breathe with Light': the square's history retold in moving light across the winter evenings.

title: Nonsan Yangchon Dried Persimmon Festival
overview: Sweet gotgam (dried persimmon) meets Christmas warmth in Yangchon, one of Korea's dried-persimmon heartlands: some 20 farms selling the winter delicacy with family programs, performances, and markets.

title: Oncheoncheon Light Festival
overview: Busan Dongnae's stream glows for 45 winter nights: 1.1km of light sculptures across six themed zones ('Love Song of Oncheoncheon'), with an artificial-snow plaza, busking, and media wish-writing near Dongnae Station.

title: Romantic Hangang Christmas Market
overview: Seven days of Christmas market on Ttukseom Hangang Park themed 'winter playground': light-and-tree photo zones, world street food, craft and ornament stalls, daily programs, and special performances on Christmas Eve and Christmas night.

title: Gangnam Media Winter Festa
overview: Media art at Samseong Station's trade-center plaza bridging the holidays: a Korean-reinterpreted K-Christmas show through December 25, then a new-year show welcoming 2026's year of the red horse, with four hands-on programs alongside.

title: Pocheon Baegun Valley Jack Frost Festival
overview: A 65-day winter festival an hour from Seoul: snow and ice sledding, children's rides, ice and indoor fishing, and a giant ice-tree photo zone against Baegun Valley's snowscape — mostly on land, so small kids manage fine. Entry 3,000 won with a 2,000-won food voucher back.

title: Science Gifted Education Festival
overview: An education conference sharing research by Korea's gifted-science students and policy results from all 17 provincial education offices, themed 'science talents light the AX era'. Free, open to anyone interested in gifted education.

title: Ulsan Seongnam-dong Snow Festival
