overview: Ulsan's downtown winter festival: snowman making, a tree forest, artificial snowfall, a Christmas choir contest, and local stages with flea markets and food zones through the young-street district.

title: Daecheon Winter Sea Love Festival
overview: The mud-festival beach in winter mode: light installations over Daecheon's night sea with couple- and family-oriented programs at the Mud Theme Park, themed sea, light, and love.

title: Suseong Light Art Festival
overview: The Suseong Light Art Festival unfolds a feast of light every year with different themes, adorning Suseongmot Lake with colorful illuminations. It also features a variety of events, including an artwork exhibition and a drone art show.

title: Open Port Christmas: Bulmeong
titleFull: 오픈 포트 크리스마스 : 불멍 (Open Port Christmas)
overview: A year-end campfire festival on the old open-port waterfront in Incheon, where visitors and their dogs sit around fires to see out the year. Bulmeong — roughly 'fire-gazing' — is the Korean word for staring into a campfire doing nothing, and the event takes it literally: a campfire zone with winter snacks for those who book ahead, lights and decorations, and a stamp trail whose completion triggers a donation to abandoned-dog shelters. There is an indoor play area and a 1,650 m² off-leash zone for dogs. Free.

title: Oh Slow Vintage Market
titleFull: Oh Slow Vintage Market (오슬로우 빈티지 마켓)
overview: Oh Slow Vintage Market is the largest vintage market in Korea for those who pursue a slow life, with numerous teams participating in the market, including vintage, antique, second-hand, flower, and small items that align with the values of "slow life." The market is characterized by vintage items and furniture that have been around for a long time and have their own unique value, as well as rare antique items that have their own history and timeless beauty. Quality second-hand clothing and miscellaneous goods provide opportunities to purchase brand products or items in good condition at reasonable prices, going beyond just low prices. The flower section includes fresh flowers and pots for adding a personal touch. Additionally, there are stylish design items and beautifully crafted handmade crafts that enrich lifestyles. Visitors can enjoy an exciting atmosphere with DJ performances and can learn about participating vintage businesses and rare vintage products in detail through a vintage docent tour.
sponsor: Korean Vintage Culture Association, Market Kizi

title: Jeongdongjin Sunrise Festival
overview:
Many people come to celebrate a fresh start at the Jeongdongjin Sunrise Festival on the eve of one year and the first day of the New Year at Sandglass Park. The sandglass at the park has a diameter of 8.06 meters, a x_width of 3.2 meters, a weight of 40 tons, and holds 8 tons of sand, making it one of the biggest sandglasses in the world. It takes a whole year for sand to trickle to the bottom and then the sandglass restarts again on New Year’s Day each year at midnight.

Festival events include a fireworks display, the turning of the sandglass to start another year, and performances by various artists.

title: Countdown Busan
overview: Busan's New Year countdown on Gwangalli Beach: concerts, a large-scale drone show over the water, and the midnight countdown against the lit Gwangan Bridge — the city's signature year-crossing party.

title: Winter in Yangpyeong: Light & Love
overview: The highlight night of Yangpyeong's two-month winter stamp-tour festival: fireworks, guest singers, light installations, and market booths on the Namhangang Terrace by the county office on New Year's Eve.

title: Yeosu Hyangiram Sunrise Festival
addr: 60 Hyangiram-ro, Dolsan-eup, Yeosu-si, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Hyangiram Sunrise Festival is an annual overnight festival that begins on New Year's Eve. It takes place at the historic Hyangiram Hermitage, which was built in the year 644. As the New Year's Day dawns, visitors can witness the sun rise above the horizon from Hyangiram, which literally means "a hermitage facing the sun."

title: Homigot Sunrise Festival
overview:
Homigot Village, the main venue of the Homigot Sunrise Festival, is located on the easternmost point of the Korean Peninsula. Homigot Village means "a village on a tiger’s tail," in reference to the Korean peninsula looking like a tiger.

The festival includes local cultural performances, a New Year celebratory event, fireworks show, sunrise concert and other diverse performances. Visitors may sample free tteokguk, a traditional New Year’s Day dish. Other events such as kite-flying and launching hope balloons with wishes attached will provide enjoyable moments to reflect on the previous year and create new year resolutions.

title: Jeonju New Year's Eve Festival
overview: Jeonju closes the year with Joseon-pop and gugak crossover stages, b-boy performances, winter ballads, family programs, a midnight drum ceremony, and fireworks at the plaza by city hall.

title: Ulju Ganjeolgot Sunrise Festival
overview: Ganjeolgot is where the sun first rises on the Korean peninsula each new year, and the point marks it with a year-end concert on December 31 followed by dawn fireworks and a drone show as 2026's first light breaks over the East Sea.

title: Gangneung New Year Sunrise Festival
overview: Korea's most famous sunrise spots — Gyeongpo Beach and the Jeongdongjin Hourglass Park — host year-end and first-sunrise gatherings, with countdown events through midnight and dawn programs on New Year's morning.

title: Sunyang Barebody Marathon
overview: Korea's coldest New Year tradition: a shirtless run through Daejeon's Expo Science Park on January 1, held since 2015 to start the year with health and grit — with events and special prizes to warm things up.

title: DDP Architecture Tour
overview: A guided walk through Dongdaemun Design Plaza, the landmark designed by Zaha Hadid, covering both the building itself and the history of the Dongdaemun area it sits in. Tours run Tuesday through Sunday (closed Mondays and on New Year's Day, Seollal, and Chuseok). The English tour departs at 13:30; Korean tours run at 10:30 and 15:30. Meet at the tour desk on the first floor of the DDP Museum; the walk takes about 60 minutes. Ages 13 and up; children under 13 must be accompanied by a guardian. Book online via the DDP website, or take a remaining spot on site from 10 minutes before departure.
fee: Adults 10,000 won · Veterans, military, visitors with disabilities, youth groups 8,000 won · Children 5,000 won

title: Korea Grand Sale 2026
overview: Korea's national winter shopping-and-culture festival for international visitors: discounts and perks across flights, hotels, beauty, food, and entertainment nationwide, with a welcome center in Myeong-dong offering travel services and events. Registration free at koreagrandsale.co.kr.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Namsan Beacon Ceremony and Traditional Culture Events
overview: In the Joseon era, the beacon mound on Namsan was the final relay point of a nationwide signal-fire network that carried news to the capital. This Seoul city program brings that system back to life: watch the beacon-lighting ceremony with historical commentary at the Namsan beacon site, join the daily noon bell-ringing at Bosingak Pavilion, and catch samulnori percussion and traditional martial-arts demonstrations at the Palgakjeong plaza by N Seoul Tower. Day programs let visitors try the night-watch and beacon-keeper roles themselves.
place: Namsan Beacon Mound and Bosingak Pavilion

title: Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony 2026
overview: Pasu — standing guard over the capital's walls — was one of the key military rituals of the Joseon dynasty, and this reenactment restores it at Sungnyemun, Korea's National Treasure gate. Guards line up before the gate, the timekeeper announces the hour, conch and trumpet signals sound, and the gate-opening ritual begins on the commander's order, followed by six rounds of guard duty and shift changes before the closing ritual. Runs daily except Mondays, 10:00–15:40, free of charge — an easy add-on to any walk between Seoul Station and Myeong-dong.

title: Gugak Performance Jinyeon
overview: The gugak performance “Jinyeon, The Music of the Royal Banquet” offers a unique opportunity to experience the diversity of traditional Korean arts on a single stage. Set in an intimate venue designed in the style of a traditional Korean house, it allows for close interaction between the audience and performers. The program features a wide range of music performed on traditional instruments, spanning Korean music, K-pop, classical pieces, and world folk songs. As an all-in-one performance, it brings together elements of Korean culture, sound, instruments, and live performance into a single immersive experience.
fee: General admission 65,000 won Free admission: Children younger than 24 months old

title: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
titleFull: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show (광안리 M(Marvelous) 드론 라이트쇼)
overview: Every Saturday evening, 1,100 drones light up the night sky over Gwangallihaebyeon Beach in a range of fascinating formations through the Gwangalli M (Marvelous) Drone Light Show. The show takes place twice, with  each show taking around 12 minutes. On special occasions such as during Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving Day) or New Year's countdown, an even more spectacular show takes place featuring up to 3,000 drones.  * Schedule subject to change depending on weather conditions.

title: Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony at Deoksugung Palace
overview: The Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony is Seoul's flagship historical reenactment: the changing of the sumungun, the guards who kept the gates of Joseon-era palaces. Reconstructed from historical records, the ceremony unfolds in front of Daehanmun Gate at Deoksugung Palace, six days a week (closed Mondays) at 11:00 and 14:00. Hands-on programs run alongside it — beat the drum that opens the ceremony, dress as a gate guard yourself, or put on Joseon-era costume for photos. It is free, central, and one of the easiest ways to see living Joseon court ritual in the middle of modern Seoul.
place: In front of Daehanmun Gate, Deoksugung Palace

title: Gamaksan Sunrise Gathering
overview: The 27th New Year sunrise gathering on Gamaksan's summit in Geochang: pungmul drumming, wish-gourd breaking, and free tteokguk (rice-cake soup) as the year's first light comes up over the ridges.

title: Walk of the Royal Family
overview: A palace procession inside an airport: before your flight out of Incheon International, you can watch a reenactment of Joseon court life. In Terminal 1, the king and queen stroll the concourse as if walking the palace grounds; in Terminal 2, a royal procession with military officials recreates a late-Joseon martial exam visit. After each performance, visitors can take photos with the cast in full court dress. A rare chance to see Joseon pageantry without leaving the departures hall.

title: Hongcheon River Ice Festival
overview: Hongcheon's January classic: ice-hole fishing for ginseng-fed trout (a local specialty), bare-hand trout catching, indoor family fishing, ice sledding, folk games, and thatched-village food streets along the frozen river.

title: Pyeongchang Trout Festival
overview: In the past, winters in this region were unforgiving. Heavy snowfalls buried villages, and neighbors would stretch ropes between their homes, carving tunnels through the snow to find their way from one house to another. When the bitter winds sweeping across the river caused the shallow channels to freeze and merge early in the season, people would hammer at large rocks beneath the ice catch fish and secure a precious meal. Today, the hardships endured by our ancestors have been transformed into celebration. Every year from late December through late January, the Pyeongchang Trout Festival brings this winter heritage to life under the theme, “A Winter Story of Snow, Ice, and Trout.” Visitors can experience the thrill of trout fishing on the frozen Odaecheon Stream, where the crystal-clear ice reveals fish swimming beneath the surface. Along with a variety of winter activities, the festival offers an opportunity to enjoy the true charm and excitement of a Korean winter.

title: Yeongyang Frozen Winter Festival
overview: A classic Korean winter festival on the frozen Banbyeoncheon in Yeongyang — one of Korea's most remote, star-dark counties: natural ice rink, ice sledding and trains, snow-sled hills, and smelt ice fishing.

title: Hongseong Namdang Port Cockle Festival
overview: Saejogae — the plump, sweet 'bird clam' — peaks in winter on the Cheonsuman Bay, and Namdang Port's restaurant row runs a whole season around it: shabu-style cockle pots by the harbor from December through the cold months.

title: Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival
titleFull: Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival (철원 한탄강 얼음트레킹 축제)
overview: Set amid the spectacular winter landscape of the Hantangang River, the Cheorwon Hantangang River Ice Trekking Festival is one of Cheorwon’s premier winter celebrations. The festival has been inducted into the Hall of Fame of the Korea Festival Contents Awards and was selected as an Outstanding Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for 2026–2027. Connected to the Hantangang River Mulwit-gil trekking course, the festival allows visitors to enjoy the river’s breathtaking snowy scenery while taking part in a variety of performances and winter-themed activities held throughout the festival period at the main venue beneath Seungilgyo Bridge. Special events, including the popular “Ttongbaram Altong Road Run," add to the festive atmosphere and excitement.

title: Anseong Dongmakgol Smelt Festival
overview: Ice fishing for bingeo (pond smelt) on Gwanghyewon Reservoir — a clean class-1 valley reservoir in Anseong ringed by hills. A straightforward, family-friendly winter fishing day out.

title: Danyang Winter Play Festival
overview: Old-fashioned winter play in snowy Danyang: ice sleds and one-blade sleds, ice tug-of-war, yut games, jwibulnori fire-can spinning, nakhwa fire-flower displays, campfire zones, and winter snacks by the Jungnyeong stream.

title: CookieRun: Kingdom Art Collaboration Project Special Exhibition
titleFull: CookieRun: Kingdom Art Collaboration Project Special Exhibition (쿠키런 : 킹덤 아트 콜라보 프로젝트 특별전 - 위대한 왕국의 유산)
overview: CookieRun: Kingdom Art Collaboration Project Special Exhibition - The Legacy of the Great Kingdom is a large-scale art exhibition that combines traditional Korean craft works with experiential media art. Visitors can experience the moment when the them song of the popular mobile RPG game CookieRun: Kingdom comes to life in collaboration with traditional, along with various exhibition facilities that invite visitors to interact and have fun. The exhibition presents various attractions, including prompts about life, the game's media art, and a variety of artworks.
place: Ara Art Center in Insa-dong, Seoul
fee: Adults 23,000 won / Teenagers 21,000 won / Children 18,000 won* Special admission (65 years old and older) 15,000 won* Special ticket (regardless of age) 45,000 won

title: Haman Dried Persimmon Festival
overview: Haman gotgam — once royal tribute, made from the small but intensely sweet susi persimmon dried in the winter winds of old Aragaya — stars in a market festival whose highlight is a rollicking national singing contest.

title: Muan Winter Mullet Festival
overview: Winter mullet at its best on Muan's mudflat coast: a seafood-market festival at Haeje with local farm-and-sea products, linked to the Hwangto Mudflat Land attractions nearby.

title: Yeongdong Dried Persimmon Festival
overview: Yeongdong's winter market festival for its famous gotgam: sales halls with the county's forest and farm products, roasted chestnuts and sweet potatoes, garaetteok grilling, warm dome lounges, and family winter play by the Yeongdong stream.

title: Daegwallyeong Snow Festival
overview: The Daegwallyeong Snow Festival is held in Daegwallyeong, Pyeongchang every January. Daegwallyeong Snow Festival first began in 1993 and was one of the first snow festivals that took place at the time. Since then it has become a prominent winter festival of the region that brings the community together. The festival's beautiful snowy hills and enjoyable activities are the perfect combination for bringing out the child in everyone.

title: Uljin Snow Crab & Red Snow Crab Festival
overview: Uljin's Hupo Port — one of Korea's snow-crab capitals — throws its winter crab festival at Wangdolcho Plaza: crab markets and meals, auctions, performances, and harbor programs at the source of the famous daege.

title: Yangyang Naksan Beach Moonlight Bonfire Festival
overview: Bonfires on the winter sand of Naksan Beach: wave sounds, crackling logs, and quiet conversation instead of stages and crowds — a contemplative seaside evening capped by the moon over the East Sea. Reserve via the GoGo Yangyang app (10,000 won).

title: Jeongseon Buckwheat Crepe Festival
overview: A food festival at the famous Jeongseon Arirang Market for memil jeonbyeong — the buckwheat crepes of Gangwon's mountain kitchens: griddle demonstrations, master classes, new-menu showcases, and market stalls.

title: Gossaum Nori Festival
overview: A full-moon festival for gossaum — the national-heritage 'go fight', where villages ram giant straw loops in a contest of strength dating to Korea's farming past — with mass rope games and torch processions at the tradition's home village in Gwangju.

title: Jecheon Red Odeng Festival
overview: Jecheon's beloved street snack — fish cakes simmered in a fiery red broth — gets its own festival: 25 pojangmacha tents serving red odeng and variations, an eating contest, magic and bubble shows, and concerts by the station plaza.

title: 1919 Seodaemun: The Cry of That Day
overview: March First Independence Movement commemorations at the very sites of 1919: a memorial ceremony, mansei march reenactment, and programs at Seodaemun Independence Park and the former Seodaemun Prison where independence activists were held.
place: Seodaemun Independence Park and Prison History Hall

title: 2026 Visit Korean Islands Year
overview: 2026 is Korea's official Year of Island Tourism, a national campaign spotlighting the ecology and culture of the country's thousands of islands. It ties into the 2026 Yeosu World Island Exhibition — the first world expo dedicated to islands — and spreads the momentum nationwide with island travel subsidies, culture weeks, and events running throughout the year. If island-hopping in the South Sea archipelago is on your list, 2026 is the year the infrastructure, discounts, and programming all line up.
sponsor: Ministry of the Interior and Safety

title: Wanju Samnye Strawberry Festival
overview: Strawberry season in Samnye, Wanju's berry heartland: picking experiences, strawberry desserts and processed goods, local food booths, and family programs — sweet, cheap, and twenty minutes from Jeonju.

title: Buyeo-gun Chungnam Gugak Group’s Saturday Show
titleFull: Buyeo-gun Chungnam Gugak Group’s Saturday Show(부여군충남국악단 토요상설공연)
place: Buyeo-gun Gugak Center, 388, Baekjemun-ro, Gyuam-myeon, Buyeo-gun, Chungcheongnam-do

title: Jindo National Gugak Center’s Saturday Show ‘I Love Gugak’
titleFull: Jindo National Gugak Center’s Saturday Show ‘I Love Gugak’(국립남도국악원 토요 상설 공연 ‘국악이 좋다’)
place: Jindo National Gugak Center Jinakdang, 3818, Jindo-daero, Imhoe-myeon, Jindo-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City

title: Jeju Fire Festival
overview: Jeju's most spectacular tradition: the slopes of Saebyeol Oreum set alight in a controlled burn that recalls the island's old pasture-burning custom. Preliminary days bring wish-writing and giant moon-house building; the main weekend delivers theme performances and the night the hill burns. One of Korea's great fire spectacles.

title: APAP Artwork Tour
overview: The Anyang Public Art Project (APAP) started in 2005 and has led to the creation of many beautiful works of art that decorate the city's public spaces. The Anyang Foundation for Culture & Arts has created a tour program to explore the wonderful works, starting from the earliest works in 2005 up until now.
place: Anyang Pavilion (Anyang Art Park), Pyeongchon Area (Jungang Park), etc.
fee: Adults 3,000 won / Children (ages 19 and younger) 1,000 won * Separate fees apply to special tours

title: 2026 Culture Day: Cheongchun Mic (Jeolla & Jeju)
overview: Cheongchun Mic is a national busking program that puts young and senior performing teams on outdoor stages across the Jeolla and Jeju regions, part of Korea's monthly Culture Day initiative. The 2026 edition pairs emerging local acts with everyday public spaces — parks, plazas, street corners — so residents and travelers run into live performance as part of daily life. Around 47 performances are scheduled; times vary by show.
place: Gwangju Jungoe Park and venues across Jeolla and Jeju
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Gwangyang Maehwa Festival
addr: 55 Jimak 1-gil, Gwangyang-si, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Gwangyang Maehwa Festival takes place next to the Seomjingang River in Gwangyang Maehwa Village, home of the largest number of plum blossom trees in Korea. During the festival period, visitors can enjoy a walk beneath the plum blossoms, and also sample and purchase local organic plum products.
fee: Adults 6,000 wonTeenagers 5,000 won * Tickets are compensated in full as a cash voucher for purchasing products at local businesses

title: Daejeon Yeonjeong Korean Traditional Music Group’s Saturday Gugak Show
titleFull: Daejeon Yeonjeong Korean Traditional Music Group’s Saturday Gugak Show(대전시립연정국악단 토요국악)
place: Daejeon Yeonjeong Korean Traditional Music Center Jakeunmadang (Little Hall), 181, Dunsan-daero, Seo-gu, Daejeon

title: Gurye Sansuyu Festival
addr: 45 Sanggwan 1-gil, Gurye-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Gurye Sansuyu Festival is an annual spring flower festival. Major programs include exhibition of local products made from sansuyu (cornus fruit), while other programs include traditional music and dance performances, experience programs, and fireworks.

title: K-Gugak Stage
place: National Gugak Center Yewondang, 54, Yangnim-gil, Namwon-si, Jeonbuk-do

title: Ssokssokdeul-i Festival
overview:
Ssokssokdeul-i Festival is a program organized by the National Theater of Korea’s Stage Arts Support Center, designed to make performing arts more accessible in everyday life. Held regularly throughout the year, it offers a variety of performances free of charge, creating greater opportunities for the public to engage with the arts in a relaxed and approachable setting.

The festival takes place at the “Ssok” Experience Theater within the Stage Arts Support Center and features dynamic stages that can be enjoyed by audiences of all ages. Tickets for the performances are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis at the on-site information desk starting at 12:00 on the day of the performance. These tickets may close early depending on the number of seats available. With artists presenting distinctive styles across a range of popular genres, it creates a vibrant cultural space where different generations can come together and share the experience.
place: National Theater of Korea Stage Arts Support Center

title: Clipper Race Port Week Tongyeong
titleFull: 클리퍼 레이스 기항지 행사 포트위크(PORT WEEK)
overview: The Clipper Round the World Yacht Race makes its first-ever Korean stopover in Tongyeong: a week of departure ceremonies, marine parades, yacht tours, and RC sailing, plus the Port Table food sessions with chef Kang Leo cooking Tongyeong seafood, fringe stages, and a jazz orchestra night.
sponsor: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries · Tongyeong City

title: Yeoju Ceramic Festival
overview: Yeoju Ceramic Festival is held every year to promote and develop the Yeoju ceramic industry and raise the level of awareness for Yeoju ceramics.

title: Comma: Empty, Stay, Fill (Choi Young-wook)
overview: A retrospective of painter Choi Young-wook's 'Karma' series at the OAR Museum in Gyeongju — moon-jar canvases whose hairline craquelure traces meetings, partings, and reconnections across a life. Four sections follow 30 years of the artist's practice.

title: Sansuyu Village Flower Festival (Uiseong)
overview: Thirty thousand cornelian-cherry trees — many over 300 years old — turn Hwajeon-ri gold each March in Korea's largest sansuyu grove. The 20-ri flower road pairs yellow blossoms against green garlic fields, a painterly early-spring walk in quiet Uiseong.

title: Seocheon Camellia & Webfoot Octopus Festival
overview: Two spring arrivals at once: camellias blooming at Dongbaekjeong and jjukkumi (webfoot octopus) hitting peak season at Maryangjin Port. Children's octopus fishing and boat-fishing experiences anchor the food-and-flowers weekend.

title: Nonsan Strawberry Festival
overview: Held every year in Nonsan, Chungcheongnam-do, the Nonsan Strawberry Festival is one of Korea’s premier festivals celebrating a regional specialty. As the nation’s leading strawberry-producing area, Nonsan has built a stable production base and efficient distribution network. Building on these strengths, the festival has evolved into an industry-oriented event that integrates agriculture, food processing, and tourism. The festival features strawberry sales and tastings, hands-on experience programs, performances, exhibitions, and industry networking events. It is distinguished by the active participation of local farmers and small business owners, who play a central role in its operation. Designated as a Cultural Tourism Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism for 2026–2027, the festival is also expanding its international reach and strengthening industry partnerships in preparation for the 2027 International Strawberry Industry Expo.

title: Sasang Garo Park Cherry Blossom Night Market
overview: Cherry blossoms over open-air drinking tables: Busan Sasang's alley merchants set up a blossom-canopied night market with signature menus, cold beer, indie bands, tap dance, and payback coupon events for three spring evenings.

title: Jinhae Gunhangje Festival
overview: The Jinhae Gunhangje Festival is one of Korea's most iconic spring festivals. It began in 1952 as a memorial ceremony honoring Admiral Yi Sun-sin and developed into a full-fledged festival in 1963. Today, the festival attracts more than two million visitors from Korea and around the world each year. During the festival season, approximately 360,000 King cherry trees burst into bloom across Jinhae, creating one of Korea's most spectacular spring landscapes. Centered around Jungwon Rotary and Bugwon Rotary, the festival features a variety of events including the eve celebration, memorial rite, and the Victory Parade. A particular highlight is the Military Band and Honor Guard Festival, a signature Gunhangje event held on Friday evenings and throughout the weekends during the festival period. Visitors also have the rare opportunity to enter the Korea Naval Academy and the Naval Base Command in Jinhae, both of which are normally closed to the public. In addition, they can visit famous cherry blossom destinations such as Yeojwacheon Stream and Gyeonghwa Station, while exploring the century-old modern cultural heritage sites surrounding Jungwon Rotary. Together, these attractions offer a unique journey through the history, culture, and tranquil scenery of Korea’s historic naval city. Combining the beauty of cherry blossoms, the traditions of the Korean Navy, and the charm of modern history, Jinhae Gunhangje Festival offers an unforgettable celebration of spring.

title: DMZ World Literature Festa
overview: Writers from around the world gather inside the DMZ at Camp Greaves — the former US base turned peace space — to talk literature against war, conflict, and hatred: three days of dialogue on democracy and peace at the world's last divided frontier, with sessions in Paju Book City.
place: Camp Greaves (DMZ) and Paju Book City
sponsor: Gyeonggi Province · Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation · Writers Association of Korea

title: Goryeong Daegaya Festival
overview: The Goryeong Daegaya Festival is the Goryeong's flagship festival and a long-standing celebration where visitors can explore and experience the unique history and culture of Daegaya. In 2025, Goryeong was officially designated as the ancient capital of Daegaya, further enhancing the significance of its rich historical and cultural heritage. In addition, the discovery of pottery bearing the inscription “Great King” at the moat of the Daegaya Palace Site provided important evidence that Daegaya was a powerful ancient kingdom. Together with the inscription of the Jisandong Ancient Tombs on the UNESCO World Heritage List, these developments underscore the importance of preserving and promoting Daegaya’s history and culture for future generations. Under the theme “Daegaya Begins Again: RE-BORN,” the 2026 Goryeong Daegaya Festival seeks to foster pride in Goryeong’s status as the ancient capital of Daegaya while continuing to grow as a leading festival celebrating history and cultural heritage.

title: Yeonsu Spring Harmony Festival
overview: The first spring festival at Incheon's new Yeonsu Hanmaeum Park: open lawn, arts programs, and neighborhood stages under the theme 'facing spring' — a fresh community green breaking in its first season.

title: Gunsan Eunpa Cherry Blossom Night Market
overview: Cherry blossom season around Eunpa Lake — Gunsan's beloved lakeside walk — revived as a night market after the old blossom festival ended: food stalls, participatory programs, and night-tour content under the petals.

title: Gyeonggi Imagine Spring Festa
titleFull: 경기도 문화사계 "봄" 경기 상상해 봄 페스타
overview: A spring culture festa at the Sangsang Campus in Suwon: talk concerts with star history lecturer Choi Tae-seong and science communicator Gwedo, busking and magic stages, spring photo zones, upcycling and flower-seed crafts — plus an MBC music-show live recording on opening day.

title: Gurye 300-ri Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: A 129-kilometer ribbon of cherry blossoms follows the Seomjin River and the skirts of Jirisan through Gurye, linking Hwaeomsa Temple, Sasung-am, and the county's spring villages. The festival adds stages, family games — including a spacing-out contest — and food to the region's most scenic blossom drive.

title: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road
titleFull: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road (인천개항장 페스타 - 1901 라이브로드)
overview: Incheon Gaehangjang Festa - 1901 Live Road is an urban music festival planned based on the historical significance and identity of Incheon Jemulpo, the original name of Incheon Open Port, and the birthplace of Western music exchange during the port's opening period. The show takes place throughout the cultural district of the open port, including the Sangsang Platform and Jemulpo Club. The performances feature a variety of genres, including jazz, folk, band, and EDM. By combining live performances, public participation, and the distinctive atmosphere of the historic port district, the festival offers a unique cultural experience that highlights Incheon’s urban heritage.

title: Seogwipo Canola Flower International Walking Festival
overview: The 28th spring walking festival through Seogwipo's canola-yellow fields: 5km, 10km, and 20km courses from the World Cup Stadium, free entry with finisher certificates, QR check-ins, and GPS course guidance — a walker's way into Jeju spring.

title: Yangjaecheon Cherry Blossom Lantern Festival
overview: Blossoms by day, lanterns by night along the Yangjaecheon stream: the 8th edition pairs the cherry-tree walk between Yeongdong bridges with lighting ceremonies, performances, guided tours, and food zones.

title: Korea Young Farmers National Convention
overview: The 20th national gathering of Korea's young farmer association at Saebyeol Oreum on Jeju — networking, policy exchange, and public programs on the future of Korean agriculture.

title: Cheongsando Slow Walking Festival
overview: Cheongsando — Asia's first designated Slow City — opens spring with a walking festival along its 42.195km slow road: stone-walled lanes, canola fields, and terraced paddies over a blue sea, with moonlight night walks and healing programs. Ferry from Wando; worth an overnight.

title: 2026 Culture Day: Cheongchun Mic (Seoul, Gyeonggi & Gangwon)
overview: The capital-region and Gangwon leg of Cheongchun Mic, Korea's Culture Day street-performance program. Young and senior performing teams selected by open call take their acts to streets and plazas across Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon from April through November. Expect anything from acoustic sets to dance crews — free, outdoors, and deliberately placed where people already are.
place: Across the capital region and Gangwon
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Andong Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Andong's spring festival timed to the bloom along the Nakdong riverside and downtown cherry roads: blossom tunnels, night lighting, street performances, flea markets, and food zones at the Mask Dance Park.

title: Marine Leisure Tourism Expo 2026
overview: A 300-booth national expo on marine leisure at Songdo Convensia: equipment, tourism content, and coastal-region showcases with trials and seminars, run by the oceans ministry.

title: Okcheon Sapling Festival
overview: Korea's only nursery-tree district — 90 years of sapling growing in Okcheon — gives away 20,000 saplings and runs auctions, exhibitions, and consultations for gardeners: landscaping trees, houseplants, and kitchen-garden stock straight from the growers.

title: Seoul International Buddhism Expo
overview: Korea's flagship Buddhist culture fair at COEX since 2013, paired with the Buddha Art Fair: temple food, meditation goods, craft, and contemporary Buddhist art — this year playfully themed on the concept of emptiness (gong). Free with pre-registration.

title: 2026 International Seon Meditation Conference
overview: Hosted by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, this conference-and-festival pairing explores Seon (Zen) meditation as a tool for mental health, now in its third year. The 2026 theme is 'Seon Meditation in the Age of AI'. Alongside the conference sessions, a public meditation festival at Bongeunsa Temple lets visitors try various forms of Seon practice first-hand — in one of the few major temples standing directly across from Gangnam's COEX skyline.
place: Bongeunsa Temple and Bongeun Culture Center

title: Gimje Flower Light Festival
overview: A downtown spring festival in Gimje pairing flower displays by day with a light garden by night — this year styled as a springtime amusement park ('Flower Light Land') with performances, flea markets, and photo zones.

title: Gangseo Nakdonggang 30-ri Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Busan Gangseo's riverside blossom festival at Daejeo Eco Park: blossom walks, pungmul parades, K-pop dance and busking stages, family and kids zones, food trucks, and flea markets along the Nakdong River petals.

title: Yangjae Art Salon
overview: A rolling weekend culture series on the Yangjaecheon stream: sunset busking stages, craft markets and art workshops along the path, a lawn healing lounge with book corner, and food trucks under Yeongdong Bridge — new themes weekly through the season.

title: Gyeongju Daereungwon Stone Wall Road Festival
overview: Gyeongju's signature spring scene: cherry blossoms over the stone walls and royal mounds of Daereungwon, with the road fully pedestrianized for the festival. Street arts, nightly blossom lighting, a QR-ordered zero-waste restaurant street, and road playgrounds for kids.

title: Nodeul Spring Preview Festival
titleFull: Nodeul Spring Preview Festival (노들 미리봄 페스티벌)
overview: Nodeul Spring Preview Festival, hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, is an event that combines expert talk shows and beautiful music performances. Various programs are prepared, including invited lectures, media exhibitions, talk shows, and artist performances. In addition, the festival explores how Nodeul Island can expand its purpose and cultural experiences under its new role as "Nodeul Global Art Island."

title: Manseokgeo New Light Festival
overview: A night festival at Manseokgeo — the Joseon-era reservoir listed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure — opening Suwon's 2026 visit-year: a combined drone-fireworks-musical fountain show (500 drones, two fireworks rounds) with six busking stages.

title: Yeonje Ancient Tombs Fantasy Festival
overview: A spring festival around the Yeonsan-dong ancient tomb mounds and Oncheoncheon park in Busan: a royal procession, falling-fire (nakhwa) show, blossom song contest — plus morning coffee raves and random-play dance aimed squarely at younger crowds.

title: Boeun Cherry Blossom Road Festival
overview: Spring on the Bocheongcheon blossom road in Boeun: busking, bubble-and-magic shows, picnic zones under the trees, and community blossom walks along the stream.

title: Icheon Baeksa Sansuyu Flower Festival
titleFull: Icheon Baeksa Sansuyu Flower Festival (이천백사 산수유꽃축제)
overview: Icheon’s Baeksa Village is home to a number of sansuyu (cornus fruit) trees, which have been growing naturally in the area for over 100 years. In early spring, the trees change colors to a striking bright yellow, whilst in autumn the village is filled with the trees’ vivid red fruits. During the festival, visitors can participate in Korean traditional folk games and watch the Sansuyu flower parade. When sansuyu trees blossom, many professional photographers travel to Baeksa Village to take pictures of this beautiful sight.

title: Jangja Lake Cherry Blossom Stroll
overview: Ten days of blossom strolling around Guri's Jangja Lake: free-flow flower walks on weekdays and a programmed weekend of performances, street art, booths, and visitor events by the water.

title: Guryong Village Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Blossoms and night lights along the Dongsam seawater stream on Yeongdo, Busan — 'Guryong nights, light and blossom fantasy': lighting ceremony, experience booths, flea markets, busking, and food zones by Amir Park.

title: Seodaemun Spring Light Festival
overview: Three thousand cherry trees on Ansan mountain plus the Hongje waterfall — Seoul's urban cascade — host spring concerts, madang plays, a singing contest, family musicals, daily busking, and month-long blossom lighting along the Hongjecheon.

title: Move Salon: Salon Ground
overview: An open-air community salon on the Yangjaecheon walking path: taste-based meetups anyone can join — or host — under the bridge by Kant's Walk, a city hideout for unwinding with neighbors.

title: Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival
titleFull: Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival (영등포 여의도 봄꽃축제)
tel: • 1330 Travel Hotline: +82-2-1330 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)  • For more info: +82-2-2670-3114
overview: Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival is held on Yeouiseo Road (Yunjung-ro) in April when the azaleas, forsythia, royal azaleas, and other spring flowers are in full bloom. The celebration is famous for its 1,886 Korean cherry trees.

title: Seokchon Lake Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: A thousand king cherry trees ring Seokchon Lake beneath Lotte World Tower — Seoul's most famous blossom tunnel. The festival adds busking, markets, food trucks, and a full-bloom concert, with night lighting turning the white canopy luminous after dark. Expect crowds; go early or late.

title: Uijeongbu Howon Cherry Blossom Festa
overview: Uijeongbu's neighborhood blossom festival on the Jungnangcheon: performances and exhibitions under the trees, food booths, flea and sharing markets, and picnic space along the stream.

title: Saenggeo Jincheon Nongdari Festival
overview: A spring festival at Nongdari — the thousand-year-old stepping-stone bridge of stacked stones across the Semi River, Korea's oldest surviving stone bridge: performances, exhibitions, and food against Chopyeong Lake scenery.

title: Yeongam Wangin Culture Festival
addr: 440, Wangin-ro, Gunseo-myeon, Yeongam-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: First held in 1997, the Yeongam Wangin Culture Festival is one of Korea’s leading Cultural Tourism Festivals and has been held every spring at the Historical Site of Wangin. Dr. Wangin played a pivotal role in cultural exchange across ancient East Asia. Through him, Baekje’s advanced culture and Confucian classics crossed the Korea Strait and reached the Japanese archipelago. His teachings represented far more than a transfer of knowledge; they became a driving force behind the emergence of Asuka culture, the golden age of ancient Japanese civilization. Wangin’s profound scholarship, together with the flowing Yeongsangang River and Sangdaepo Port, symbolizes the currents of exchange that carried culture across the sea. Here in Yeongam, visitors can rediscover the roots of Asuka culture.

title: Raftman
place: Jeongseon Arirang Culture, Arirang Hall, 51, Aesan-ro, Jeongseon-eup, Jeongseon-gun, Gangwon-do

title: Yudalsan Spring Festival
overview: Mokpo's mountain festival under the spring blossoms of Yudalsan — 'a picnic on a blooming day': slow walks on the ring road, treasure hunts, rock-stacking at Nojeokbong, and rentable picnic sets with harbor views.

title: ARI-The Spirit of Korea
place: Jeongseon Arirang Center, 51, Aesan-ro, Jeongseon-eup, Jeongseon-gun, Gangwon-do

title: Blooming Namhae Spring Festival
overview: Cherry blossoms over the strait where Admiral Yi fell: Namhae's spring festival at Chungnyeolsa Shrine and the Noryang battle site pairs history with drone light shows, fireworks, stamp tours, and flea markets.

title: Golche Oreum Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: A hidden Jeju blossom spot: villagers of Seonheul 2-ri have planted king cherries on Golche Oreum for 20 years, and each April the little volcanic cone turns pink. A gentle two-day village festival with music, home-style food stalls, and easy slopes for all ages.

title: Gangseo Spring Light Festa
overview: An evening spring festival at Banghwa Park in western Seoul — 'spring light, moonlight, play all night': camping-style rest zones, retro experience booths, and light displays for all ages.

title: Goheung Nokdong Port Drone Show 2026
overview: A recurring night-sky drone show over Nokdong Port in Goheung, one of the darker, clearer coastal skies in Jeollanam-do. Regular shows run Saturdays at 21:00 at the Nokdong Port sea garden, with a larger 900-drone show in front of the county office plaza on the last Friday of each month (April–October), preceded by an open-air busking stage at 20:00. Holiday specials are added around New Year sunrise and Seollal. Shows may move or cancel in bad weather.
hours: Sat 21:00 (Nokdong Port) · Last Fri of the month 21:00 (county plaza)

title: Infinity Flying
place: Cultural Center Munmu Hall  at Gyeongju Expo Grand Park , 614 Gyeonggam-ro, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do

title: Chungjang Raon Festa 2026
overview: A monthly street festival in Gwangju's Chungjang-ro shopping district, running the first Saturday of each month from April. Launched in 2022 to revive the downtown commercial area, it layers culture and hands-on programs over the streets and underground arcade — music, markets, and family-friendly events. Times vary by program; the district itself is Gwangju's classic downtown, dense with shops and street food.
hours: Varies by program · First Saturday of the month
sponsor: Dong-gu, Gwangju · Chungjang District Revitalization Team

title: Gangneung Gyeongpo Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Blossoms wrap Gyeongpo Lake all the way to the beach — a drive-and-walk classic since 1993 drawing 250,000 visitors a year. The wetland plaza hosts blossom song contests, picnics, play zones, and a 'catch the blossom thief' event, with evening lights across the lakeshore. Dates track the bloom.

title: Gombaengi Teotta
place: Anseong Namsadang Performance Site, 198-2, Namsadang-ro, Bogae-myeon, Anseong-si, Gyeonggi-do

title: Mulgeum Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Blossoms along the old Mulgeum rail line and Hwangsan Park — the Nakdong River's biggest waterside park: the blossom road goes car-free for walkers, with exhibitions, experience booths, rest zones, and night landscape lighting.

title: Trot Festival X Spring Flower Festival
overview: Dongdaemun-gu pairs its blossom festival with Korea's beloved trot music: local singer competitions, booths, and resident-run food stalls at the Jangan waterside park, with photo zones and night lighting along the Jangan blossom road.

title: Geumnam-ro Car-Free Street 'Geotjaing' 2026
overview: On the first Saturday of each month from April to November, Gwangju closes Geumnam-ro — the city's most symbolic downtown boulevard — to cars. The name Geotjaing blends the local dialect for 'let's walk' with '-ing'. The street fills with walkers, pop-up culture programs, and performances, part of the city's push toward transit, cycling, and walking. A good date to aim for if you want to see downtown Gwangju at its liveliest.
hours: 13:00–19:00 · First Saturday of the month, Apr–Nov

title: Danjong Culture Festival
overview: The Danjong Culture Festival, a major festival of Yeongwol-gun in Gangwon State, is a historic cultural event held annually since 1967 in memory of King Danjong, the 6th monarch of the Joseon dynasty. The festival includes a range of activities and programs open to all visitors.

title: Yangyang Namdaecheon Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: A quiet-leaning blossom festival on the Namdaecheon in Yangyang: petal walks, lawn concerts, and a full-moon photo zone timed to the lunar 17th — lantern-lit blossom paths completing the spring evening.

title: Jeju Canola Flower Festival
overview: The Jeju Canola Flower Festival is one of the most famous festivals in Jeju, bringing news of spring arrival with fields upon fields of bright yellow flowers. Large numbers of visitors come to the festival every year to take in this beauty. In addition to enjoying the vibrant landscape, visitors can participate in a variety of festival events that showcase the unique spirit of Jeju Island.
place: Pony Experience Park in Gasi-ri, Seogwipo

title: Jecheon Cheongpung Lake Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: The 30th blossom festival on Cheongpung Lake — Jecheon's inland sea: busking and local performances by day, a blossom laser show and open-air cinema by night, with lawn plazas for slow lake-and-petal viewing.

title: Gyeongbokgung Saenggwabang Royal Dessert House
overview: The royal dessert kitchen of Gyeongbokgung reopens as a tearoom: court sweets and medicinal teas recreated from the Annals, served in the palace's kitchen quarter. The 2026 edition presents storytelling tea tables built on two kings — Yeongjo's austere longevity table and Sukjong's celebratory banquet spread. Ticketed sessions; reserve ahead.

title: Changnyeong Nakdonggang Canola Festival
overview: Korea's largest single canola field — 110 hectares of yellow along the Nakdong River at Namji — blooms into Changnyeong's signature spring festival, running since 2006 with performances, orienteering through the flowers, and riverside picnicking.

title: Gijisi Juldarigi Folk Festival
tel: • 1330 Travel Hotline: +82-2-1330(Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese) • For more info: +82-41-358-4646
overview: Gijisi Juldarigi Folk Festival aims to promote the 500-year traditional folk custom of juldarigi. Juldarigi, a tug-of-war game, was started to pray for peace and fortune in the new year and to be in concord with neighbors as part of a village’s feast.
fee: Free (Separate charge may apply to activities)
sponsor: Gijisi Juldarigi Preservation Committe, Gijisi Juldarigi Festival Organizing Committee

title: Busan Urban Agriculture Expo
overview: A city-farming expo in the canola fields of Daejeo Eco Park: urban growing, healing and companion agriculture, landscape farming exhibitions, and hands-on programs over four spring days.

title: Treasure Island Canola Festival (Gwanmaedo)
overview: Canola gold on Gwanmaedo — a remote island of the Jindo archipelago reachable only by ferry: 75,000 pyeong of blossom fields with mini-train rides, folk games, island trail walks with forest interpreters, and local stalls by the wharf.

title: Yeoju Heungcheon Namhangang River Cherry Blossom Festival
titleFull: Yeoju Heungcheon Namhangang River Cherry Blossom Festival (여주흥천남한강 벚꽃축제)
overview: Yeoju Heungcheon Namhangang River Cherry Blossom Festival is a representative spring festival in Yeoju, taking place among the blooming cherry blossom trees on the banks of the Namhangang River. During the festival period, sections of the road are closed to vehicular traffic, and a range of events, performances, and photo zones are set up to enjoy.
place: Area of Gwibaek-ri in Heungcheon-myeon, Yeoju-si
sponsor: Yeoju Heungcheon Namhangang River Cherry Blossom Festival Organizing Committee

title: Seoul Spring Festival
overview: Seoul's K-lifestyle mega-festival — beauty, fashion, pop, food, art — staged across the Han River itself in 2026: programs on the water and along the banks turn walking the river into the festival experience.

title: Library Day & Library Week
overview: Korea's national library celebration around April 12: an international conference and hackathon at the National Library, a commemorative ceremony, and campaigns at libraries nationwide in the 62nd library week.
place: National Library of Korea and libraries nationwide
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Sancheong Farm Products Festival
overview: The medicinal-herb county under Jirisan brings its best to Donguibogam Village: honey, strawberries, herbs, wild greens, and black pork direct from growers, with programs and performances in the herbal-medicine theme park.

title: Jinju Strawberry Festival
overview: Jinju leads Korea's strawberry exports, and its spring festival celebrates the premium Geumsil variety: picking and tastings, sales at farm prices, performances, and family events in the growing heartland of Sugok-myeon.

title: April 19 Revolution National Culture Festival
overview: A national commemoration of the 1960 April Revolution — the student-led uprising that toppled a rigged election — at the National April 19 Democratic Cemetery: memorials, performances, and citizen programs carrying the movement's values of freedom, democracy, and justice.
place: National April 19 Cemetery and Gangbuk district

title: Gimpo Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Two days of blossoms along the Gyeyangcheon stream — 'purely blossoms': citizen-arts-school ukulele and magic stages, busking, photo zones, and rest spots on Gimpo's favorite petal walk.

title: Donghaeng Festival
overview: Korea's biggest small-business shopping festival: nationwide discounts and events across traditional markets, local shops, and online platforms, opening with ceremonies in Jeonju — a country-wide campaign rather than a single-venue event.
place: Opening in Jeonju · nationwide markets and platforms

title: Jayu Park Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Incheon's classic blossom spot — Jayu (Freedom) Park above the open port — hosts a spring festival with local and headline stages (past lineups include Jang Yoon-jeong and K.Will), world-DJ sets, pressed-flower crafts, the 1888 art market, and food zones.

title: Yeongnangho Cherry Blossom Festival
overview: Sokcho's lakeside blossom festival: an 8km blossom-tunnel loop around Yeongnang Lake with walking events, lakeside yoga, busking, 40 food and market stalls, and a lit blossom tunnel after dark — with Seoraksan's peaks in the background.

title: International Ki Sports Festival Daegu
titleFull: International Ki Sports Festival Daegu (2026 인터내셔널 키스포츠페스티벌 대구)
overview: The International Ki Sports Festival is the only multi-sport event in Korea, with participation from both elite athletes as well as the general public who have an interest in sports. The festival is divided into four categories of competion, expo, conference, and additional events.

title: Korea Science Festival with Busan Science Festival
overview: The 25th Busan Science Festival joins forces with the national science festival at BEXCO, themed 'the taste of science — AI cooks too': taste-labeled experiment zones, robot and research booths from local universities and institutes, lectures, and shows for families.
sponsor: Ministry of Science and ICT · Busan

title: Traditional Culture Programme at the Uijeongbu Site
overview: The Uijeongbu was the highest council of the Joseon government, and its excavated site now forms a public historical plaza on Sejong-daero, a few minutes from Gwanghwamun. The programme staged here recreates yeolmu — the military review drills of the Samgunbu troops once garrisoned along this street of six ministries — alongside a chance to try seunggyeongdo, a Joseon board game about climbing the official ranks, and hands-on traditional martial arts. Free, and easy to fold into a day at the palaces, since it runs late morning to mid-afternoon.

title: Eden Cherry Blossom Road Festival
titleFull: Eden Cherry Blossom Road Festival (에덴벚꽃길 벚꽃축제)
overview: The Eden Cherry Blossom Road Festival satisfies the five senses of youngsters by enjoying not only the cherry blossom tunnel, but also stage performances of classical and popular songs, a handmade flea market, local specialties in Gapyeong, and colorful food.
place: Area of Edenbeotkkot-gil, Cheongpyeong-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do

title: Seogwipo Old Downtown Culture Festival 2026
overview: Evening performances on Ijungseop-ro, the artist street in Seogwipo's old downtown on Jeju Island. Under festival lighting, the street hosts music, dance, and performance acts every Friday through Sunday at 19:00, from April 11 to October 30. It pairs naturally with the Lee Jung-seop gallery and the street market nearby — come for dinner, stay for the show. Performances may be cancelled in bad weather, so check ahead.

title: Geumsan Bogok Valley Wild Cherry Festival
overview: Korea's largest wild-cherry (san-beotkkot) colony — roughly 10 million square meters of hillsides in Bogok Valley — blushes pink each April. Footpaths from 'Boineyo-gil' to 'Jajinbaengi-gil' wind through untouched spring woodland dotted with dogwood, azalea, and wildflowers.

title: Gyochon Cultural Performance Silla Ogi
titleFull: Gyochon Cultural Performance Silla Ogi(교촌문화공연 신라오기)
place: Gyeongju Gyochon Traditional Village Square, 71 Gyo-dong, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do

title: Moonlight Tour at Changdeokgung Palace
titleFull: Moonlight Tour at Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁 달빛기행)
overview: The Moonlight Tour at Changdeokgung Palace is a high-quality cultural event held at Changdeokgung Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage. The tour offers a unique opportunity to witness and experience palatial beauty under the moonlight.
sponsor: Cultural Heritage Administration Royal Palaces and Tombs Center

title: Seoul Buramsan Azalea Festival
overview: A hundred thousand royal azaleas paint Buramsan's healing town pink for one short window each spring: flower-path walks, sensory performances, and family programs at the mountain's foot in northeast Seoul.

title: Jindo Miracle Sea Road Festival
overview: Twice a year the tide drops far enough to expose a 2.8 km strip of seabed between Hoedong-ri and the island of Modo, and for about an hour people walk across the sea on a path 30–40 m wide. It is designated Scenic Site No. 9. The phenomenon became internationally known in 1975, when the French ambassador to Korea — visiting to see the Jindo dog — witnessed it and described it in the French press as a modern parting of the Red Sea; a 1996 Japanese hit song about it still brings Japanese visitors every year. The festival programmes Jindo's intangible heritage alongside the crossing: Jindo Arirang, ganggangsullae circle dance, ssitgimgut shamanic rites, and Jindo drum dance. Free. The crossing window is tide-dependent and lasts about an hour — check the exact time before travelling.

title: Hwasun Spring Flower Festival
overview: Flower roads by day, 'blossom night walk' by night: Hwasun's spring festival strings canola fields, pop-up pochas, dinosaur installations, and performances along the flower river path and Namsan Park.
place: Hwasun flower river road and Namsan Park

title: Daejeon Science Festival
overview: Held in conjunction with the 2026 Korea Science Festival, the Daejeon Science Festival is Korea’s largest science event, co-hosted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and Daejeon Metropolitan City. The festival invites visitors to experience how advances in science and technology are transforming everyday life while encouraging them to explore and prepare for the future together. Government agencies, public institutions, private companies, and organizations participate in the event, presenting a wide range of programs, including exhibitions, hands-on experiences, performances, lectures, and competitions. Covering everything from cutting-edge technologies to the science embedded in everyday life, the festival offers engaging programs and content for visitors of all ages, from students to adults. More than Korea’s premier science festival, it continues to evolve as a people-centered urban festival and a leading global platform for science and technology culture.
sponsor: Ministry of Science and ICT, Daejeon Metropolitan City

title: Namhansanseong World Heritage Programs
overview: Season-long programs at UNESCO-listed Namhansanseong: palace education experiences, the OUV Expedition storytelling walk along the walls, a climate-protection program for the fortress, and participatory lectures remembering the 1636 siege.

title: Yangju Hoeamsa Temple Site Royal Festival
overview: Hoeamsa was the greatest temple of late-Goryeo Korea — King Taejo Yi Seong-gye retreated here — and its excavated site is on UNESCO's tentative list. The festival reenacts the royal procession and governor's welcome, with site-mystery quests, bell experiences, heritage performances, temple-food talks, and healing concerts among the ruins.

title: Busan Spring Flower Exhibition
overview: Busan Citizens Park in full spring dress — 'Garden Go Round': flower sculptures and topiary, themed beds, bonsai and wildflower special exhibitions, a national flower-tea contest, proposal photo zones, and a growers' market.

title: Gangjin Jeolla Byeongyeongseong Fortress Festival
overview: A history festival inside the actual walls of Jeolla Byeongyeongseong — the garrison fortress that commanded Jeolla and Jeju for 500 years: soldier-drill reenactments, period costume, and traditional performances along the ramparts.

title: Seonnong Daeje Royal Farming Rite
overview: The 47th reenactment of Joseon's royal farming rite at Seonnongdan altar — where kings prayed for good harvests and plowed the first furrow themselves. After the rite and royal procession, the crowd shares seolleongtang from giant cauldrons: the beef soup whose very name, tradition says, comes from this altar.

title: Culture Lounge Gyeonggi-Jang
overview: A hands-on cultural space in Suwon showcasing local content from across Gyeonggi Province in one place. 'Local Radar' builds a personalized Gyeonggi travel plan around your tastes; the 'Gyeonggi Ceramics Shop' combines pottery-craft experiences with tea tasting. The space mixes exhibition, performance, and participation — less a museum than a browsing room for what the province around Seoul has to offer.

title: Biseulsan Azalea Festival
overview: Korea's largest azalea colony — some 300,000 pyeong across Biseulsan's 1,000m summit plateau — turns the mountaintop pink in mid-April. Running since 1997, the festival pairs shuttle-accessible viewing with performances at the mountain base; the summit fields at full bloom are among Korea's great spring sights.

title: Play Turns Into Science!
overview: The Incheon Children's Science Museum's Science Day festival: science shows, family challenges, roaming events, robot and AI experiences, and hands-on programs built for kids across the museum.

title: Jeonju Hanok Village Traditional Performance Parade
titleFull: Jeonju Hanok Village Traditional Performance Parade (한옥마을전통연희 퍼레이드-노상놀이야)
overview: The Jeonju Hanok Village Traditional Performance Parade is packed with various street performances, allowing visitors to experience Jeonju's folk culture on the streets. During the parade, visitors can witness Jeonju gijeopnori, a representative traditional performance of Jeonju; madangnori, a traditional performance featuring dance, music, and storytelling through various forms, or sing along to folk labor songs.
place: Jeonju Hanok Village Taejo-ro Street (Namcheongyo Bridge – Gyeonggijeon Shrine)

title: Gochang Green Barley Field Festival
overview: Korea's original landscape-agriculture festival: 770,000 square meters of young green barley waving at Hagwon Farm, drawing 300,000 visitors each spring since 2004. Walk the barley path (3,000 won), browse farm markets, and catch the fields at their photogenic peak from mid-April to mid-May.
fee: Parking 10,000 won (refunded in local currency) · barley path 3,000 won

title: Queen Jeongsun Culture Festival
overview: A festival for Queen Jeongsun, who was separated from the deposed boy-king Danjong at eighteen and spent sixty years gazing east toward his exile from Dongmangbong hill. Her story of 'purple longing' becomes a neighborhood festival of remembrance and consolation at Sungin Park.

title: Hangang River History Tour
overview: Guided walking tours along the Han River, pairing riverside scenery with the history layered around it. Sixteen courses cover different stretches of the river and nearby heritage sites, each led by a Hangang interpreter. Tours run in two daily slots (10:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00) and take about two hours. It is one of the simplest ways to turn a riverside walk into something with a storyline — though note the commentary is primarily in Korean.
place: Hangang parks and nearby heritage sites

title: Reading Korea Campaign Launch
overview: A World Book Day launch event at COEX's Byeolmadang Library: a mass book-opening performance and message wall kicking off the national reading campaign, with side programs through the weekend.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: International Horticulture Goyang Korea
tel: • 1330 Korea Travel Hotline: +82-2-1330 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)  • For more info: +82-31-908-7750~2
overview: International Horticulture Goyang Korea, an international flower exhibition,  is considered to be Korea’s representative international flower exhibition. The festival takes place at Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang with organizations, groups, and companies from all over the world showcasing flowers and various products made with flowers. Also, unique and rare plants exhibition, indoor garden decorated with flower art pieces, outdoor theme parks, making of flower plant experience, flower arrangement contests and other cultural events and performances are planned to add more joy to the flower festival.
fee: Refer to the website for details

title: Icheon Ceramics Festival
overview: The 40th Icheon Ceramic Festival is a celebration of ceramic culture held at Icheon Ceramics Village and throughout Sagimakgol Pottery Village in Icheon, Gyeonggi-do. Renowned for its high-quality clay and advanced kiln techniques, Icheon has long been one of Korea’s leading ceramic centers, preserving and advancing a ceramic tradition that bridges the past and the present. Marking its 40th anniversary, this year’s festival reflects on the history and significance of the Icheon Ceramic Festival while exploring new directions for the future of ceramic culture. During the festival, ceramic artists and visitors come together to share the artistic value of ceramics and experience the creative process firsthand through programs such as pottery wheel workshops and wish-writing activities on large ceramic pieces. The festival also features a wide range of exhibitions and sales, showcasing everything from traditional pottery to contemporary ceramic art. Academic seminars, competitions, and performances further expand the festival's role as a platform for cultural and artistic exchange. Through the active participation of local ceramic artists and residents, the festival contributes to the local economy while sharing the excellence of Icheon’s ceramic culture with the world.
place: Icheon Ceramics Village, Sagimakgol Pottery Village

title: Gwangju Heritage Night Tour
overview: The 10th anniversary of Gwangju's heritage night: the '8 nights' format — night views, history tours, crafts, exhibitions, performances, food, market, and stay — around the May 18 Democracy Plaza and the old town's heritage sites.
place: May 18 Democracy Plaza and heritage sites

title: Hampyeong Butterfly Festival
addr: 27, Gonjae-ro, Hampyeong-eup, Hampyeong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The 28th Hampyeong Butterfly Festival will be held under the theme “Dreaming Butterflies, A Journey Begins.” This year’s festival captures the atmosphere of a special spring picnic, featuring vibrant displays of flowers and butterflies throughout the venue. Surrounded by colorful blooms and fluttering butterflies, visitors can enjoy a variety of hands-on activities and performances that celebrate the beauty of life and nature. It is the perfect spring outing for families, couples, and friends to share joyful moments and create lasting memories together.

title: Gwangju Royal Ceramic Festival
overview: Gwangju (Gyeonggi) housed the royal kilns that fired Joseon's palace porcelain, and its festival at Gonjiam Ceramic Park revives that lineage: wheel-throwing and traditional ceramic workshops, madang plays, performances channeling 500 years of royal ware, and K-pop guest stages.

title: Asian Esports Games 2026
overview: Seven Asian nations compete in Jinju across six titles — PUBG Mobile, Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8, KOF XV, eFootball, Eternal Return — plus a K-pop dance AI platform as a demonstration event, wrapped in a culture-festival format. Free entry.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Korea Science Festival in Gyeonggi
overview: Korea's flagship science festival at KINTEX, themed 'imagination becomes daily life': 60 years of national research achievements plus AI-in-everyday-life exhibitions, hands-on programs, and shows over three April days. Free.

title: Gijang Anchovy Festival
overview: Thirty years of spring anchovies at Daebyeon Port: free myeolchi sashimi tastings, boat-fishing trips, surprise seafood auctions, bare-hand fish catching, a song contest, EDM parties, an anniversary parade, and fireworks over the harbor — Busan's definitive taste-of-spring festival.

title: Udo Conch Festival
overview: Udo — the little island off Jeju's east coast — celebrates its horned turban conch: harbor restaurants serve conch dishes, the youth association grills samples, and visitors completing island challenges earn goods and boat discounts at Cheonjin Port.

title: Miryang Heritage Night Tour
overview: A night festival at Yeongnamnu — the grand riverside pavilion counted among Korea's three finest: the '8 nights' program with Eungcheon Arirang performances and falling-fire displays over the Miryang River, plus the Arirang market and artist stalls.

title: Nongae: Open-Air Historical Musical
overview: A musical staged on the Nam River itself, where the story happened: Nongae, the gisaeng who pulled a Japanese general into the water at Uiam Rock during the Imjin War, retold on a floating stage beneath the lit Chokseongnu pavilion with fireworks and full-scale staging. Runs during the Jinju Nongae Festival.

title: Cheongnamdae Spring Flower Festival
overview: Spring at the former presidential villa on Daecheong Lake: flower displays, daily music performances, wildflower and bonsai exhibitions, plus art special exhibitions across the lakeside compound.

title: Taebaek Heavenly Wild Greens Festival
overview: Korea's highest city greets its late spring with mountain greens: highland namul with intense flavor sold at source prices, plus food streets, night markets, contests, and performances at the Jangseong market grounds.

title: Dureup Wild Greens Festival
overview: A village festival in Gapyeong for dureup (angelica shoots) and spring greens: farm markets, food stalls, music, prize draws, and children's programs at the Chorongi Nest village.

title: NAORA Show: Night of Light
overview: A night media-art show at Ganhyeon Tourist Area in Wonju, where sheer rock cliffs meet a slow river. Part one is a warm-up of busking, live instruments, and dance; the finale projects video across a natural rock face 250m wide and 70m tall using 12 projectors and 7 lasers, synchronized with a musical fountain that fires jets up to 60m high. It shares the site with the Sogeumsan Grand Valley suspension bridges — do the skywalk before dark, then stay for the show.
place: NAORA Show Plaza, Sogeumsan Grand Valley

title: Jongmyo Myohyeonrye Ceremony
overview: The only Joseon state rite in which royal women took part: the newly married queen or crown princess presenting herself at Jongmyo shrine. The 2026 edition pairs a musical recreating Queen Inwon's 1703 ceremony with royal costume photo experiences at the UNESCO-listed shrine.

title: Gangseo Children's Fairy Tale Festival
overview: The 14th children's festival of Gangseo, themed 'fairy tales drawn together by children and AI': a street parade from the digital-content high school to Banghwa Park, then AI storybook experiences, rides, food, and shows.

title: Spring Walk Seoul
overview: A non-competitive 7.5km spring walk around Namsan's northern loop from Baekbeom Plaza: warm-up stretching, brand booths and sampling, stage games, and a finisher medal — a packaged city-walking event (entry 42,000 won).

title: Yun Bong-gil Peace Festival
overview: A family peace festival at the shrine of independence hero Yun Bong-gil in his hometown of Yesan — education programs at his memorial hall, family activities at his birth home, and a youth exhibition marking 80 years since his remains returned to Korea.

title: Hoeryongpo Spring Outing Festival
overview: Spring at Hoeryongpo — the famous river bend where the Naeseongcheon nearly circles a sand-island village: canola blooms, sand play, performances, and flea markets, with the observatory view over the meander ranking among Korea's best spring panoramas.

title: Taean International Horticultural Healing Expo
titleFull: Taean International Horticultural Healing Expo (2026 태안국제원예치유박람회)
overview:
As the world’s first horticultural healing expo, this year's Taean International Horticultural Healing Expo is held under the theme, “Finding a Healthy Future in Nature: Horticulture and Healing.” A variety of exhibition halls are featured throughout the venue. Visitors can explore special halls that highlight the importance of horticultural therapy, present the current landscape and future outlook of the industry, and trace its development over time. Dedicated exhibition spaces introduce outstanding products from leading companies by category, while experiential exhibits showcase advanced smart farm facilities from the region. 

In addition, the expo features vibrant outdoor attractions, including themed gardens, a healing garden, and a symbolic clock tower. Held in spring, the expo offers a wonderful opportunity for families to enjoy nature while discovering the healing power of horticulture.
fee: Adults (ages 19-64) 15,000 wonTeenagers (ages 13-18) 12,000 wonChildren (ages 3-12) 9,000 won* Free admission: Children under 2 years old

title: Saeyeongyo Bridge Weekend Show
overview: Seogwipo's signature night program at Saeyeongyo Bridge, where performances meet the harbor scenery. Every Friday and Saturday evening from late April through October, the waterfront hosts music, dance, and performance acts under the lights, capped by a fireworks show over the water and a musical fountain. Afterward, cross the bridge for a lit-up night walk on Saeseom Island. Schedules can shift with the weather.

title: Yi Sun-sin Festival
overview: Admiral Yi Sun-sin — the naval commander who defeated a far larger Japanese fleet at Myeongnyang in 1597, and the most revered figure in Korean military history — was born in what is now Jung-gu, Seoul, and the district holds a birthday festival at the site. It is staged as a party rather than a commemoration: a giant birthday cake carrying 481 messages, a naval honour guard parade, an 'Iron Man Yi Sun-sin' contest for residents, and stage performances. A food zone brings together 20 of the district's restaurants, a flea market sells Yi Sun-sin merchandise, and the activity area runs from paper-hat making and calligraphy to VR horseback riding, turtle-ship puzzles and a Roblox birthday party.
place: Around Yi Sun-sin's birthplace, near Myeongbo Art Hall

title: Asan Admiral Yi Sun-sin Festival
overview: Asan — home of Hyeonchungsa, the national shrine to Admiral Yi — marks his birthday with its biggest festival, running since 1961: parades, reenactments, and programs on his life and loyalty across the hot-spring city and the shrine grounds.

title: Goesan Space City: Star Explorers
overview: A hands-on children's exhibition at the Goesan Eco Museum built around an imagined 'space ecology', exploring fruits and plants through seeing, touching, and moving. Kids question, imagine, and build their own stories through the interactive course, with parents cast as fellow guides on the expedition. A useful rainy-day or family stop if you are in the Chungbuk countryside.

title: Hangang Night View Tour
overview: A relaxed guided night walk along the Han River with stories behind the skyline, on two courses: the Banpo Moonlight Course (Seorae Island, Some Sevit, the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, and Jamsugyo Bridge) and the Yeouido Starlight Course (Hangang Art Park, Mapo Bridge, the floating stage, and the water-light plaza). Runs Friday and Saturday evenings, 19:00–20:30. Free, but spots are allocated by lottery.

title: Jinbong Saemangeum Barley Field Festival
overview: Green barley to the horizon on the Saemangeum plain: walk freely through the waving fields, browse farm markets, and let kids loose in the play zones — a photogenic green-season counterpart to autumn's golden paddies.

title: Imsil N Pet Festa
overview: Korea's boldest pet festival, in the county building a companion-animal cluster — held at the Osu Loyal Dog site, home of Korea's most famous dog legend: FCI agility competition, bonding programs, and a special dog-friendly train tour making the trip itself part of the festival.

title: Gwacheon Jazz Picnic
overview: Ten Korean and international jazz acts play free on Gwacheon's civic plaza while the audience picnics on the lawn — vocal-jazz-forward lineups, artist signings, coloring and soundbook programs, food trucks, and a delivery pickup zone.

title: Boseong Green Tea Festival
addr: 775, Nokcha-ro, Boseong-eup, Boseong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Celebrating its 49th year, the Boseong Green Tea Festival will be held this year under the theme of Boseong Matcha. In today's fast-paced world, where the need for rest and rejuvenation is greater than ever, visitors can recharge both body and mind amid the tranquility of the region's lush green tea fields. Set against the breathtaking backdrop of emerald tea plantations, the festival offers a variety of tea-themed experiences, including tea leaf picking, tea making, creating and enjoying personalized tea blends, and green tea therapy programs. Through these immersive activities, visitors can fully experience the physical, emotional, and mental benefits of green tea.
place: Korean Tea Culture Park & Boseong tea fields

title: Hyeonchungsa Moonlight Night Tour
overview: The national shrine of Admiral Yi Sun-sin opens after dark for a spring edition: light-scaped grounds, performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs giving the solemn shrine a different, softer register by night. Free.

title: Seoul Street Performance: Every Corner Live 2026
overview: 150 artist teams selected by open call perform across central Seoul's streets and plazas through late November. The point is the surprise: performances appear where people already are — station exits, plazas, park corners — rather than on ticketed stages. Free by nature; times and spots vary by performance.

title: Hongcheon Wild Greens Festival
overview: Hongcheon — Korea's largest county, 85 percent forest — brings its high-mountain greens to market: myeongi, dureup, eomnamu shoots, and prized san-yangsam (wild-simulated ginseng), with a special grill house pairing fresh greens with Hongcheon pork.

title: Hajeon Clam Five-Senses Festival
overview: Wade into the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Gochang mudflats and dig your own clams: Hajeon village is Korea's biggest short-necked-clam producer, and May clams are at their plumpest. Cooking programs, food stalls, and discounted direct sales round out the tidal-flat day.

title: Hwaseong Haenggung Palace Night Opening 2026
overview: Hwaseong Haenggung — the grandest of Korea's temporary royal palaces, built for King Jeongjo's visits to Suwon — opens after dark for its signature night program, 'Moonlight Hwadam: Stories of Flowers under the Moon'. Flower installations and atmospheric lighting turn the palace courtyards into a slow evening walk, quieter and more intimate than daytime visits. It sits inside the UNESCO-listed Hwaseong Fortress, so you can pair it with a night walk on the fortress wall.
fee: Adults 2,000 won · Youth/military 1,500 won · Children 1,000 won

title: Haman World Watermelon Festival
overview: Haman watermelons — famously sweet from the county's sun and soil — star in a festival of giant watermelon-punch sharing, tastings, contests, and performances at Hamju Park, at the source of one of Korea's favorite summer fruits.

title: Yeosu Turtle Ship Festival
overview: Yeosu was the headquarters of Admiral Yi's Jeolla Left Navy, and this festival marks the fleet's first sortie of May 1592: naval rite reenactments, parades, and programs around Yi Sun-sin Square in the old naval city where the turtle ship was built.

title: Busan Lotus Lantern Festival
overview: Busan's edition of Yeondeunghoe — the UNESCO-listed lantern festival for Buddha's Birthday: a grand lantern parade, traditional lantern exhibitions, and celebration stages at Songsanghyeon Square, carrying a 1,200-year tradition through the city night.

title: East Asia Culture City Andong
overview: Andong holds Korea's 2026 East Asia Culture City title, opening a year of Korea-China-Japan exchange: a three-country opening festival with traditional performances, East Asian games and food fairs, cooking classes, and city pavilions from the partner cities.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Andong City

title: Seocheon Wild Flounder & Sea Bream Festival
overview: Wild-caught flounder and sea bream from the clean West Sea at Maryangjin Port: bare-hand flounder catching, boat-fishing trips, and harbor-fresh sashimi — a hands-on spring seafood weekend.

title: Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival
overview: The Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival is held every May in Hadong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, Korea’s first tea cultivation site.
