Designated by the government as an Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival, the festival celebrates Hadong’s wild tea, long renowned for its rich flavor and aroma and grown in the area’s pristine natural environment. Since hosting the Hadong World Tea Expo in 2023, Hadong has strengthened its identity as a “tea wellness culture city” and continued to enhance the value of its tea industry and culture. In 2026, the festival marks its 29th edition. Visit Hadong in May, when the landscape is at its freshest and greenest, and enjoy music and art programs such as “Busking in a Teacup” and “Melody on Tea Leaves,” along with healing programs including tea classes, book talks, and walks along the Horibyeong Byeolcheonji Trail. Here, a single cup of tea can turn an ordinary day into something special while allowing visitors experience the full flavor and charm of Hadong. This year, the festival will also feature a variety of Children’s Day programs for the whole family on May 5.
place: Hadong Wild Tea Healing Center (Tea Café Hadong), Hadong Wild Tea Museum
sponsor: Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival Organizing Committee

title: Ansan Street Arts Festival
overview: Korea's leading street-arts festival since 2005: international and Korean companies transform Ansan's plazas and streets each May with aerial theater, large-scale spectacle, and intimate street pieces — expanded kids' zones and strong accessibility make it genuinely for everyone. Free.

title: Chajeon General & Princess Noguk Festival
overview: Andong's spring folk festival across the old downtown: the spectacular Chajeon Nori — massed log-frame battles pushed by teams of men — and Notdari Bapgi, the human-bridge walk of women, both centuries-old local traditions, joined by parades and international performances.
place: Andong Station 1942 and Mask Dance Park

title: Mungyeong Chasabal Festival
overview: Celebrating its 28th edition, the 2026 Mungyeong Chasabal (Tea Bowl) Festival is one of Korea’s leading festivals, where deep-rooted tradition meets contemporary creativity. The festival will run for ten days from May 1 to 10, 2026, at the Mungyeongsaejae Open Set, surrounded by the area’s stunning natural scenery. Mungyeong ceramics are crafted in traditional wood-fired mangdaengi kilns and fired at temperatures exceeding 1,300°C. Rather than relying on elaborate decoration, they are known for their rustic, natural beauty. Chasabal tea bowls possess a quiet charm that brings a sense of calm to those who use them. This year’s festival will offer even more hands-on programs for Millennial and Gen Z visitors and families. With more opportunities to participate, stay, and explore, the festival continues to evolve into an immersive experience visitors can truly be part of.

title: Ulsan Onggi Festival
overview: The Ulsan Onggi Festival is Korea’s only festival dedicated to onggi, the traditional earthenware that has been an integral part of Korean life for more than a thousand years. Held in Oegosan Onggi Village in Ulju-gun, where artisans continue to produce onggi using traditional techniques, the festival naturally serves as a showcase the region’s signature craft. It also contributes to the promotion of everyday onggi use and the continued development of this traditional industry. Visitors can enjoy onggi-making demonstrations by master artisans, as well as a variety of hands-on programs, exhibitions, and performances.

title: Haman Citizens' Day
overview: Haman's community day at Hamju Park: reunion halls, nongak competitions between townships, county sports day, performances, fireworks, food fairs, and free markets.

title: Damyang Bamboo Festival
addr: 130, Jungnogwon-ro, Damyang-eup, Damyang-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Held under the slogan “Shine Bright, Bamboo!” this year’s festival celebrates the spirit of bamboo with a message of hope. During the day, visitors can enjoy lively hands-on programs and performances. At night, the bamboo forest lights up, offering a completely different festival experience. The festival features a wide range of programs that bring together tradition and modern creativity. As visitors walk through the bamboo grove and listen to the wind moving through the trees, they can take in the history, culture, and natural beauty of Damyang. With family, couples, and friends, visitors can enjoy the beauty and calm of bamboo while reflecting on the value of sustainable nature. In the green bamboo forest, the festival offers bright, memorable moments filled with hope.
place: Damyang Sports Complex, Juknokwon, Dambit Music Hall

title: Yeoncheon Paleolithic Festival
overview: The Yeoncheon Paleolithic Festival is a hands-on prehistoric culture festival held at the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site in Yeoncheon, where some of the earliest humans on the Korean Peninsula once lived. The site is world-renowned for the discovery of Acheulean hand axes, evidence that highly advanced Paleolithic people inhabited Korea some 300,000 years ago. Once a year, Jeongok-ri becomes a gathering place for prehistoric cultures from around the world, inviting modern visitors to step into the world of early human life through a wide range of immersive experiences. Rooted in the historical significance of the Jeongok-ri Prehistoric Site, the festival promotes harmony between cultural heritage and the public, strengthens the region’s identity, and demonstrates how archaeological sites can be actively preserved while being brought to life.

title: DDP Children's Design Festival
overview: DDP's outdoor spaces become a kids' design land over the Children's Day holidays: toy play, design play, and family play zones where children build, imagine, and create across the plaza and lawn hill. Free.

title: Children's Seonbi Festival
overview: Kids sit the state exam of Joseon: a play-based festival at Yeongju's Seonbi World teaching scholar-gentleman culture through a mock gwageo exam, honor parades for the 'top graduates', and Joseon-themed games across the traditional campus.

title: Goheung Aerospace Festival
overview: A space festival at Naro Space Center — Korea's rocket launch site: Black Eagles aerobatic shows, launch-vehicle site tours (advance booking), real hardware exhibitions, and family space programs under the slogan 'Space Signal'.

title: Gangbuk Children's Day Festival
overview: Children's Day at North Seoul Dream Forest — the big green of northeast Seoul: magic, bubble, and character shows, craft and traditional-game booths, safety education, and play zones across the park (entry 1,000 won).

title: Family Arts Festival TokTok
overview: Seoul's first fine-arts festival built for young children and parents: an outdoor painting canvas ('Paint TokTok'), a pop-up art playground ('Sense TokTok'), and movement-friendly performances ('Rhythm TokTok') around Seoseoul Lake Park for Family Month.
place: Seoul Arts Education Center Yangcheon and Seoseoul Lake Park
sponsor: Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Yanggu Gomchwi Festival
overview: Gomchwi — the aromatic 'bear's greens' beloved for ssam wraps — peaks each May in Yanggu, its biggest growing region. Tastings and sales at source, performances, and family programs at the leports park in one of Korea's cleanest inland counties.

title: Boryeong Children's Day Celebration
overview: Children's Day at the Mud Expo Plaza, run alongside the AMC motor festival: K-pop dance and bubble shows, a puppet play, and two days of craft booths — keyrings, soap, perfume, cooking classes — plus a wooden playground and photo zones.

title: Hangang River Festival
overview: In May, the Hangang River offers a range of activities that appeal to both children and adults. Programs include plays based on Korea's folklore, as well as family-friendly experiences. Visitors can also participate in silent yoga sessions using headsets or enjoy the natural scenery of Seoul through activities such as kayaking, yachting, and river cruises. These programs provide a variety of ways to experience the Hangang River during the spring season.
place: Ichon Hangang Park next to Parking Lot 3 grassy area
fee: Free (Separate fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Pocheon Pet Festa: Spring Edition
overview: A pet festival in the Hantangang gorge parkland: dog trekking along the river, pet-fitness yoga, a dog olympics, live big-dog encyclopedia, kids' agility challenges, and a pet fair — open equally to visitors without pets.

title: Elixir Expedition: Find the Herb of Immortality!
overview: A storytelling mission tour through Donguibogam Village in Sancheong: chatbot clues and mission books lead explorers through the herbal-medicine theme park's halls and gardens on the trail of the legendary elixir — learning the county's healing traditions along the way.

title: Children's Ceramics Festival
overview: The Gwangju National Museum marks its new ceramics culture hall with a hands-on kids' festival: children's wheel-throwing, a pottery market, expert talks, and outdoor performances over the Children's Day holidays. Free.

title: Jongmyo Daeje Royal Ancestral Rite
overview: The grand ancestral rite for Joseon's kings and queens at Jongmyo shrine — UNESCO-listed both as architecture and as living ritual, with its solemn court music and line dances performed as they were for 500 years. Held the first Sunday of May; one of the most profound spectacles in Korea, and free.

title: Young Choreographers Creative Showcase
overview: An annual platform staging new works by Korea's emerging choreographers, selected by open audition — the launching pad that has fed the country's contemporary dance scene for years. At the Daehangno Arts Theater small hall.

title: 104th Children's Day Ceremony
overview: The national Children's Day commemoration hosted by the welfare ministry: a formal ceremony with performances and programs centered on children's rights and healthy growth.

title: Seoul Circus Festival
overview: Korea's only circus-dedicated festival, on Nodeul Island around Children's Day: traditional big-top acts to contemporary circus — aerial, tightrope, juggling, acrobatics — plus try-it-yourself workshops, exhibitions, and markets. Free.
sponsor: Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Wonju Children's Day Festival
overview: A citizen-run Children's Day tradition since 1989, organized by Wonju's civic groups around themes of life, peace, and dreams — 2026 runs on 'dreams' with stages and programs at the Dancing Carnival grounds.

title: Love for Living Things Children's Festival
overview: A Children's Day festival at the National Institute of Biological Resources: play-based programs rediscovering Korea's endangered wildlife through a child's eyes and teaching biodiversity by doing.

title: Family Month Children's Festival
overview: A 'kids-venture' amusement-park day at Yeongjong Seaside Park: circus, anime OST concerts, bubble and magic shows, samba percussion, bounce rides, mini trains, water play, treasure hunts, and family photo booths.

title: Little Farmer's Color Farm Adventure
overview: The National Agricultural Museum's Children's Day week: little farmers explore the museum turning a colorless countryside into a vivid color farm through performances, hands-on programs, and events.

title: Children's Day Library Festival
overview: The National Library for Children marks its 20th anniversary with a Children's Day festival — 'growing with stories': family reading programs, exhibitions, performances, a drawing-contest award ceremony, library golden bell quiz, and paper-plane wish launches.
place: National Library for Children and Young Adults

title: Uiwang Children's Railroad Festival
overview: Korea's only railway-themed children's festival, in its 20th year beside the Railroad Museum and Wangsong Lake: diesel-locomotive and train simulators, rail-safety quizzes, drawing contests, and family stages — train-mad kids' heaven.
place: Wangsong Lake Park and Railroad Museum

title: Growing with Science (Children's Day)
overview: Children's Day at the Incheon Children's Science Museum: science storytelling shows, family challenges, XR and robot-dog programs, rocket launches, solar-penguin builds, and craft benches across the museum.

title: Chunhyang Festival
overview: Taking place in Namwon, Chunhyang Festival celebrates the love between Chunhyang and Lee Mongryong, based on the famous Korean love story, Chunhyangjeon. Held since 1931, the festival aims to spread the story not only around Korea but to international visitors as well through hands-on experiences and moving performances. The highlight of the festival is the beauty pageant that attracts many people.
fee: Free (fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Culture Flows at Seoul Plaza
overview: Free open-air concerts on the outdoor stage at Seoul Plaza, running roughly eight months from May to December. The 2026 season opens on May 6 and cycles through pop, hip-hop, jazz, bands, and performance acts month by month, in the plaza in front of City Hall — easy to fold into any evening downtown.

title: Daegu Yangnyeongsi Herbal Medicine Festival
overview: Yangnyeongsi has been Daegu's herbal medicine market since 1658 — 367 years — and remains the largest in the country, a dense grid of streets where the smell of dried roots and bark carries for blocks. The festival opens the market up with traditional-medicine programmes, performances and hands-on sessions built around a time-slip theme. Entry is free; a few activities charge up to 3,000 won.
fee: Free entry (some activities up to 3,000 won)

title: Miryang Arirang Festival
overview: The Miryang Arirang Festival celebrates and preserves Miryang Arirang, which was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2012. First launched in 1957 as the Miryang Cultural Festival, it has grown into one of Gyeongsangnam-do’s leading regional festivals. Visitors can enjoy the Miryang Arirang Competition, Arirang-themed experiences, and a variety of traditional cultural programs. The highlight of the festival is Miryanggang Odyssey, a fantasy musical brings together thousands of years of Miryang’s history and the spirit of Miryang Arirang. Featuring spectacular performances, beautiful music, and captivating storytelling, the production leaves a lasting impression on audiences and stands as one of the festival's signature attractions.
place: Yeongnamnu Pavilion, Miryanggang Riverside, Namcheongangbyeon-ro, Naeil-dong Shopping District

title: Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival
titleFull: Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival (두위봉 철쭉축제&산맥페스티벌)
overview: During the Duwibong Azalea Festival & Mountain Range Festival, visitors can walk along azalea-lined mountain trails and unwind by clear valley streams during the day, then enjoy live performances and DJ sets in the evening. They can also visit the Arirang exhibition at the historic former National Land Development Corps building for a closer look at Jeongseon Arirang and the area’s local history. A range of hands-on activities, including wellness programs and bracelet-making, is available, along with beer and local food zones offering regional specialties and craft brews.
place: Uirimgil Daebak Market and Dangokgyegok Valley in Sindong-eup

title: National Bread Pride Festival
overview: Seoul's first national bread festival on the Garak Market sky garden: 22 famous bakeries from around the country, 100-plus breads, concerts and magic shows, bread cosplay with prizes, kids' zones, and coupon events among spring flowers.

title: Ulsan Soeburi Iron Festival
overview: Korea's only iron-culture festival, at Dalcheon Cheoljang — the peninsula's oldest iron mine, worked for two thousand years: live reenactments of traditional iron smelting, performances, and programs tracing how this ore became the root of Ulsan's industrial rise.

title: Yuseong Hot Springs Culture Festival
overview: The signature festival of Daejeon's hot-spring district, genuinely resident-run: programs fusing Yuseong's two identities — healing waters and science city — with foot baths, performances, and neighborhood booths across Yurim Park.

title: Hangang Seoraeseom Picnic Concert
overview: A spring picnic concert on Seoraeseom — the flower island in Banpo Hangang Park: acoustic bands and classical ensembles on the riverside stage, a picnic food market, treehouse and beanbag zones for lingering.

title: Daejeon Together Day Festival
overview: A World Day for Cultural Diversity festival at Seodaejeon Park: 33 experience and counseling booths, Kyrgyz dance, Chinese wushu, a world costume fashion show, visa and settlement consulting, and global games — Daejeon's residents and international community in one park.
sponsor: Daejeon Metropolitan City · Ministry of Justice

title: Mokpo Marine W Show 2026
overview: Mokpo's flagship night show and one of the signature attractions of this southern port city: a multimedia performance combining a floating sea stage, Korea's largest marine fountain, and fireworks over the water. Over five years it has drawn more than a million viewers across 51 shows. The 2026 edition scales up the sea-stage performances, fireworks, and choreographed fountain work. Free viewing from Peace Plaza on the waterfront.

title: Busan Wheat Festival
overview: A food-culture festival on the wheat theme in Buk-gu — once a major wheat entrepôt: world wheat cuisines in a 3,200-pyeong camping-ground food lounge (zero-waste, QR ordering), plus lotus-pond programs and local collaborations.

title: Paju Spiel 2026
overview: Korea's answer to Essen Spiel: an outdoor board-game festival by Korea Boardgames drawing 20,000 players to the European-styled Paju campus — tables under spring sun in the gardens, from hardcore strategy to family-first fun. Free.

title: Seoul World Cities Culture Festival
overview: The 30th anniversary of Seoul's global-culture festival at DDP: embassy zones from dozens of countries, world performance stages and busking, world food and dessert zones, traditional costume and games, and international photo exhibitions.

title: Uijeongbu Music Theatre Festival
overview: Korea's dedicated music-theater festival, every May at the Uijeongbu Arts Center for 25 years: international productions alongside Korea's best, with open-air stages and lobby concerts where amateurs share billing with professionals.

title: Sunyang Barefoot Festa
overview: Sunyang Barefoot Festa is an exclusive festival that participants can walk or run barefoot along the red clay trail while enjoying a cultural experience. Feet are thought to be the second heart in our body as it connects the entire living being. Moreover, stimulating the feet by walking on clay road are known to have positive health benefits such as preventing and healing diseases, and stress relieving. This event invites people of all ages to participate in a healthy and fun walking festival where attendees can admire the beautiful nature scenery as well as take part in various entertaining programs.
place: Jangdong Forest Park in Gyejoksan Mountain

title: Gyeomjae Culture & Arts Festival
overview: Marking 350 years since the birth of Jeong Seon (Gyeomjae) — the master who invented true-view landscape painting — at the museum devoted to him: a national sketching contest, exhibitions, performances, and traditional games where he once painted the Han River's western reaches.

title: Donghak Peasant Revolution Commemoration
overview: The national ceremony for the 1894 Donghak Peasant Revolution — the popular uprising against feudal corruption and foreign encroachment — held on the anniversary of its first victory at Hwangtohyeon, at the National Museum of Korea.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Fishing Village Life & Tourism Fair
overview: Fishing villages from around Korea set up on Gwanghwamun Square: village booths, specialties, and hands-on programs presenting coastal life — with evening wave-and-sea healing lounges — for city dwellers imagining a life by the sea.

title: Forest Food Festival
overview: The Korea Forest Service brings the country's forest products to Gwanghwamun: mushrooms, nuts, wild greens, and regional specialties to taste and buy, with performances and hands-on programs on the square.

title: Suragan Royal Dining Experience
overview: Dine where the palace cooked: an evening in Gyeongbokgung's Sojubang kitchen quarter tasting royal cuisine with court performances and games, attended by costumed court staff — see, taste, watch, feel, as the name promises. 30,000 won, reservation required.

title: Seongju Chamoe Melon & Life Culture Festival
overview: Seongju grows most of Korea's chamoe (the yellow oriental melon), and its festival in the ancient Seongbak Forest — beside the royal placenta shrine of King Sejong's princes — pairs melon tastings, auctions, and lounges with life-themed walks under 500-year-old willows.

title: Global Yeongdo Coffee Festival
overview: Busan's Yeongdo island — an emerging coffee destination anchored by harbor-warehouse roasteries — hosts a coffee-industry festival: specialty tastings, roasting demos, barista performances, and pop-ups against the shipyard seascape.

title: Haeundae Sand Festival
overview: Held every year between May and June, the Haeundae Sand Festival is Korea’s largest sand festival. Set on Haeundae Beach, one of the nation's most iconic seaside destinations, the festival celebrates the beauty of Haeundae and highlights the value of sand as an important marine resource. Each year, world-class sand sculptures, hands-on programs, and performances are presented under a new theme. In 2026, the festival will be held under the theme “Busan,” showcasing the city’s dynamic transformation from past to present and into the future, while highlighting the unique charm that has captivated visitors from around the world. The festival runs from May 15 to 18, while the sand sculpture exhibition will remain open through June 14.

title: Millennium Naju Eupseong Culture Festival
overview: Naju — 'the Hanyang of Honam', a former provincial capital of a thousand years — stages madang plays, gate-guard ceremonies, and heritage programs around Geumseonggwan hall and the old town walls.

title: King Sejong's 629th Birthday
overview: Sejong City celebrates its namesake king's birthday with a book fair, talk concerts, performances, and Hangeul education programs at Central Park — linked to the Sejong falling-fire festival the next evening.

title: When Roses Feel (Rose Festival)
overview: Fourteen thousand roses of 120 varieties bloom at Igok Rose Park in Daegu for a fantasy-themed spring festival — 'a day in the rose kingdom' — with art programs and evening openings among the beds.
hours: Varies by day (evenings on opening day)

title: Yeon Deung Hoe
overview: Started approximately 1,200 years ago during the Silla dynasty and continued through the Goryeo Yeon Deung Hoe and Joseon lantern festival, the Yeon Deung Hoe Festival is a traditional festival registered as an Intangible Cultural Heritage and UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity. The lanterns at Yeon Deung Hoe Festival brighten the heart and the world!

title: Sejong Nakhwa Falling Fire Festival
overview: Sejong's designated intangible heritage brought to a lake park: nakhwa — charcoal-filled mulberry-paper wicks strung between poles — burn and shed embers like falling petals over the water, an old rite against misfortune reborn as one of Korea's most photogenic night spectacles. Free.
place: Sejong Lake Park and Central Park

title: D.FESTA Street Performance Festival
overview: Daehangno's street-arts festival turns 20: two days of performances filling Marronnier Park and the surrounding theater district, taking art out of the black boxes and onto the street where Korea's small-theater culture lives.

title: Jakdang Festa
overview: Busan's youth-culture space Jakdangso marks its sixth year with a maker festival: a youth creators' market and live stages outdoors, participatory exhibitions in the BNK gallery, and creator workshops upstairs.

title: Central Asia Spring Festival
overview: The cultures of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Tajikistan fill Seoul Plaza: yurt experiences, 20 culture booths, traditional performances, food tastings, crafts, and costume try-ons over a spring weekend.

title: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival
titleFull: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival (하늘숲길 걷기축제)
overview: Sky Forest Trail Walking Festival (Haneulsupgil Walking Festival) is a family-friendly forest festival held along the Sky Forest Trail at an altitude of 1,300 meters. Visitors can explore the area’s rich natural environment, including native trees, wildflowers, insects, and various plant species, making it an especially enjoyable experience for children and families. The festival features well-maintained walking trails converted from former coal transport routes, offering safe trekking courses suitable for participants of all ages, along with forest-themed experiential programs. Surrounded by pristine nature, the festival provides a relaxing opportunity to unwind and enjoy healing time outdoors.
fee: Participation fee 15,000 won* Free for children under 24 months old

title: Suwon Theatre Festival
overview: Running since 1996 and now centered on 'theater in public space': street theater, circus, and site-specific performance turn the leafy Sangsang Campus into a forest party each May — free, outdoors, and family-friendly.

title: Flower Gazing + Water Gazing Book Spot
overview: An open-air library series in Gongju's old royal quarter: reading lounges by the Jemincheon stream (a Local 100 culture spot), author talks, poetry readings, night performances, and archive photo exhibitions of the neighborhood's past.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Wonju Yongsugol Poppy Festival
overview: Korea's only village-run ('ri'-level) flower festival: what began as one returning farmer's 300-pyeong poppy patch in 2005 now covers 13,000 pyeong with poppies and 43 companion blooms in a Wonju valley — a 'star village' pick among Korea's 1,200 rural communities.

title: Ulsan Grand Park Rose Festival
overview: Three million roses in Korea's finest rose garden: Ulsan Grand Park's 18th rose festival pairs the massed blooms with performances, citizen programs, and night lighting that turns the garden luminous after dark.

title: 14th Diaspora Film Festival
overview: A film festival on migration and coexistence in Incheon — the port where Korea's first emigrant ship sailed for Hawaii in 1902: international films on diaspora themes, talks, and programs at the Incheon Art Platform. Free.

title: Geumsa Chamoe Melon Festival
overview: The capital region's only chamoe-growing town celebrates its 20th melon harvest by the Namhangang: melon-picking, surprise auctions, family programs, and a youth music festival at Geumsa Park in Yeoju.

title: Gokseong International Rose Festival
addr: 232 Gichamaeul-ro, Ogok-myeon, Gokseong-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Gokseong International Rose Festival is a vibrant spring celebration featuring 1,004 varieties of roses, including rare European species and famous roses from around the globe. Held at the landmark Gokseong Train Village, the festival is filled with the romantic fragrance of roses.

title: Busan Old Town Revitalization Festival [Taxchelin]
overview: Enjoy the charm of of Busan's old downtown through "Taxchelin!" Taxulain is a combination of taxi and Michelin, and it is a festival where you can enjoy performances, experiences, and tours centered around local hidden gems recommended by veteran taxi drivers with over 10 years of experience. The festival highlights on a  different theme each year, making every moment special.

title: Gangneung Bread Festa
overview: Gangneung's bakeries and dessert makers gather in the courtyards of the old Daedohobu government office: pop-up, experience, and event zones with local favorites, tastings, and prize draws — the coffee city proves it can bake too.

title: Danyang Sobaeksan Royal Azalea Festival
overview: Royal azaleas crown Sobaeksan's ridgelines in late May, and Danyang celebrates below with a mountain-spirit rite, riverside stages, busking, and food streets — pairing summit hikes through the pink fields with the town's famous garlic dishes.

title: Hwaseong Boating Festival
overview: The Hwaseong Boating Festival, Hwaseong’s signature festival, is the largest marine cultural event in the Seoul metropolitan area. Visitors can experience a variety of activities on the waters of the West Sea, including sailing yachts, powerboats, marine cable cars, and the Voyage of the Pungnyudan. The festival also features the Messengers of the Wind dance parade, showcasing the energy and enthusiasm of local residents, as well as spectacular performances and fireworks that light up the night sky. From mudflat ecology programs and traditional fish-trap experiences to a large beach playground and marine plogging, the festival offers a diverse range of attractions and activities both on land and at sea.

title: ING Festival
overview: A family ESG festival at Understand Avenue in Seongsu: children's art contests, values markets, and a retro 'romance festival' of 90s–00s playground games, stationery shops, and snack stalls bridging parents' nostalgia and kids' discovery.

title: Goesan Red Taste Festival
overview: Goesan built a festival on one color: the red of its famous gochu peppers and early-summer blooms. Spicy-food challenges, red-themed events, and flower fields at the organic expo plaza — with festival-linked discounts at local attractions and markets.

title: Hangang Love Children's Drawing Contest
overview: The 23rd riverside drawing contest for kindergarteners and elementary kids by the Han River authorities — art on the river's ecology, with performances and hands-on programs at the Ttukseom waterside stage.

title: Busan Family Festival
overview: Family Month at Busan Citizens Park: the 20th edition runs 40 family-play booths, caricature and counseling corners, exhibitions, and the 'language of family' video contest — a gentle, free day out for households of every shape.

title: Jeju Food and Wine Festival
overview: The Jeju Food & Wine Festival (JFWF), Jeju’s premier gastronomic festival, is a cultural event that showcases the value of Jeju’s local ingredients and culinary heritage to both domestic and international audiences through dishes crafted from the island’s pristine produce. The festival presents a diverse program of culinary experiences, including Gala Dinners featuring multi-course fine dining by renowned chefs, and Gourmet Week, which highlights collaborations with chefs, celebrities, and brands at leading local establishments. Signature ingredients of Jeju, such as its famed pork, are showcased through curated dining events led by top restaurants and guest chefs. Visitors can also take part in interactive cooking classes, dessert and café showcases, and other programs that allow one to fully experience Jeju's gastronomic culture.
fee: * Refer to the official website for details
sponsor: Jeju Food & Wine Festival Organizing Committee

title: Yeongju Sobaeksan Royal Azalea Festival
overview: The Yeongju side of Sobaeksan's azalea season: guided ridge treks through the pink colonies with ecology interpreters, plus food and farm markets at the Punggi ginseng pop-up park below — the mountain's sweeping views doing the heavy lifting.

title: Chuncheon Mime Festival
overview: The Chuncheon Mime Festival is one of Korea’s leading performing arts festivals, connecting the city, art, and its people through mime, an art form that communicates through movement. Held every year during the last week of May in Chuncheon, the city of water and springtime, the festival is recognized as one of the world’s three major mime festivals, alongside France’s Mimos Mime Festival and the London Mime Festival in the United Kingdom. Over the years, it has developed a distinctive artistic identity that blends Chuncheon, mime, and festival culture into a genre of its own. Through wordless movement and the creative fusion of water, fire, flowers, light, video, and other artistic forms, the festival expresses the emotions and spirit of the city and its people. It is also a vibrant “nanjang” festival that transforms the desires and energies of both the city and the times into artistic expression. Under the theme “Body Landscape,” the 2026 Chuncheon Mime Festival will take place from May 24 to 31. Beginning with the opening nanjang, Ah! Surajang, the eight-day festival will present diverse "body landscapes" throughout Chuncheon through theater performances, Walking Mime, Art Nanjang X, and the all-night Dokkaebi Nanjang.
place: Festival Theater MIME and other locations across Chuncheon
sponsor: Chuncheon Mime Festival, KBS Chuncheon Broadcasting Center

title: Radiant Seogwipo (Hayeong)
overview: Seogwipo strings day into night: an olle-trail city walk by day, a seaside music festival at dusk, and a drone light show over Jaguri Park after dark — the southern city's coast as one continuous evening.

title: Korea Youth Expo
overview: The national youth expo at Yeosu Expo: some 300 booths on AI, digital, and renewable-energy careers, 20-plus participation programs, a youth talent stage, and a water-boom festival for teens from across the country.
sponsor: Ministry of Gender Equality and Family · Jeollanam-do

title: Imsil N Rose Festival
overview:
The Imsil N Rose Festival is a spring event held in the Rose Garden at Imsil Cheese Theme Park in Imsil-gun, Jeonbuk State. Set within a 65,705 ㎡ rose garden showcasing over 150 varieties and more than 22,000 rose plants, the festival is designed as a tourism-focused event that integrates performances, hands-on experiences, and food offerings.

Featuring a rose-themed parade and performances, interactive programs, and local agricultural and specialty products, it seeks to provide visitors with a rich and engaging experience while supporting the local economy and strengthening the region’s tourism brand. As an inaugural festival, it also captures a unique sense of freshness and anticipation, offering an emotionally engaging springtime experience that encourages longer stays through immersive, rose-inspired content and participatory activities.

title: Asan Oeam Village Night Tour
overview: The 500-year-old folk village of Oeam — stone walls, thatched roofs, and noble houses still lived in — opens after dark: lantern-lit lanes, performances, and heritage programs recreating the romance of a Joseon night stroll.

title: Janghang Port Kkolgap Seafood Festival
overview: A fishermen's-association festival at Janghang Port on the Geum River estuary: fresh sashimi and dried seafood at co-op prices, tastings, and a waterside raw-fish cafe — pair it with the Sinseong-ri reed fields and the old smelter chimney nearby.

title: Pyeonghwa Ondam
overview:
“Peace On: Dam” in Dongtan is a cultural event designed to bring the theme of “peace,” which often feels distant, into everyday life. As part of the regional peace consensus-building project first launched by the Ministry of Unification in 2026, the event provides an opportunity to engage with the concepts of peace and unification in a familiar, local setting.

Held near residential communities, the event invites residents to participate in a variety of cultural experiences, share stories with family and neighbors, and reflect on topics that are not often considered in daily routines.

At the venue, visitors of all ages can enjoy a diverse lineup of hands-on programs, performances, and interactive activities. Through moments of laughter, creativity, and connection, “Peace On: Dam” fosters a warm and welcoming festival atmosphere that encourages a renewed appreciation for peace through small but meaningful experiences.

title: Cheongju Pet Culture Event
titleFull: Cheongju Pet Culture Event (청주시 반려동물 문화행사 )
overview: The Cheongju Pet Culture Event “School Bell Ring Ring Ring” takes place on the spacious lawn of Chungbuk Health and Science University. The open setting provides a safe and comfortable environment where children can run freely, while professional programs organized by the Department of Pet Culture offer structured and engaging activities.  The event creates opportunities for pet owners to connect with one another and participate in a variety of hands-on experience programs, all within the pleasant surroundings of the university campus. Designed with families in mind, it offers an inclusive atmosphere that welcomes visitors of all ages.
place: Chungbuk Health and Science University Lawn
fee: Free (some booths may require a participation fee)
sponsor: Chungbuk Health Science University Department of Pet Culture

title: Ansan Seongho Culture Festival
overview: A festival for Yi Ik (Seongho), the great Silhak pragmatist philosopher who spent his life in what is now Ansan: a Confucian memorial rite at his shrine, local folk performances, silhak-themed experiences, a golden-bell quiz, and museum lectures.

title: Port Village Busan
overview: Port Village Busan takes place at Pier 1 of Busan Port, transforming a 4,300-pyeong site (approximately 14,200 ㎡) into a unique underwater-themed village. The event will bring together over 60 of Busan’s most popular local brands. Visitors can explore everything from limited-edition foods available only within this mysterious “underwater village” to signature menus from well-loved eateries. The market will also feature a curated living and lifestyle shop, along with a variety of pop-up stores. As a large-scale, 12-day market, Port Village Busan offers an exclusive opportunity to experience a diverse range of food, shopping, and activities centered around its immersive underwater theme.
sponsor: Food Travel Co., Busan Tourism Organization

title: Palsaek Chanran: Regions Full of K
overview: A special exhibition at the Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae asking where the 'K' in K-culture actually comes from. Through regional-content displays and media art, it traces how local histories, arts, and cultural assets across Korea's provinces feed into today's K-content — an argument that hallyu's roots run through the regions, not just Seoul. Runs through December on the first floor of Sarangchae, next to the former presidential compound.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Easygoing Hangang Triathlon Festival
overview: A triathlon with no rankings and no clock: swim, cycle, and run the Han River at your own pace over three days at Ttukseom — 30,000 participants and 660,000 visitors made it Seoul's feel-good sports festival. Entry 30,000 won per event.

title: Gochang Getbol Mudflat Festival
overview: Walk the UNESCO World Natural Heritage mudflats at Mandol: barefoot tidal-flat ecology programs, daily performances, and discounted local seafood — including free tastings of Gochang's famous pungcheon eel.

title: Iksan Modern History Culture Festival
overview: 'Walking through Iksan's time': the arts street and Somni modern-history quarter stage the years from 1910s opening to liberation — era theme songs and busking, land-registry mission tours, colonial-era costume experiences, and independence-movement performances.

title: Seongbuk World Food Festival Nurimasil
overview: Seongbuk-ro becomes a world food street for the 18th Nurimasil: national dishes and embassy booths from dozens of countries, a coexistence-themed parade, world culture experiences, and stages — Seoul's neighborhood take on the global table.

title: Bangaun Festival (Dog Walking & Giving)
overview: A dog-and-owner festival at Ansan Lake Park where exercise meets charity: a walking event, pet-etiquette games, health counseling, experience zones, and gift packages for every participating pair.

title: Jeju International Tourism Marathon Festival
overview: The Jeju International Tourism Marathon Festival, which began in 1995, is the first citizen-participation marathon in Korea that allows the general public to participate. It is a sports festival that can be enjoyed by people of all ages, families, and couples, featuring a marathon course along the beautiful coastline of Jeju.
fee: FULL (42.195 km) 50,000 wonHALF (21.0975 km) 50,000 wonGeneral course (10 km) 40,000 won

title: Organic Day
overview: Korea's organic-farming day (June 2 — a pun on 'yugi-nong') celebrated at Cheonggye Plaza: eco-food events, a certified-organic market, webtoon contest exhibitions, and consumer programs on climate-friendly eating.

title: Eumseong Pumba Festival
overview: The Eumseong Pumba Festival is rooted in the life of the late Choi Gwi-dong, often remembered as a saint of compassion and love. Although he lived with a disability himself, Choi traveled throughout Mugeuk-ri in Geumwang-eup collecting food—not for himself, but for beggars who were too weak even to beg. His life later inspired Father Oh Woong-jin to establish Kkottongnae, and his example of selfless service continues to inspire many today. Various explanations have been passed down regarding the origin of the word pumba. Traditionally, it refers to an onomatopoeic refrain used in gakseori taryeong, the songs associated with wandering performers and itinerant peddlers. The Eumseong Pumba Festival combines this traditional image of pumba with Choi Gwi-dong’s spirit of philanthropy and compassion. Although modern society enjoys greater material prosperity, spiritual emptiness and social inequality still remain. The festival was created around the idea that society can find catharsis through satire and humor and be healed through love and sharing. For this reason, the Eumseong Pumba Festival has become a unique cultural festival dedicated to putting the values of love, compassion, and sharing into practice.
place: Seolseong Park and Kkottongnae in Eumseong-eup

title: Korea Wine Festival
overview: Korea's biggest wine festival in Yeongdong — the country's largest grape and wine county: local winery tastings, food pairings, parades, and wine-making exhibitions along the Yeongdong stream. The place to survey how far Korean wine has come.

title: Korea Buddhist Culture Expo
overview: A Buddhist-culture trade fair at EXCO Daegu across nine genres — temple food (the 'urban temple kitchen' special), architecture, craft, art, ritual, tea — spanning traditional philosophy to contemporary art in the heartland of Silla Buddhism.

title: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef Festival
titleFull: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef Festival (남해 마늘한우축제)
overview: Namhae Garlic & Korean Beef celebrates Namhae’s signature agricultural products: garlic and premium Korean beef. The festival takes place at the Namhae Exile Literature Museum, with five nearby parking areas for easy access. Visitors can browse and purchase a wide range of local specialties in one place, prepared by local farmers and fishermen, and enjoy the event alongside residents. There is a shuttle bus that takes passengers back and forth between the parking lot and the festival venue.

title: Jeodo Giant Octopus Festival
overview: The fishing families of Daejin Port — Korea's northernmost East Sea harbor — cook their own giant Pacific octopus catch: blanched slices, spicy salads, and harbor-side feasting where the daemuneo actually lands.

title: Gwangalli Eobang Festival
overview: The Suyeong area has long been rich in fishery resources and was one of the first places in Busan where fishing developed on a large scale. During the Joseon Dynasty, Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong Naval Command was established here, along with eobang, a cooperative fishing organization formed by local fishers and naval forces. The fishing practices of that era have been preserved and passed down through Jwasuyeong Eobang Nori, a traditional folk performance based on the work and customs of fishing communities. The Gwangalli Eobang Festival takes its name from this heritage. Celebrating the history of Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong and the folk traditions of Korea's coastal fishing villages, it has become one of Busan’s representative cultural festivals.
place: Gwangalli Beach and Suyeong Historical Park

title: Geoje Okpo Great Victory Festival
overview: Commemorating Admiral Yi's first naval victory of the Imjin War (Okpo, 1592): memorial rites, a victory procession with navy band and honor guard, water-gun battles, drone light shows, and a musical staged with real ships and fireworks on Okpo bay.

title: Hansan Ramie Fabric Cultural Festival
overview: The Hansan Ramie Fabric Cultural Festival is Korea’s leading eco-friendly traditional textile festival, celebrating Hansan Mosi Weaving, which is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Held every June around the Hansan Mosi Museum in Hansan-myeon, Seocheon-gun, the festival offers a variety of ramie-related cultural programs, including Hansan Mosi School, mini loom-weaving experiences, and Jeosanpal-eup Gilssamnori. Bringing together tradition, nature, and hands-on experiences, the festival offers visitors a unique opportunity to explore the history and artistry of Korea’s renowned ramie culture.

title: Sokcho Silhyangmin (Displaced People) Culture Festival
overview: Korea's only festival of displaced-family culture, in the city where war refugees from the North built Abai Village: performances, exhibitions, and food carrying the memory of separation into its third and fourth generations — Sokcho's most distinctive story, told by those who live it.

title: Seocho Classic Theme Park
overview: A neighborhood park in Bangbae becomes a classical-music theme park: open-air concerts, music workshops, an art-salon flea market, water play set to classical scores, and picnic zones — classical without the concert-hall formality.

title: Hoengseong Lake Trail Festival
overview: A 'festival of rest' on section 5 of the Hoengseong Lake trail: 9km of quiet waterside walking with three viewpoints and small installations, plus stalls of local hangwa sweets and fresh produce from the valley farms.

title: Gunsan Craft Beer & Blues Festival
overview: Korea's only truly local craft-beer festival: four Gunsan breweries pouring beer brewed from 100% Gunsan-grown barley malt, 16 blues bands from home and abroad, and 30 of the food-famous city's best restaurants at the modern-history museum lot. Entry 6,000 won with 5,000 back in local vouchers.

title: Camping Cooking Festival
overview: A three-day stay-in camping cook-off at Imjingak's Peace Nuri campground, now in its 10th year: teams cook competition menus at their campsites for a judged final, with regional-food booths, performances, and family programs around the grounds.

title: Firefly & Insect Festival
overview: An ecology festival at the Chungbuk agricultural research institute: nighttime firefly watching, insect exhibitions and hands-on programs, and family ecology education — one of the accessible places to see fireflies near Cheongju.

title: Mudeungsan Humanities Festival
overview: A thinking-person's festival at Mudeungsan National Park's Jeungsimsa district: lectures, performances, and quiet programs built on the mountain's name — 'without rank' — inviting visitors to switch off the noise and build a thought of their own.

title: Forced Mobilization Memorial Gathering
overview: A remembrance event for victims of wartime forced mobilization and their families: a stamp walking tour through Gwanghwamun's colonial-era historic sites from Cheonggye Plaza, with quizzes, performances, and booths open to all.
sponsor: Foundation for Victims of Forced Mobilization

title: Yangpyeong Wheat Festival
overview: Golden wheat fields at Gahyeon-ri host Yangpyeong's eco-minded wheat festival: field photo spots at peak gold, a Korean-wheat food market, wheat-and-sool classes, and environment-first operations.

title: Stay Night: Yeongdeok Starlight Walk
titleFull: stay night, 별빛따라 걷는 영덕의 밤
overview: A family night event on Yeongdeok's sunrise coast: azalea planting, a starlight night trek along the shore, snow-crab games, and kids' programs under one of the east coast's clearest night skies.

title: Goyang Haengju Culture Festival
overview: Commemorating the Battle of Haengju (1593) — one of the Imjin War's three great victories, won with civilians hurling stones beside General Gwon Yul's troops: a national stone-throwing (bak-bursting) contest, drone and fireworks shows over the Han, and the Haengju musical at the fortress where it happened.

title: Jeungpyeong Jangttul Field Song Festival
overview: The 20th festival of Jangttul dure nongyo — Jeungpyeong's designated communal farming songs: field-song demonstrations, farming and traditional-food experiences, kids' ssireum contests, and folk performances at the folklore museum.

title: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Riverside Concert
titleFull: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Riverside Concert (창립 65주년 기념 한국경제인협회와 함께하는 2026 서울시향 강변음악회)
overview:
To mark its 65th anniversary, the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra presents the “2026 Seoul Riverside Concert with the Federation of Korean Industries” on June 13 at Yeouido Hangang Park. The event brings together a full orchestral performance, appearances by world-class guest artists, and a fireworks finale.

Open to all free of charge, the concert offers a chance to experience live classical music alongside the nightscape of the Hangang River, creating a memorable and romantic evening in the heart of the city.

title: N Seoul Tower Global Night Walk
titleFull: N Seoul Tower Global Night Walk (N서울타워 글로벌 나이트워크)
overview:
The N Seoul Tower Night Walk is a nighttime walking event that begins at Baekbeom Square and continues through the Seoul Education Research & Information Institute, Samsuni Stairs, Waryongmyo Shrine, Seokhojeong Pavilion, and the southern access road, before reaching N Seoul Tower Plaza. The program features an approximately 6-kilometer course, offering participants the opportunity to enjoy the night views of central Seoul and the surrounding landscapes of Namsan Mountain.

Before and after the walk, a variety of programs are available, including warm-up stretching sessions, live performances, interactive events, checkpoint rewards, completion rewards, on-site activities, and the Namsan Night Market. Participants also receive commemorative items such as a functional T-shirt, LED armband, handkerchief, storage bag, finisher’s medal, certificate, and a coupon pack.

title: Le Mouton Walking Club in Suncheon
overview: A 1,400-person branded walking event through Suncheon Bay National Garden: a morning walk from Green Island to the workation center, finished with a garden concert — walking-shoe culture meets Korea's most famous garden city. Entry 10,000 won.

title: Sejong Dano Festival
overview: Dano — the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, once one of Korea's great holidays — revived at Sejong Lake Park: hair-washing in iris water, rice-cake pounding, 15 craft benches, ssireum wrestling for adults and kids, and holiday foods.

title: Gimje Moaksan Music Festival
overview: A healing music festival on the lawn before Geumsansa — the great Baekje-founded temple under Moaksan: multi-genre outdoor stages, barefoot red-clay path walks, kids' programs, and Gimje farm-food booths in the green of early summer.

title: Mureung Byeoryucheonji Lavender Festival
overview: A limestone quarry turned wonderland: Mureung Byeoryucheonji's emerald lakes and gardens host June lavender fields with day and night programs, illuminated evenings, lavender foods, and city goods — one of Gangwon's most surreal landscapes.

title: Global Creator Art Fair
overview: An international creator fair on the plaza by Hongdae's exit 8: busking stages, markets, and content showcases connecting Korean and international creators in Seoul's indie-culture heartland. Free.

title: Gyeonggi Rice Gimbap Festa
overview: A gimbap expo built on Gyeonggi-grown rice: a national gimbap cooking contest, tastings, exhibitions, and sales booths — Korea's everyday seaweed roll given a whole convention hall.

title: Gangneung Danoje Festival
overview: A UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity with a thousand years behind it: eight days of Confucian rites, all-night shamanic gut ceremonies where gods and people meet, and Korea's largest open-air market — 71 programs across 13 fields drawing over half a million visitors. This year's theme, 'unraveling', centers Dano's oldest promise: let worries loosen and relationships come untied.

title: Rural Travel Festival
overview: A one-day 'countryside vacation in Seoul' on Seoul Plaza for Urban-Rural Exchange Day: farm-stay and rural-tourism booths, healing-farm and forest-trail showcases, and young rural-travel startups pitching offbeat countryside itineraries to city dwellers.
sponsor: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

title: Seoul Food Show (K-Food Show)
overview: A food-industry expo at the aT Center themed 'K-Street Food, To Global Tables': Korea's beloved bunsik snack culture as global content, with food trucks, tasting programs, and new-product showcases aimed at teens through thirty-somethings.

title: Jinju Garden Expo
overview: Marking its new provincial-garden designation, Jinju opens the forests of Wolasan for a citizen garden expo — 'tend, feel, share': garden art exhibitions, healing programs, and cultural events among the trees of 'the pearl in the Wolasan woods'.

title: Korea International Ocean Film Festival (KIOFF)
overview: A film festival devoted entirely to the sea, held at the Busan Cinema Center. It began in 2015 as 'Sea & See' and has run under its current name since 2018. The programme ranges from the scale and strangeness of the ocean to the crises now facing it, with the stated aim of imagining a future in which people and the sea coexist. Screenings are 5,000 won a ticket — cheap by festival standards — and the venue is the same landmark building that hosts the Busan International Film Festival.
sponsor: Busan Metropolitan City · Korea Ocean Business Corporation

title: Daegu International Musical Festival (DIMF)
overview: Asia's musical-theater festival turns 20: official invited productions from abroad (many never staged in Korea), premieres of supported new Korean musicals, a university musical festival, and audition programs — the global art market that made Daegu Korea's musical city.
place: Daegu Arts Center and theaters citywide
fee: Varies by show — see official site

title: Craft Week Korea
overview: Ten days of craft across the whole country, anchored this year in Buyeo with five regional clusters (Sejong–Gongju, Jeonju–Gochang, Chilgok–Gumi, Ulsan–Busan, Jeju–Seogwipo): exhibitions, workshops, markets, and craft tours letting handwork seep into daily life since 2018.
place: Buyeo hub city and venues nationwide
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Taehwagang Maduhee Festival
overview: Maduhee is a traditional folk game rooted in Hakseongji, a historical record of Ulsan from the reign of King Yeongjo of the Joseon Dynasty. Through storytelling and historical interpretation, the festival reinforces the tradition and identity of Maduhee while evolving into a community-led tourism festival. By combining summer leisure activities along the Taehwagang River with lively evening programs such as the Chimaek (chicken and beer) Festival, it offers a unique seasonal experience. As the first major summer festival of the year in Korea, the Taehwagang Maduhee Festival provides a venue for community unity through the Maduhee Tug-of-War, in which citizens from across Ulsan take part. Held in the historic downtown area of Jung-gu, Ulsan, the 2026 festival features the grand Maduhee Tug-of-War, Water Tug-of-War on the Taehwagang River, the Chimaek Festival, EDM parties with DJs, ssireum (traditional Korean wrestling) competitions, and a variety of hands-on experiences.
place: Taehwagang Riverside and Seongnam-dong Area, Jung-gu, Ulsan

title: Chuncheon Mini Sool Festa
overview: Sixteen Chuncheon breweries pour traditional sool at the Hwadong 2571 complex: tasting and bottle-sale booths, food pairings from local F&B brands, brewing-salon lectures, 'fermentation yoga', a drinking book club, and a media exhibition — a compact local liquor culture festival.

title: Hoengseong Summer Night Festa
overview: A 'night picnic' on the Seomgang riverbanks: daytime water activities flowing into evening acoustic stages, food zones, rest lounges, and photo spots — a stay-all-day night-tourism festival in Hoengseong's clear river country.

title: Gangwon Hanwoo Day
overview: Gangwon's premium hanwoo beef takes over Chuncheon's city-hall plaza: discounted sales direct from producer co-ops, free grilled tastings, gifts for buyers, kids' shows, and a flea market — a city-center beef festival connecting farms and tables.

title: Gimpo Ara Marine Festival
overview: The capital region's only inland marina throws its summer festival: kayaking, SUP, and water-bike sessions on the Ara waterway, dinghy races, an opening concert, food trucks, and a local market — marine leisure made easy an hour from Seoul.

title: Seoul Gugak Festival
overview: Korean traditional music on the Han River: master-musician stages, participatory madang, hands-on heritage programs and one-day classes at Banpo's Moonlight Plaza — gugak crossing from tradition into the trendy, free by the water.

title: Busan Port Festival
overview: Busan's harbor celebrates itself: fireworks over Busan Harbor Bridge, daytime water-leisure programs on the waterways, port tours, and maritime-culture experiences around the North Port waterfront park — the working port's history made festival.

title: Choansan Hydrangea Festival
overview: Ten thousand hydrangeas of 17 varieties on a restored hillside in northern Seoul: night lighting, picnic decks, an ecological pond and waterfall, plus two days of food trucks and concerts (including Jang Sa-ik and orchestra stages). Public transit recommended — no on-site parking.

title: Yangsan Ungsang Hoeya Festival
overview: The Ungsang district's festival of its Ubul shrine and rain-rite legends: a citizens' military-band parade re-enacting the Joseon Tongsinsa envoy processions, the local Nongcheong Jangwon folk-play, and the signature 'Ungsang Water Festa' — the old rain prayer reborn as a summer water performance.

title: Yonggol Dance Festa
overview: Yongdusan Park — 'Yonggol', birthplace of Korea's 90s dance boom and a shrine of world b-boy culture — hosts a youth dance-battle festival: any genre, any teen dancer can take the stage, with events and food stalls around the competition.

title: 2026 Culture Day: Culture Delivery
overview: A traveling arts program that brings street performances to places with the least access to culture — remote villages, border areas, and industrial districts across the capital region and Gangwon. Young and senior performing teams stage free shows in everyday local spaces from June to October, delivering the arts to audiences who rarely get them nearby.
place: Samgot-ri Village, Yeoncheon and other sites
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: MyK FESTA
overview: A four-day K-culture mega-event at KINTEX: top-tier K-pop stages (MyK Live), talk sessions with K-content icons (MyK Voice), brand pop-ups and showcases (MyK Street), and a B2B export fair (MyK Trade) — the industry and its global fans in one place.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Busan International Magic Festival
overview: The world's largest magic festival, running since 2006: a magic convention, the international busking championship, and gala shows at Busan Cinema Center and Haeundae Beach — the dream stage of Korea's million magic fans.

title: Semiwon Lotus Culture Festival
overview: Semiwon — a water-and-flower garden wrapped on three sides by Paldang Lake, Gyeonggi's first designated provincial garden — celebrates its lotus season: 270 plant species, traditional Eastern garden courts, exhibitions and performances timed to the blooms, on ground where the Joseon scholar Jeong Yak-yong once bridged the Han with boats.

title: Masterpieces and Teatime: A Cup of Calm in Light and Color
titleFull: 안다미로귀때박물관 기획전시 '명화와 티타임(Teatime) : 빛과 색채로 마시는 차 한 잔의 여유'
overview: A themed exhibition at the Andamiro Gwittae Museum pairing famous paintings of tea with the real teapots and cups depicted in them. When the Age of Exploration carried tea from Asia to Europe, it carried the vessels too — and painters began capturing the warmth of teatime in luminous color. From the quiet glow of William McGregor Paxton's 'Tea Leaves' to the silver teapot in Mary Cassatt's 'The Tea', the show lets you stand in front of the scene and the object at once.

title: Gangjin Hydrangea Road Festival
overview: Eight kilometers of hydrangea path winding up Boeunsan past the temples of Goseongsa and Geumgoksa: locally grown blooms line the trail, with performances, hands-on programs, and farm-product markets at the V-Land park below — 'Beautiful hydrangea, beautiful Gangjin'.

title: Busan Food Film Festa
overview: The Busan Food Film Festa is a unique cultural event that brings together film and food through a diverse range of programs and experiences. It offers an engaging platform where cinematic storytelling and culinary culture intersect. One of its signature programs, the Food Terrace, provides a setting to explore food-related themes in film while enjoying curated tastings guided by experts. The festival also features a flea market showcasing small businesses, a range of food trucks, and interactive programs such as pizza-making experiences suitable for families. With its rich blend of storytelling and gastronomy, the event offers a vibrant and memorable cultural experience.
fee: Free (separate fees may be required for certain programs)
hours: 12:00~20:00 *Please refer to the official website for detailed event times as they are subject to change.*
sponsor: Busan Food Film Festa Organizing Committee, Busan Cinema Center

title: Muan Lotus Festival
overview: Korea's largest lotus festival at Hoesan Baekryeonji — 100,000 pyeong, the East's biggest white-lotus pond, blooming since 1997: white lotus rising through a sea of green leaves, with lotus-themed programs, performances, and exhibitions in the far southwest.

title: Come to the Forest
overview: A family eco-festival on Jeju's forests: expert-guided forest expeditions ('Environment Guardians'), three-generation family programs, kids' flea markets, choir and nonverbal performances, character parades, and nature-play zones teaching conservation by doing.

title: Gyeongsan Cafe Festival
overview: A night-time cafe festival on the Namcheon riverbanks: a 'starlight night cafe' grand opening, limited-edition desserts fusing Gyeongsan's shinbi peaches with local specialty coffee, and a following week of orchestra and choir tours through 20 cafes across the city.

title: Daegu Chimac Festival
overview: The Daegu Chimac Festival is Daegu’s signature summer festival and Korea’s largest food-and-drink event celebrating the much-loved pairing of chicken and beer. Since its launch in 2013, it has grown steadily, now drawing one million visitors and helping boost the local economy while raising Daegu’s profile as a global destination. Selected in 2026 for Korea’s Local 100 list and as a Preliminary Global Festival, this year’s event will run from July 1 to 5 in and around Duryu Park. Beyond chicken and beer, the festival offers a full lineup of performances, exhibitions, hands-on programs, and promotional booths. The main venue, 2.28 Freedom Square, will be transformed into a water concert zone where water play meets electronic music, with a new 360-degree central stage added this year. Across the festival grounds, visitors can explore themed zones such as Daefrica Waterpia, Chimac Sing-along Club, and Chisangnakwon EGG Island. Artist-designed installations and photo zones will bring even more energy to the festival grounds.
sponsor: Korean Chicken and Beer Industry Association

title: ASYAAF 100
overview: The gateway art fair for Asia's young artists, now in its 19th year: 100 selected artists aged 19–39 show some 300 works at Art Chosun Space in two rotations, with visitor votes picking ten winners — where collectors meet future masters first.

title: Buyeo Seodong Lotus Festival
overview: Ten million lotus blooms on Gungnamji — Korea's oldest artificial pond, built by Baekje's King Mu, whose love story with Princess Seonhwa names the festival: lotus paths by day, illuminated pond magic by night, with performances, family programs, and Baekje's garden heritage all around.

title: WSL Siheung Korea Open Qualifying Series
titleFull: WSL Siheung Korea Open Qualifying Series (WSL 시흥 코리아 오픈 국제 서핑대회)
overview:
The WSL Siheung Korea Open is held at Wave Park in Siheung, Asia’s largest artificial surfing facility, over three days. As Korea’s first official World Surf League (WSL) Qualifying Series event, and the first to take place in an artificial wave pool, it has drawn global attention from the surfing community. The venue features a 2,240-meter-long cove and can accommodate up to 160 athletes and 20,000 spectators.

The competition features top surfers from multiple countries across men’s and women’s shortboard and longboard divisions. Recognized as a key international event, it is broadcast in several countries and serves as an important stage for competitive surfing in the region. The event is hosted by the Siheung and organized in collaboration with local sports and media partners, with support from national and regional institutions.

title: Gangneung Beach Beer Festival
overview: Craft beer on Gyeongpo Beach as the swimming season opens: a Blue Wave zone with stage shows, beer olympics, water-gun battles and EDM nights, and a Green Wave zone of pine-forest lounging and busking — brews from across the country plus Gangneung local food.

title: 9.81 Park Dog Festival
overview: A dogs-and-owners travel program at 9.81 Park in Jeju's Aewol hills: walks and activities through the greenery with coaching from celebrity vet Seol Chae-hyun and professional trainers — the dog-friendly Jeju trip, organized.

title: Stationery Fair Summer
overview: A fancy-goods and illustration fair at the aT Center: independent creators and brands selling stationery, fancy products, and illustration work to Korea's devoted stationery-collector crowd.

title: Yangpyeong Watermelon Festival
overview: Three Ws — watermelon, water, wellness: Cheongun's high-sugar, crisp watermelons (big day-night temperature swings do the work) star in tastings, contests, and watermelon foods, with kids' water play and family programs at the Yongdu folk market.

title: Daegu Apsan Festival
overview: Apsan — the healing mountain in the middle of Korea's hottest city — cools off its July: water-cannon games and family water-gun battles, a dress-code event rewarding loud aloha shirts with cool towels, stamp tours, and hand-drip and latte-art workshops tied to the Apsan coffee street.

title: Dancing Sangsoe: The Pilbong Gut Encounter
titleFull: Dancing Sangsoe: The Pilbong Gut Encounter(춤추는 상쇠〈만남〉)
place: Pilbong Cultural Village, 272, Gangun-ro, Imsil-gun, Jeonbuk-do

title: Busan Brand Festa
overview:
Busan Brand Festa is a large-scale consumer festival that highlights Busan, showcasing hidden gem brands from across the region and introducing them to both residents and visitors. This year’s event brings together over 190 leading local brands and well-known creators, offering a glimpse into the city’s diverse appeal.

In addition to local brand booths, the festival features a variety of programs, including a live drawing show by a popular webtoon artist and collaborative merchandise with well-known Busan-based food YouTubers. Visitors can also enjoy on-site cash coupon promotions and a range of events with prizes, creating a lively summer experience for friends and families alike.

title: Geumsan Samgyetang Festival
overview: Korea's first festival for its great summer restorative — samgyetang, ginseng chicken soup — in the ginseng capital itself: hearty bowls loaded with real Geumsan ginseng, modern ginseng-chicken snacks for younger tastes, herbal health programs, family water play, and night stages against the summer heat.

title: Ulsan 119 Safety Culture Festival
overview: Learn survival by playing: 93 programs across five themed zones at Ulsan's convention center — fire-escape and earthquake simulations, CPR training, firefighting robots and VR, and firefighter-for-a-day experiences for all ages.

title: Korea Petcance
overview: A pet expo at Gumico for the age of 15 million pet owners: spaces for dogs, cats, reptiles, and amphibians alike, adoption campaigns for rescued animals, and pet-industry booths — a vacation fair for the whole multi-species family.

title: Tongyeong Theatre Arts Festival
overview: Ten days of theater in the port city of artists: the 18th edition, themed empathy and connection, stages new works and contemporary reinterpretations where Tongyeong's memories and world narratives cross — the south coast's flagship performing-arts festival.
place: Tongyeong Citizens' Culture Center and citywide

title: Groove in Gwanak
overview: Seoul's street-dance battle festival, five years in and linked to Japan's World Dance Colosseum: popping, locking, waacking, breaking, house, and krump crews compete for a 7-million-won purse along Sillim's starlight stream — a ministry-award-winning youth culture festival.

title: Chilgok Honey Beer Festival
overview: Beer brewed with honey from Korea's largest acacia forests, and German-style sausages made by Benedictine monks at Waegwan Abbey: Chilgok's odd-couple festival adds honey crafts, water slides and water-gun play, balloon shows, and local stages at the Peace Fountain.

title: Board Game Con
overview: Korea's board-game convention at COEX: open play tables for all ages, tournaments, a designers' zone, and industry booths — hands-on tabletop gaming backed by the culture ministry and KOCCA.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · KOCCA

title: Gyeonggi Puppet Festival in Suwon
overview: Twenty-four years of puppetry: seven days of Korean and international companies — including Czech troupe Dazuma — performing across the Gyeonggi Arts Center's stages, a genre-spanning festival for audiences of every age.

title: Life Bookstore Book Fair
overview: Thirty-six local bookshops from across Korea gather in Jeonju under the slogan 'keep reading and it becomes your life': each shop brings its own character and life-book curations picked by the owners, with reading programs for every stage of life.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Chuncheon Summer Water Festival
overview: A lakeside water park festival at Chuncheon's waterfront: main, lazy-river, and toddler pools, a 30m mega-slide, and the new challenge-bounce obstacle escape — family water play in the lake city, Thursday through Sunday.

title: Contemporary Artist Project: Lee Wan — I Write
overview: An exhibition at the Seoul Arts Center's Calligraphy Museum reinterpreting traditional Korean calligraphy through contemporary art. Working from brush and ink, artist Lee Wan combines script, image, painting, and seal-carving to push at what calligraphy can be — and asks not 'is the writing beautiful' but 'why do we write at all'. A compact, thoughtful show where tradition and contemporary practice meet.
place: Gallery 3, Calligraphy Museum, Seoul Arts Center
fee: Adults 5,000 won · Ages 3–19 2,500 won · Seniors 65+ 3,000 won · Free for visitors with disabilities, veterans, Art Pass holders

title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival
overview: Korea's leading photography festival, held since 2002 in Yeongwol, a mountain county in Gangwon-do. The 24th edition runs July 17 to October 11 across the DongGang Museum of Photography and venues around the county. Highlights include the DongGang Photography Award exhibition — this year featuring Im An-na — and an open-call international show of 19 photographers selected from worldwide submissions, alongside a full slate of themed exhibitions. Worth combining with Yeongwol's river valleys and the Jangneung royal tomb.
fee: Adults 3,000 won · Youth/military 2,000 won · Children 1,000 won
sponsor: DongGang Photo Village Committee · Yeongwol Foundation for Culture and Tourism

title: Jeonju Chaekkwae Indie Book Fair
overview: Named for Joseon's itinerant book peddlers: independent publishers, creators, and bookshops from across the country selling new titles at Jeonju's culture warehouse quarter, with lectures, exhibitions, and events for the book-loving city.

title: Jangsu Cool Valley Festival
overview: A mountain-valley summer escape at Banghwadong recreation forest: swimming pools and water slides beside a clear natural stream, valley-night concerts, family programs, and Jangsu farm-food stalls deep in the cool of Jeonbuk's highlands.

title: Taebaek Sunflower Festival
overview: A purely private-run festival painting the highland canvas of Guwau village sunflower-yellow: fields at 800m elevation, artists' installations among the blooms, and a philosophy of quiet healing over commerce — one of Korea's most contemplative flower festivals.

title: Hongcheon Waxy Corn Festival
overview: The 30th festival of Korea's corn capital: Hongcheon hosts the nation's only corn research institute and supplies 78% of its seed corn, and its big day-night temperature swings give the chalok (waxy corn) its sweetness and chew — taste the difference at the Tori Forest park.

title: Dalseong Water Splash
overview: Daegu's first municipal water festival, back for round two at the Gangjeong-bo ARC plaza: young local performers plus special-guest stages, water-splash sessions against the 'Daefrica' heat, youth markets, and startup food trucks by the river.

title: Comic World Summer
overview: Korea's flagship amateur comics convention at KINTEX: fan-made zines, fancy goods, and illustration circles selling direct, gacha lotteries and stamp events, best-zine voting, and the cosplay stage where dance, song, and performance close the day.

title: Seoul Summer Beach
overview: A beach in the middle of Gwanghwamun: pools, water slides, water buckets and bounce pools in the Water Play zone, a sand hideout and rest lounges in the Play Wave zone, plus flea markets and food trucks — 'Wave Summer, Play Seoul', free downtown.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government · Seoul Tourism Organization

title: K-Heritage House
overview: Marking the 48th UNESCO World Heritage Committee session in Busan: all 17 of Korea's World Heritage sites in one exhibition, Memory of the World displays, heritage media art, royal gate-guard ceremonies, living-heritage craft demonstrations, and a K-goods shop at BEXCO.

title: Miryang Performing Arts Festival
overview: The Miryang Performing Arts Festival, which has established itself as Korea's leading summer performing arts festival, is held across Miryang City, including Miryang Arena and the Miryang Arirang Art Center. Selected by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the festival is designed to allow citizens and tourists to naturally encounter performances in their daily lives. Under the slogan "The City as a Stage, Daily Life as a Performance," the festival has significantly expanded its venues to include Miryang Arena, the Arirang Art Center, Eoreumgol Valley, and other locations throughout Miryang City. Diverse performances and rich events will take place during the festival period. From stages of warm empathy that bridge generations to unique immersive performances that boldly break down the barriers between stage and audience, a variety of theatrical performances blurring the boundaries between the audience and art are set to unfold against the backdrop of Miryang's beautiful nature and urban spaces.

title: Myeongju Puppet Festival
overview: Gangneung's beloved family puppet festival since 2014: hand puppets, paper-cup theater, puppet musicals, and shadow plays at the Myeongju arts yard — carefully selected productions with real storytelling that outgrow the 'kids only' label, drawing 10,000 visitors a year.

title: Music in PyeongChang
overview: Music in PyeongChang is dedicated to inspire the audience with the passion for music and build a foundation for future musicians. The festival welcomes all who love music with a variety of music programs that take place among the beautiful nature of Gangwon State.
place: Alpensia Concert Hall & Daegwallyeong Outdoor Stage (Music Tent)

title: Sanhwabi: HEXAGRAM 22
titleFull: 제48차 유네스코 세계유산위원회 특별공연 산화비 : HEXAGRAM 22
overview: A special performance for the UNESCO World Heritage Committee session: artists who wrestle tradition into the present day put Korea's intangible heritage on the BEXCO auditorium stage — tradition and contemporaneity colliding, reconciling, and breathing together. Free.

title: Jeju Rural Convergence Industry Expo
overview: An agri-food-tech expo at Jeju's international convention center: this year's theme pairs food tech with AI robotics, alongside producer-consumer markets, export trade meetings, and an international forum on rural convergence industries.

title: Busan Wartime Capital Heritage Night
overview: 'Walk the emotional heritage of the city of memory': Busan's 1950s wartime-capital sites open after dark — a media facade on Yeongdo Bridge, a pop-up museum of postwar daily life, young artists' showcases at the old Mildawon teahouse site, and AR stamp tours across 20 programs in 8 night themes.
place: Yeongdo Bridge (Yurari Plaza) and wartime-capital sites
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Busan Metropolitan City

title: K-Handmade Fair Busan
overview: The K-Handmade Fair serves as a platform for exchange between creators and consumers. It is also a space where visitors can explore the market trends and sustainability of creator brands. Held annually with a unique theme, the fair provides creators with an opportunity to showcase their products, while visitors can purchase trendy, high-quality handmade goods, check out DIY kits, and take part in various hands-on experience programs.
fee: On-site purchase 7,000 won / Online reservation 5,000 won* Please refer to the website for more info

title: Pyeongchang Heat Hunting Festival
overview: Ttamtti Park's spring water holds 10°C all year, and Pyeongchang built its summer festival on it: the water battle between the heat-ghost and the guardian spirit, giant water cannons, night camping under mountain skies, and cold makguksu noodles when you climb out shivering.

title: Ulsan Shipbuilding & Sea Festival
overview: Ulsan Shipbuilding & Sea Festival is held at Ilsan Beach with a feast of music and fun activities to enjoy, including concerts and a night run.
fee: Free (Separate fees may apply to programs)
sponsor: Ulsan Shipbuilding & Sea Festival Promotion Committee

title: Boryeong Mud Festival
overview: The Boryeong Mud Festival is Korea’s leading global summer festival, where visitors can enjoy mud in every possible way. Overlooking the expansive Daecheon Beach, the festival features a variety of zones, from the General Zone for full-scale mud activities to the Family Zone and Water Park Zone, where visitors of all ages can cool off and have fun safely. During the day, mud attractions help beat the summer heat, including Mud Mob Scene, a one-of-a-kind program featuring DJ and EDM performances and blasts from mud water cannons. At night, the excitement continues with a spectacular drone show over the sea and large-scale evening performances.
