In Boryeong, the fun lasts from day to night, making it the perfect place to create unforgettable summer memories.

title: Texture of Rest
overview: The Wooran Foundation's second textile exhibition offers fiber art as an answer to modern overload. Taking textiles' inherent qualities — connection and patience — as its medium, the show frames weaving as a way of re-threading a scattered self: not avoiding difficulty but passing through it toward genuine rest. A quiet, meditative stop in Seongsu-dong, Seoul's converted-warehouse art district.

title: K-Illustration Fair Busan
overview: The K-Illustration Fair takes place in BEXCO in Busan. The event exhibits illustration in a way that offers an inspiration to visitors' everyday life. It also acts as a platform where artists, consumers, and business partners can all connect, as well as showcase current trends in the illustration art industry.
place: BEXCO Exhibition Center 2, Halls A & B

title: Bonghwa Sweetfish Festival
overview: Catch your dinner in the Naeseongcheon: net-fishing and bare-hand sweetfish (eun-eo) catching in the clear shallows, ayu dishes to try afterward, water play, performances, and full summer amenities — Bonghwa's participatory eco-festival.

title: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival
titleFull: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival (정남진 장흥 물축제)
addr: 83, Chilgeoriyeyang-ro, Jangheung-eup, Jangheung-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival is one of Korea’s leading summer festivals. It has been named an Honorary Culture and Tourism Festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and selected as a Preliminary Global Festival. Set against the clean waters of the Tamjingang River and Jangheung Dam, the festival is packed with water-themed programs and continues to strengthen its presence on the global stage. Its signature event, the Salsu Battle Street Parade, turns the city streets into a giant splash zone where anyone can join in the fun. Other highlights include the World’s Largest Water Fight, Catch the Golden Fish, and a range of action-packed water activities. During the day, visitors can cool off with lively water games and activities. After sunset, the energy continues with K-pop concerts, Jangheung Water Beat, and other spectacular night performances. Programs such as the Papillon ZIP experience and Jangheung Camping Stay also invite visitors to enjoy the area’s nature, food, and local attractions. Open to visitors of all ages and backgrounds, the festival is a refreshing summer getaway where everyone can escape the everyday and dive into the fun.
place: Tamjingang River, Cypress Forest Woodland and Papillon Zip in Jangheung-gun

title: Andong Su (Water) Festa
overview: A summer water festival on the Nakdong riverbanks: giant water slides, pools, and paddleboard zones by day, then 'Andong Summer Night' concerts and fireworks after dark — with auto and tent camping so you can stay the night at the festival itself.

title: Dudu Summer Dong (Daegu Dong-gu Summer Festival)
overview: Dong-gu's answer to the 'Daefrica' heat on the Geumho riverside: water-bomb concerts, water survival games, dance contests, craft-beer pubs, and flea markets — young energy and river breezes at the Jijeo waterfront.

title: Saturday Permanent Stage Propose and Sacheon Rock Festival
titleFull: Saturday Permanent Stage Propose and Sacheon Rock Festival (토요상설무대 프러포즈 및 사천 락 페스티벌)
overview: This summer, a special music journey called the Saturday Permanent Stage Propose will be held in Sacheon at the maritime stage of Samcheongpo Bridge Park. Every Saturday evening, various genres of artists will come against the backdrop of the beautiful sea and sunset. It is a performance where you can enjoy a midsummer night’s show with the cool sea breeze and create unforgettable memories with family, friends, and loved ones. Additionally, participation in the national proposal event "To Reach You" is also possible, and special gifts can be received.

title: Geoje Summer Marine Festival
overview: A participatory ocean festival at Jisepo Port: a large water world with toddler pools, ocean-gun battles, a paper-boat 'shipyard' contest, yacht, kayak, and paddleboard sessions, plus a food festa, kids' playground, and an ocean horror parade — Geoje's shipbuilding-island summer at full tilt.

title: Balcony Music Show & Street Festa
overview: Gwangbok-ro's car-free street becomes a stage from July to December: fusion gugak, jazz, K-pop dance, tap, and popera on street spots — and the signature Balcony Music Show, performed from actual building balconies above the crowd, with sing-along parades and 60 Busan local brands.

title: Seongbuk Culture Vacance
overview: Seongbuk's 10th urban water-play festival: exciting slides and mom-and-baby pools at a schoolyard and the Uicheon stream plaza, with magic shows, K-pop dance, drumming performances, and water-gun and bubble programs. Seongbuk residents free; others 2,000 won.

title: Hongcheon Esports Festival
overview: A family gaming festival at Hongcheon's gymnasium: four-title amateur tournaments with a 20-million-won prize pool — Korea's biggest for amateurs — plus VR, drone, and game experience zones, cosplay, esports coaching, and career counseling.

title: Garden Night Market
overview: The Garden Night Market is a night market held in urban parks during the summer season. It consists of 10 sales booths, 5 experience booths, 10 food booths, and 16 food trucks, providing a variety of experiences for citizens and tourists. Play facilities and forest experiences are prepared for participants visiting with children, and colorful busking performances add to the ambiance of a summer night. Amidst the hot summer, the vibrant night market offers participants a fresh and unique experience as a nighttime themed tourist attraction.

title: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives
titleFull: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives (도기陶器, 우리를 담은 질그릇)
overview: Earthen Vessels: Stories of Our Lives is a special exhibition held at the National Gwangju Museum. By looking back at earthenware, a type of pottery which has been at the core of our daily lives for a long time, we can encounter the practicality, aesthetic sense, and the stories contained in the earthenware that has been passed down through tradition. This exhibition showcases over 300 artifacts, including a ribbed bottle and large jars excavated from the Cheonghaejin site in Wando.
place: National Gwangju Museum Main Building 1st Floor Special Exhibition Hall

title: Gyeongpo Summer Festival
overview: Seven days of beach life on Gyeongpo: giant claw-machine games and sand challenges by day, pine-grove picnic game zones, beer gardens on weekends, water-gun battles, and a different artist genre plus EDM party every single night.

title: KIMA WEEK Marine Leisure Festival
overview: Korea's flagship marine-leisure festival, running since 2013 at Dadaepo Beach: try-anything water sports sessions open to all, the KIMA Beach culture zone, family programs, and performances — the sea made approachable on Busan's sunset shore.
sponsor: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries · Busan

title: Andong National Heritage Night - Wolyeong Night Stroll
titleFull: Andong National Heritage Night - Wolyeong Night Stroll (안동 국가유산 야행 월영야행)
overview: The Andong National Heritage Night "Wolyeong Night Stroll" takes place around Woryeonggyo Bridge, offering visitors the opportunity to explore Andong’s national heritage while walking under the moonlight. The program is centered on storytelling inspired by the area’s cultural heritage and is held in the vicinity of Woryeonggyo Bridge. Visitors can engage with the historical value of Andong’s heritage through a variety of themed programs, including night views, guided routes, historical storytelling, performances, markets, food offerings, exhibitions, and lodging. These activities provide multiple ways to experience the cultural significance of Andong in an immersive nighttime setting.
sponsor: National Heritage Service, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Andong City

title: Sokcho Summer Festival
overview: Three days on Sokcho Beach: a retro arcade tournament ('Reply Arcade'), the Summer Splash water-run survival battle, dance crews and crowd grooving, then Beach Sound concerts and the Summer Night Electric DJ festival after dark — with free DIY crafts and a 14-team local food market.

title: Geomundo-Baekdo Silver Sea Festival
overview: On remote Geomundo island off Yeosu — gateway to the jagged Baekdo islets: cruise tours, traditional dragnet fishing, bare-hand fish catching, performances of the island's designated boat songs, a 'silver song contest', and fresh island seafood with sea-breeze mugwort to taste.

title: Incheon Pentaport Rock Festival
titleFull: Incheon Pentaport Rock Festival (인천펜타포트 락 페스티벌)
overview: The Incheon Pentaport Music Festival is one of Korea’s premier global music events and a major fixture in the country’s rock scene. Since its launch in 2006, it has grown into one of Korea’s flagship festivals, earning recognition from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The 2026 festival will be held at Songdo Moonlight Festival Park in Incheon, featuring headline performances by top Korean and international artists along with a wide range of high-quality festival programs. Beyond the main stages, programs such as Penta Super Rookie and Live Club Party support emerging artists and help energize the local music scene. Ahead of the festival, special pre-festival shows will take place in Hongdae and Tokyo, giving fans in Korea and abroad more ways to connect with Pentaport while building anticipation for the main event. Pop-up stores will offer official merchandise and branded content, adding another layer to the festival experience. At the crossroads of music and urban culture, the festival has become a global cultural platform and a signature event that raises Incheon’s profile as a city of culture.

title: Yeongju Cool Night Festa
overview: Yeongju's signature summer night market festival at the civic stadium: multi-genre stages, local food, atmospheric open-air drinking yards, and all-generation programs — a stay-late festival built to cool the old downtown's summer nights.

title: Night Race in Busan
overview: A night running festival over Gwangalli Beach and the Gwangan Bridge: the signature stretch runs the bridge's normally closed upper deck above the lit-up sea — music, photo zones, and festival energy over finishing times.

title: Illustar Fes 12
overview: A subculture fair at BEXCO with some 1,000 individual and team creators selling illustration books, goods, and albums of original and fan works, plus game companies from mobile to Nintendo and Steam, an indie-game hall, and the cosplay crowds and stage shows that fill the venue.

title: Hangang Festival
overview: Seoul's summer programme on the Han River, spread across the riverside parks. Events include a raft race in homemade boats to pick fruit hung over the water, all-night screenings of nostalgic summer dramas and horror films with late-night food, jazz and K-pop concerts, a drone show flying over the river surface, DJ sets and hip-hop at an infinity pool overlooking the skyline, and traditional tightrope walking staged at a swimming area. There is a cinema under a bridge, a water picnic with activities for families at Seoul Battleship Park, silent-disco DJ parties and yoga with headsets, an overnight Han River walk now in its tenth year, and paddleboards, kayaks, yachts and cruises on the water. Mostly free, with some programmes charged.
place: Mangwon Hangang Park, Seoul Battleship Park and other riverside sites

title: Hangang Night Walk 42K
overview: Walk the Han River all night: Korea's signature night-walking festival offers 42K, 22K, and 14K courses from Yeouido, prizing completion over competition — eleven years of walkers watching Seoul's river lights from dusk to sunrise.

title: Samgilpo Rockfish Festival
overview: The 20th rockfish festival at the pretty harbor of Samgilpo: traditional stone-weir fishing, platform angling, fry releases at sea, bare-hand conger catching in air pools — and free fresh rockfish sashimi from the festival committee, with spicy maeuntang all around.

title: EX Horror Season 6: Silla X Zombie
overview: A walk-through horror attraction staged after dark in the Hwarang Forest at Gyeongju Expo Park, along a 2 km woodland trail dressed with set pieces and live performers. It draws more than 15,000 visitors a year. The 2026 season sets zombies loose in Silla-era Gyeongju. Open to all ages, though the operator advises against it for anyone elderly or with a medical condition, and preschool children must be accompanied by an adult. Later and slightly cheaper on weekdays.
fee: Mon–Thu 10,000 won · Fri–Sun and holidays 12,000 won (discount for online booking)

title: Hongcheon River Starlight Music & Beer Festival
overview: 'Cool Music, Cold Beer!' — the 10th edition of Hongcheon's summer flagship: Terra draft straight from Korea's largest brewery (the HiteJinro Gangwon plant is local), Hongcheon craft brewers, a World Wet Dance contest, and EDM, rap, and hip-hop stages in the Tori Forest park.

title: Jeonju Gamaek Festival
overview: 'Drink today the beer made today': Jeonju's gamaek culture — cold beer with dried squid and snacks at corner shops — scaled into a festival, with same-day beer from the local HiteJinro plant, dishes from the city's certified gamaek joints, and summer-night stages. Entry 1,000 won.

title: Busan International Buddhism Expo
overview: Buddhism gone hip at BEXCO: 370 booths of temple food, meditation art and experience zones, traditional practice, and Buddhist crafts — this year playfully themed on the Heart Sutra's emptiness ('form is emptiness: the ball games you love'). Half price with advance booking.

title: LH Housing Gallery Culture Hideout
overview: LH's model-home galleries in Sejong, Incheon, Paju, and Namyangju turn their idle space into open cultural lounges: weekly one-day classes, local artists' stages, and cool indoor rest — an urban culture vacation without leaving town.
place: LH galleries in Sejong, Incheon, Paju, Namyangju

title: Seoul Fringe Festival
overview: Seoul Fringe Festival has been held every summer annually since 1998. The festival is open to artists of all genres, from dance to music and media art. Due to the open style and non-competitive element of the festival, artists and festival-goers alike are free to express themselves however they choose.
fee: Varies by program * Refer to the official website for details

title: 100 Years Night Night Market
titleFull: 100 Years Night Night Market (백년나이트 야시장 (메기의 귀환))
overview: 100 Year Market, a traditional market with a long history, transforms into a vibrant night market as evening falls. With a mini mirror ball, neon signs, and a mini DJ booth alongside new dining options each month, this retro-themed market is perfect for visitors of all ages.
sponsor: Ministry of SMEs and Startups, SEMAS, Seoul Metropolitan Government, Gangbuk-gu

title: Busan Sea Festival
overview: The Busan Sea Festival takes place at Dadaepo Beach and offers various cultural events and unique hands-on programs. All programs take place against the backdrop of the beautiful beach and sunset, and are carefully organized for a fun and lively event.
fee: Free (Fees may apply to certain programs)

title: Miryang Su-per Festival
overview: Water play, sport, and stages on the Miryang River: a big pool complex and water slides, water bikes and pedal boats on the river, 'super challenge' races anyone can join, and DJ and concert nights with food trucks along the banks.

title: Songdo Beach Festival
overview: An artificial white-sand beach and themed pools under Songdo's glass skyline: retro rides recalling the old Songdo amusement park, cultural stages, and food stalls — family water play by day, the district's famous night views by evening.

title: Hangang Bridge Cinema
overview: Open-air movies under the Han River bridges: Saturday nights at 20:00 for three weeks, free screenings beneath Wonhyo, Cheongdam, and Cheonho bridges — Seoul's coolest (literally) summer cinema, with citizen photo-contest winners on screen from 19:00.
place: Under Wonhyo Bridge, Yeouido Hangang Park (and 2 more)

title: Tongyeong Hansan Battle Festival
overview: The 65th Tongyeong Hansan Battle Festival is one of Korea’s leading patriotic history and cultural festivals, commemorating the victory at the Battle of Hansan, one of the three great naval victories of the Imjin War, and honoring the spirit and leadership of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Held throughout Tongyeong around the anniversary of the victory, on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month (August 14 in 2026), the festival features programs that bring this historic event to life, including a reenactment of the Battle of Hansan, the Parade of the Three Provinces Naval Commander, the departure ceremony, and a victory homecoming ceremony. Visitors of all ages can enjoy traditional cultural experiences, performances, exhibitions, marine leisure activities, media content, and nighttime programs. Set against Tongyeong’s beautiful coastline and rich historical heritage, the festival blends tradition and modern creativity while continuing to grow as a globally recognized festival of history and patriotic remembrance.
place: Tongyeong Hansan Battle Plaza and other locations across Tongyeong

title: Annotated Youth Concert: Summer Story
overview: The original commentary concert for young audiences, 23 years running and reliably sold out: a piano quartet plays the classical hits you know from films and ads, sorted by mood and moment, with the signature live commentary at Sejong Chamber Hall.

title: Yuseong On-Day
overview: A stay-and-relax program in Daejeon's Yuseong hot-spring district, built for slowing down rather than sightseeing. The lineup includes healing yoga classes combining aromatherapy and tea ceremony on the Kyeryong Spatel lawn, an open-air cinema with big screen and wireless headsets, small classical and film-music concerts in the front yard of Biryongjae — a former presidential villa — and an anytime running challenge along the Gapcheon stream. Participants get coupons usable at hotels, cafes, and bakeries in the hot-spring district. Schedules and sign-up at the official site (yu-on.com).
fee: See official website for program fees

title: Suwon Heritage Night
overview: Suwon Hwaseong — the UNESCO-listed fortress — after dark: eight night themes (views, roads, history, art, markets, food and more) light up Banghwasuryujeong pavilion, Hwahongmun gate, the Yongyeon pond, and Haenggung plaza with exhibitions, performances, and hands-on programs.

title: Heritage Media Art: Jinjuseong Fortress
overview: Jinjuseong was the site of one of the defining sieges of the Imjin War, where General Kim Si-min held the fortress against a far larger Japanese force in 1592. This event projects that history onto the walls themselves after dark — media facade projections, light and sound installations and interactive pieces across Gongbungmun and Chokseongmun gates, Chokseongnu Pavilion and the Yeongnam Pojeongsa government office, each keyed to what happened in that particular spot. Free, and it runs late: 19:30 to 22:30.
place: Jinjuseong Fortress and Jinju Daecheop History Park
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Gyeongsangnam-do · Jinju City

title: Dadaepo Sunset Film Festival
overview: Cinema against Busan's most famous sunset: a beach red carpet, opening and closing screenings on the sand, a national short-film competition, audience talks, concerts, and the 'Dadaepocha' food market — film and nature sharing one horizon.

title: Hongseong Heritage Night
overview: 'The walled town with a secret': Hongju-eupseong — seat of Joseon's Hongju magistracy and battleground of the righteous armies — opens at night with special lighting, history performances, heritage experiences, media content, and local food inside the old walls.

title: Gamtan Road Travel Gacha Pop-up
overview: A travel gacha arcade in Seongsu: pull capsule prizes to discover Taebaek, Samcheok, Yeongwol, and Jeongseon — Gangwon's former coal country reborn as travel destinations — with a photo gallery, quizzes on the mining-to-tourism story, and a black wall visitors fill with colorful messages.

title: Gaya Theme Park Light Festival
titleFull: Gaya Theme Park Light Festival (가야테마파크 빛 축제 빛을 향한 항해)
overview: The Gaya Theme Park Light Festival showcases the story of departure, navigation, and the encounter with Gaya through light sculptures, illuminations, media art, and photo zones. Walking along the path of light resembling the blue sea and night sky. On weekends and holidays, a local food zone, regional creator art market, and outdoor performances featuring jazz, fusion traditional music, and acoustic music will be added. Experience a special summer night in Gimhae where light, history, performances, food, and art come together.

title: Gangneung National Heritage Night
titleFull: Gangneung National Heritage Night (강릉 국가유산 야행)
overview: Gangneung National Heritage Night is a program selected by the Korea Heritage Service as a representative Korea heritage brand project. It promotes the active use of cultural heritage through a variety of activities such as performances, hands-on experiences, and art programs set in historically significant areas. The program encourages visitors to engage with and appreciate the meaning and value of cultural heritage, offering immersive nighttime experiences that highlight Gangneung’s history and culture through sights, food, and entertainment.
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service, Gangwon State, Gangneung City

title: BIC Festival (Busan Indie Connect)
overview: Korea's largest indie-game-only festival since 2015: 250+ indie games from around the world playable at BEXCO under the slogan 'Buff your Indie Spirit', with stage events, streaming content, and a three-week online festival alongside.

title: Dunnae Highland Tomato Festival
overview: Dive into a pool of tomatoes: the headline 'find the golden ring' hunt hides real gold rings and prizes in a tomato pool, alongside tomato stacking and weighing games, water slides, KBS's National Singing Contest, and highland-tomato tastings in cool Hoengseong.

title: Yeogijeogi Festival in Cheorwon
overview: Tourism startups test-drive their newest ideas on real travelers in DMZ-adjacent Cheorwon: AI and data-driven travel services, experiential content built on the county's nature and history, and a local flea market — a proof-of-concept festival where your feedback shapes the products.
sponsor: Ministry of SMEs and Startups · Gangwon · Cheorwon

title: Gyeongju Esports Festival
overview: Korea's biggest amateur gaming event meets a water park: the 18th President's Cup amateur esports finals, the national para-esports championship, and the Gyeongju Water Pool Festival with giant pools and water bounces — competitive gaming and summer splash in the ancient capital.

title: Samcheonpo Gizzard Shad Festival
overview: Autumn's famous fish, straight off the boats: Sacheon's 23rd jeoneo (gizzard shad) festival at the Palpo food district serves the oily, nutty seasonal catch — grilled whole or as sashimi — at the peak of its late-summer run, a nationally known food festival in a clean-water port.

title: K-Illustration Fair Magok
overview: The K-Illustration Fair Magok takes place at the COEX Magok Exhibition Center, showcasing the influence of illustration on people’s lifestyles in both everyday life and special occasions. The fair also highlights the powerful impact of illustrated works across both online and offline marketing, as well as their continued growth as an industry. Visitors can explore the latest trends in illustration and discover the diverse world of artists.
fee: On-site tickets: 10,000 won (Pre-registration 5,000 won / 2nd Pre-registration 7,000 won)

title: Busan International Comedy Festival
overview: Asia's first international comedy festival, launched 2013: top comedians from home and abroad play stages across the whole city, crossing generations and borders — K-comedy's flagship showcase, discovering new content and talent each summer.

title: Pohang Chimaek Festival
overview: Chicken and beer by the sea pavilion: two days at Yeongildae with chimaek sales zones, invited and citizen stages, EDM parties, a song contest, 'Chimaek Star K' and chimaek-king contests, water and art zones, and receipt lucky draws against the night sea.

title: Seocheon Hongwonhang Gizzard Shad and Blue Crab Festival
titleFull: 서천 홍원항 자연산 전어 꽃게 축제
overview: Late summer is gizzard shad season on Korea's west coast, and Hongwonhang — one of the larger fishing ports in Seocheon — builds a festival around it. Jeoneo is eaten grilled whole or raw as hoe, and is proverbially so fragrant in autumn that a runaway daughter-in-law would come home for it; blue crab, at its meatiest at the same time of year, shares the billing. Entry is free, with a bare-hands fish-catching event at 15,000 won, folk games, and photo spots along the harbour.

title: Mungyeong Saejae Bare-foot Walking Festival
titleFull: Mungyeong Saejae Bare-foot Walking Festival (오감만족 문경새재맨발페스티벌)
overview: Mungyeong Saejae Bare-foot Walking Festival, held annually in Mungyeong, is a bare-foot walking festival covering approx. 7 kilometers. The festival hosts a variety of programs, including the  main performance, various event booths, bare-foot-walking event, and a singing contest, allowing visitors to enjoy the festivities while keeping an eye on their health.
sponsor: Hankook Ilbo, Daegu Hankook Ilbo, mPLUS Korea

title: COSMOS BIGBANG 20TH ANNIVERSARY MEDIA EXHIBITION
overview: The COSMOS BIGBANG 20TH ANNIVERSARY MEDIA EXHIBITION is an exhibition that celebrates the 20th anniversary of the group BIGBANG’s debut by presenting their music and activities over the past 20 years through media art. With “COSMOS” as its theme, the exhibition uses content tailored to each space to embody the connections and continuity linking the past, present, and future. It is being held at Dududo Seoul, an underground space located between Seoul Station and Euljiro 1(il)-ga Station, and visitors enter sequentially according to their pre-booked time slots. The exhibition space consists of a media tunnel, sound visualization and listening zones, a media archive, an interactive art wall, a VR zone, and a hologram show. Utilizing digital technologies such as AI, XR/VR, holograms, and 3D motion graphics, the exhibition presents BIGBANG’s music and history through audiovisual content. It also features interactive content and message-based content that encourage visitor participation. The exhibition period is divided into PHASE 1 and PHASE 2, with changes to some VR and hologram content as well as purchase perks. The exhibition operates on a 100% advance reservation basis with 12 sessions per day, and an MD ZONE for visitors will be available on-site.

title: 5th Jeju Biennale: The Art of Transformation
titleFull: 2026 제5회 제주비엔날레 허끄곡 모닥치곡 이야홍 : 변용의 기술
overview: Jeju's civilization arrived by sea and from the northern mainland alike — scattering, gathering, and transforming into the island's present-day ecology and way of life. The 5th Jeju Biennale takes that dynamic as its subject, borrowing its key concept 'Iyahong' from the refrain of a folk song that itself drifted in from the mainland and became native. Anchored at the Jeju Museum of Art with satellite venues including the Jeju Stone Park's Obaekjanggun Gallery (free with a biennale ticket), it presents an aesthetics of survival shaped by nature, human life, and the sacred.
place: Jeju Museum of Art and satellite venues
fee: Adults 8,000 won · Youth 4,000 won · Children 2,000 won (satellite venues free)

title: Yeongyang Chili H.O.T Festival
overview: Korea's most famous chili county sets up on Seoul Plaza: the largest single-item direct farm market in the country, selling Yeongyang's prized gochu straight from growers, with culture programs, tastings, and exhibitions bridging farm and city.

title: Wonju Rooftop Film Festival
overview: Ten years of independent cinema on Wonju rooftops: a free, non-competitive summer-night festival planned by local youth, opening with a Gangwon short-film selection — programmed, staffed, and run by citizen-activists as true community cinema, this year atop the Korea Tourism Organization building.

title: Yanggu Baekbop Festival
overview: Yanggu sits at the exact geographical centre of the Korean peninsula, and has turned that fact into a festival: baekbop means navel. The 2026 theme is 'Navel Log-in'. It is built around water — hybrid water games and events designed for hot weather — with a street parade, fireworks, nightly concerts and a concert by soldiers from the units stationed in this border county. Free to enter, with some activities charged. Yanggu is close to the DMZ, about three hours from Seoul.

title: Jeonpo Saitgil Beer Festival
overview: Beer Road returns to the alleys of Jeonpo: DJ sets and bachata parties on the main stage, a standing beer-and-food lounge of drum-can tables and beer machines, and a mellow craft-beer lounge with floor seating and its own DJ — Busan's coolest cafe district after dark.

title: Creator Media Festival
overview: Korea's biggest creator-industry event at COEX Magok: a main stage streamed live on YouTube, fan meetings, live-commerce demos, AI and new-tech zones, platform talk shows, business matching, busking, DIY goods, and flea markets — 'the square where everyone's creation gathers'.

title: Saengsaeng Korean Music Festival
overview: Live and unplugged Korean traditional music in the small venues of Bongdam: artists selected from 120 national applicants play three days across ten neighborhood spots — little libraries, cafes, book shops, and a lake park — an award-winning grassroots gugak festival.

title: Yuseong Jazz & Beer Festa
overview: A summer festival that represents Yuseong, the Yuseong Jazz & Beer Festa is a classy cultural event that involves jazz music and craft beer. Attendees can taste quality craft beef from all over the country while enjoy live jazz performances.

title: Gochang Nongak Kkotdaerim Festival
overview: Gochang's designated farmers'-music tradition celebrates its harvest-blessing kkotdaerim rite: pungmul, gate, and pan gut performances at the nongak training center, with invited music and theater acts, participation programs, markets, and scholarly exchange — three days where players, scholars, and villagers share one yard.

title: Dongdaemun-gu Beer Festival
overview: A late-summer beer festival on the waterside at Jangan 1 Waterfront Park in eastern Seoul, held in the last week of August. Craft breweries and food trucks set up along the water, with jazz performances, outdoor film screenings and photo zones. Entry is free; drinks and food are paid for individually. It is a neighbourhood event rather than a tourist attraction, which is rather the point of going.
fee: Free entry (drinks and food charged separately)

title: Ganggyeong Heritage Night
overview: The old river-port town of Ganggyeong — once one of Joseon's three great markets — links its scattered modern-era heritage into one walkable night: landscape lighting and media art down the historic street, 30 programs across 8 night themes reinterpreting the town's trading-era stories.

title: Local Ground Yeonnam
overview: Yeonnam-dong's alleys as one festival: flea markets, busking, and events connecting the neighborhood's independent shops with the picnic culture of the Gyeongui Line Forest Park — wander, linger, and discover the backstreets behind Seoul's favorite stroll.

title: Jemulpo Wave Market
overview: Incheon's local brands in one harborside hall: this edition's theme is gastronomy, with 50 of the city's cafes and restaurants joining handmade candles, perfume, and craft stalls — plus blind tastings, lucky draws, craft workshops, and busking at the Sangsang Platform.

title: Ansan Esports Festival
overview: A city gaming day at the Kim Yeon-koung Gymnasium: League of Legends and Tales Runner tournament finals, cosplay performance contests, retro and Brawl Stars play zones, and meet-and-greets with gaming influencers and cosplayers — free for all ages.

title: Treasure Hunter in Jinan
overview: A county-wide treasure hunt across seven zones of Jinan, a mountain county in Jeonbuk best known for the twin peaks of Maisan. Buy a pass, then visit sites like Maisan's northern zone, Tapsa Temple with its stone pagodas, Yongdam Dam, Jucheon Eco Park, the highland arboretum, the Bugwi metasequoia road, and Suseonru Pavilion, completing QR missions in the LocalVibe app. Hidden 'dragon orbs' are revealed zone by zone each Saturday — find a regular orb for on-site rewards, or a shining one to enter the finals. A clever excuse to actually cover the county's best spots.
place: Maisan north zone, Tapsa Temple, Yongdam Dam and other sites
fee: Early bird 2,000 won · Pre-registration 4,000 won · On-site 5,000 won

title: Busan Night Walk 42K
overview: An overnight walking festival from APEC Naru Park: courses of 42K, 24K, 16K, and a new family 8K trace the Suyeong riverside and Oncheoncheon stream to Gwangalli Beach — crossing the newly opened Suyeong Human Bridge with Busan's night skyline for company.

title: Seocho Music & Art Festival (SMAF)
overview: The express-bus-terminal district becomes a culture plaza: Seocho's young summer festival stages a music-meets-fashion K-culture show in the Goter-Sebit tourism zone, with linked programs across the district — downtown Seoul's newest late-summer evening out.

title: Muan Red-Clay Mudflat Festival
overview: 'The mudflat is alive': an eco-festival on the UNESCO-listed Muan getbol — Korea's first protected wetland — at the Hwangto Mudflat Land, with its 1.5km over-sea boardwalk, tidal-flat ecology programs, exhibitions, and family activities on the living red-clay flats.

title: Semiwon Water Lily Festival
overview: Semiwon is a water garden at the point where the north and south branches of the Han River meet, with Paldang Lake on three sides — Gyeonggi-do's first designated provincial garden, laid out in the Korean traditional style. This autumn festival is built around its water lilies: the enormous Victoria amazonica whose leaves carry a child's weight, Australian species, and tropical varieties in every colour. The grounds also hold a lotus museum, a fountain built from onggi jars, and a replica of the pontoon bridge the Joseon scholar Jeong Yak-yong designed for King Jeongjo's procession. In 2026 it also hosts the Gyeonggi Garden Culture Expo. About an hour east of Seoul.

title: Nam-gu Youth Arts Festival
overview: Daegu's annual September showcase for young artists, returning with a two-part program: the small-venue 'Fringe FESTA' at the Daegu Music Creation Center (Sep 1–4) and the main-stage Youth Arts Festival at Daedeok Culture Center's Dream Hall (Sep 10–11). All seats are free, ages 5 and up. Alongside the performances, the 'ART CONNECT' exhibition brings together 104 young artists from regional art schools across painting, media, visual design, craft, and webtoons — free entry at Daedeok Culture Center galleries from Aug 18 to Sep 18 (closed Sundays).
place: Daedeok Culture Center and Daegu Music Creation Center

title: Cheonan K-Culture Expo
overview: The Cheonan K-Culture Expo is a K-culture–driven cultural industry fair held primarily at the Independence Hall of Korea, a landmark symbolizing Korea’s spirit of independence and national identity. Since its inaugural edition in 2023, the expo has been held annually for three consecutive years, integrating exhibition, performance, interactive, and consumer-oriented programs into a comprehensive cultural platform. Through ongoing collaboration with the Independence Hall, cultural and arts institutions, and regional industries, the expo continues to strengthen its operational stability while expanding its scale and scope.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Chungcheongnam-do, Cheonan City

title: Gyeongbokgung Palace Starlight Tour
overview: A guided night program through the quieter northern grounds of Gyeongbokgung, Seoul's main royal palace, combining history and royal cuisine. With a specialist guide you move through the palace after dark, then sit down in the former royal kitchen for a modern reinterpretation of the Joseon royal table — a 12-dish surasang served dosirak-style. This year adds a changgeuk (Korean opera) performance inside Jibokjae, King Gojong's private library, before the evening closes at Hyangwonji Pond under the stars. One of the most sought-after tickets among the palace night programs — book early.
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: Seoul Light DDP Autumn
overview: The world's largest media-art projection on a freeform facade returns to Dongdaemun Design Plaza for 11 nights, September 3–13. Under the season theme DAYBREAKER, the autumn edition 'K-Original Light' traces the original lights behind today's Korean culture: a first-ever live performance stage with real-time responsive media art built on Nam June Paik's philosophy, media-art reinterpretations of painter Yoo Youngkuk and the Korean alphabet, and a finale combining light, sound, and lasers across Zaha Hadid's curved walls. Free, nightly 19:30–22:30.

title: Jinju Heritage Night
overview: Jinjuseong Fortress and the old downtown by night, themed on the amhaengeosa (secret royal inspectors): eight night themes of views, performances, exhibitions, guided history walks, and night markets connecting the fortress's heritage with the city's living streets.

title: Waegwan Holy Festival
overview: Holiday in a holy place: Waegwan Abbey — Korea's Benedictine monastery with a medieval-European air — opens for light installations ('cathedral of light', 'dream forest'), Gregorian chant and pipe-organ concerts, talk shows with a young priest, monastery tours with monks, and monk's-habit photo booths.

title: Gangbuk Baengmaek Festival
overview: The Baengmaek Festival, which has grown into a representative event of Gangbuk-gu since 2023, aims to help transform Uicheon Stream into a permanent night market and a cultural space centered along the stream. In line with Seoul’s efforts to develop attractions near the stream, the festival highlights the area’s scenic waterfront as its main venue. Bringing together local businesses and young entrepreneurs, the festival creates a welcoming space for people of all ages. Rather than focusing on big-name performers, it features a variety of busking acts and performances by local artists, encouraging community participation. It also expands opportunities for small businesses by offering spaces for traditional market foods and craft beer, helping vendors reach new customers.
place: Baengnyeon Market and Uicheon Stream Area (Ssanghangyo Bridge to Uigyo Bridge) in Gangbuk-gu

title: Youth Culture Week
overview: 'Today's youth, today's culture': the culture ministry's youth festival takes over a Hongdae cafe with performances, talks, workshops, and community programs spanning arts, travel, sport, and lifestyle — young creators, planners, and brands showing what Korean youth culture is right now.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Gangwon Livestock Fair
overview: Korea's oldest livestock competition, running since 1968: Gangwon's farms present their finest hanwoo cattle for rigorous judging at the Gangneung Dano grounds, with premium-beef contests proving the province's breeding achievements — a farmers' gathering with real stakes.

title: Gongju Heritage Night
overview: Ten straight years of night heritage in the old royal capital: this year marks the centenary of the 1926 Gongju city map with the subtitle '1926 Gongju Romantic Banquet' — eight night themes around the old town hall, first church, and other modern-era heritage of the walking royal district.

title: Hyoseok Cultural Festival
overview: The Hyoseok Cultural Festival is one of Korea’s best-known fall cultural tourism festivals, held in Bongpyeong-myeon, Pyeongchang-gun, Gangwon-do. First held in 1999, the festival takes place around September every year in Bongpyeong-myeon, the real-life setting of When the Buckwheat Flowers Bloom, a classic modern Korean short story by Lee Hyo-seok (pen name: Gasan). The festival is best known for its vast fields of white buckwheat flowers, which bloom so densely that they look as if they have been dusted with salt. Visitors can experience firsthand the natural scenery of Bongpyeong that serves as the backdrop to the story. The program includes literary events honoring Lee Hyo-seok and his work, traditional folk games, a food market featuring local specialties, and a variety of cultural and artistic performances by local residents and artists. In doing so, the festival helps promote the region’s literary heritage and rural traditions while also supporting the local economy.

title: Upcycling Festival
overview: A circular-economy festival at the Seoul Upcycling Plaza: upcycled-goods markets, repair programs, hands-on upcycling workshops, exhibitions, performances, and picnic space — companies, creators, and citizens practicing resource circulation together, run as a low-waste event itself.

title: Hongseong Namdang Port Jumbo Shrimp Festival
titleFull: Hongseong Namdang Port Jumbo Shrimp Festival (홍성남당항 대하축제)
overview: Namdang Port, located at the west end of Hongseong, is a famous west coast port known for its exceptional seafood. Surrounded by the clean waters of Cheonsuman Bay, Namdang Port is home to a wide array of sea life including blue crab, cockle and webfoot octopus. Namdang Port also draws throngs of visitors from early September to mid-October every year for the country’s largest Jumbo Shrimp Festival.
fee: Free (Separate fees apply to food and experiences)
sponsor: Namdang Port Jumbo Shrimp Festival Committee

title: Jikji Culture Festival
overview: Celebrating Jikji — the world's oldest extant book printed with movable metal type, a UNESCO Memory of the World — on the anniversary of its listing: 'Jikji opens the door of time' brings exhibitions, printing experiences, performances, and lectures to Cheongju's Early Printing Museum quarter.
place: Cheongju Early Printing Museum and Arts Center

title: Rural Madang Theater Festival
overview: Open-yard madang theater brought to the countryside: begun as an arts festival for underserved rural audiences and now drawing city visitors too, its 22nd edition fills the restored Chojeong Haenggung palace with traditional performance, play, and shared laughter — free in the famous mineral-spring village.

title: Wonju Heritage Night
overview: 'Observing Wonju's history' at the Gangwon Gamyeong — the old provincial governor's compound — with the cathedral and colonial bank building alongside: eight night themes woven around three historical figures, from the righteous-army commander Min Geung-ho to the poet-governor Jeong Cheol.

title: Starry Sea Busan - Night Camp Picnic
titleFull: Starry Sea Busan - Night Camp Picnic (별바다부산 나이트 캠크닉)
overview:
Dadaepo Beach Park will transform into a festival full of emotions. The Starry Sea Busan - Night Camp Picnic is a special event that highlights the charm of Dadaepo, famous for its beautiful sunsets.

This event is not just about enjoyment; it is composed of various programs. Visitors can enjoy delicious food against the backdrop of a beautiful sunset, experience the camping vibe with live music under the starlight, create precious memories with pets, and take part in a wellness program to invigorate tired daily lives.
fee: [Live Performance] Adults 13,000 won / Children 5,000 won* Refer to website for details

title: Hwajeokyeon: A Thousand-Year Promise
overview: An open-air musical staged on the real scenery of Hwajeokyeon — the scenic-monument rock pool where Joseon rain rites were held: dramatic lighting on the natural stage, musical star Hong Ji-min with a cast of Pocheon citizens, two performances, all seats free.

title: Pohang 10 Flavors Night Market Festival
titleFull: Pohang 10 Flavors Night Market Festival (포항 10미 야장축제)
overview:
The Pohang 10 Taste Night Market Festival is an urban night food festival held in the area of Munduk Hello Military Street, linking Pohang's representative delicacies, the Pohang 10 Tastes, with local alley economies. It is aimed at revitalizing the local economy and promoting coexistence. Starting with an opening ceremony and celebratory performances, the festival will feature a variety of content that all generations can enjoy, including booths for Pohang 10 Taste and night market food, a food promotion hall, DJ club parties, a GOGO singing contest, a small business flea market, and a children's fire truck experience zone. It will be conducted as a clean festival using eco-friendly reusable containers, aiming to enhance the brand value of Pohang as a food city through specialized night market experiences that combine food, performances, and activities.

* Pohang 10 Taste: Mori Noodles, Pohang Mulhoe, Bluefin Sashimi, Guamegi, King Crab, Beef Head Soup, Pohang Chosanchae Bibimbap, Yeongildae Clam Grilled, Agutang, Haeshintang
place: Area of Ocheon Mundeok Hello Military Steet

title: Muju Firefly Festival
overview: The Muju Firefly Festival is one of Korea’s leading environmental festivals, themed around fireflies, a designated Natural Monument in Korea, and Muju’s pristine natural environment. Held throughout Muju-gun each year from around late August to early September, the festival offers visitors a special opportunity to see fireflies glowing in the wild and appreciate the value of nature and the importance of preserving the ecological environment. During the festival, visitors can enjoy a wide range of ecological and environmental activities, traditional cultural events, performances, and nighttime attractions. A signature highlight is the Firefly Mystery Exploration, Muju's unique program that takes visitors directly to firefly habitats to witness their magical glow in the wild. The experience leaves visitors with unforgettable memories. The Muju Firefly Festival has established itself as a celebration of the value of coexistence between people and nature, while raising awareness of the importance of environmental conservation.

title: Mungyeong Trot Song Contest
overview: Korea's beloved trot genre in full competition mode: finalists chosen from nationwide auditions battle it out at Mungyeong's riverside sports park, with star performances by Park Seo-jin and Kim Hee-jae, prize events, and fireworks to close the night.

title: House of the Upright Minister
overview: A family-friendly heritage program at the Chunghyeon Museum in Gwangmyeong, the head house of Yi Won-ik — one of Joseon's most celebrated 'clean officials', whose modest pavilion Gwangamdang was a gift from King Injo. The day mixes a participatory play about his life, mulberry natural-dye workshops, and a hanok exploration program for children, plus a free gayageum recital. Held four times: September 5 and 19, October 17, and November 7. Book via the official website; paid programs open Aug 10.
fee: Play 6,000 won · Hanok program 8,000 won · Natural dyeing 10,000 won · Combos 9,000–11,000 won · Gayageum recital free

title: 16th Gwangju Biennale: You Must Change Your Life
overview: Asia's most established contemporary art biennale opens September 5 under a title borrowed from the last line of Rilke's 1908 poem 'Archaic Torso of Apollo' — the moment a broken ancient statue upends how the viewer sees the world. The 16th edition builds on that jolt: when your vantage point shifts, you can no longer live as before. Held at the Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall, the event anchors Korea's contemporary art calendar and pairs well with the city's May 18 memorial sites and food scene.

title: Yesan Stork Festival
overview: An eco-festival in the village that brought storks back: Korea's reintroduced storks return here on strong homing instinct, and the 7th festival shares the village's habitat-restoration work through exhibitions and hands-on ecology programs at the Yesan Stork Park.

title: Hello Maker
overview: The National Busan Science Museum's 10th-anniversary maker festival: build ideas into real things at creation workshops for all ages, browse maker exhibits, and join the network of Korea's tinkerers — free entry, workshops from 3,000 won.

title: Chemistreet Gangnam Station Festival
overview: A commercial-district festival around Gangnam Station under Seoul's local-brand program: music, wellness, brand pop-ups, K-culture, and food across themed tracks (MIDNIGHT, LIFE, CHEMI, TASTE) running day into night, with district coupons and showcases.

title: Dalseong Family Festival YES! Kids Zone
overview: Dalseong's flagship children's festival at the National Daegu Science Museum: big balloon and bubble shows, comedy circus, magic and science-magic stages, hands-on booths from every district, and special appearances by kids' creators — a full family day, mostly free.

title: Car-Free Jamsugyo Bridge Walking Festival
overview: On festival Sundays, Seoul closes Jamsugyo — the low double-deck bridge that skims the Han River at Banpo — to traffic and hands it to pedestrians. Regular attractions include the Moonlight Diner (global street food), the Moonlight Market for crafts and eco goods, and riverside rest zones, while each edition adds rotating specials like the 'Jamsugyo Water Wars' water-gun battle and the reimagined 'Moonlight Jamsugyo'. Free, 14:00–22:00, with the Banpo Rainbow Fountain nearby — one of the most pleasant free evenings in the city.
place: Jamsugyo Bridge and Banpo Hangang Park

title: Seongbuk Book Festival (Chaekmokkoji)
overview: Seongbuk's library-network reading festival spreads along the Seongbukcheon stream: 18 teams — 13 district libraries plus universities and reading groups — run themed booths, an open-air library under the autumn sun, afternoon busking, and evening choir and folk-ensemble stages by the water.
place: Seongbukcheon stream by the district office

title: Heritage Media Art at Buyeo Jeongnimsa Temple Site
overview: For three weeks, the UNESCO-listed Jeongnimsa Temple Site in Buyeo — heart of the ancient Baekje capital of Sabi — becomes a night media-art park. Projections on the five-story stone pagoda and lecture hall, laser art, large-screen displays, AI-based interactive pieces, and kinetic sculpture draw on Sabi-era motifs: the Great Gilt-bronze Incense Burner, lotus-pattern roof tiles, Baekje astronomy, craft, and architecture. Nightly 19:00–22:00, September 7–27, free. A rare chance to see one of Korea's most austere heritage sites in a completely different register.

title: 2026 National e-Festival for Students with Disabilities
overview: A national esports and digital-skills festival for students with disabilities, co-hosted by the National Institute of Special Education, KOCCA, and the Netmarble Foundation under the theme 'A world opened by AI, boundless possibility'. Students selected through regional preliminaries in all 17 provinces compete in esports and IT contests, alongside AI and digital-technology experience programs, cultural performances, exhibition booths, and exchange programs at Sono Calm Vivaldi Park in Hongcheon.
sponsor: KOCCA · National Institute of Special Education · Netmarble Foundation

title: Bookshelf Concert: Sherlock Holmes
overview: Gyeonggi Arts Center's signature chamber-music series reads literature through music — and the 2026 edition takes on Sherlock Holmes. Mystery novelist Jeong Myeong-seop hosts, unpacking Conan Doyle, the stories' Victorian backdrop, and their behind-the-scenes history, while a chamber ensemble scores the moods and scenes of the canon. No prior reading required; for Holmes devotees it is a fresh angle on a familiar world. A 90-minute evening for mystery fans, classical newcomers, and families alike. Note the talk is in Korean.

title: Deoksugung Palace: Night at Seokjojeon Hall
overview: An evening at Seokjojeon, the neoclassical Western-style hall of the Korean Empire inside Deoksugung Palace. The program pairs a guided night tour of the hall with a terrace-cafe experience — coffee (gabae, the drink Emperor Gojong loved) and dessert over live classical music — and a musical performance telling the story of the imperial household. Running since 2021 and now a twice-yearly fixture, it closes with period-prop photos to take home. Around 100 minutes per session; tickets are limited and sell fast.
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: Gumi Local Food Festa in Seoul
overview: The city of Gumi brings its farm produce and G-Food brand to Seoul Plaza for a two-day showcase: sales booths direct from farms, a city promotion hall, an agri-food export fair, hands-on programs, and a produce auction visitors can join. A chance to browse regional Korean produce without leaving downtown Seoul.

title: 38th Chuncheon Puppet Festival
overview: Asia's largest puppet-theater festival, drawing top puppeteers and companies from around the world to Chuncheon. Centered on the Chuncheon Puppet Theater but spilling across the city, the program spans international performances, a large-scale parade, an art market, and workshops, exhibitions, and hands-on programs that push the boundaries of the genre. Long a fixture of the world puppetry circuit, it is genuinely all-ages — as rewarding for adults as for children. Fees and times vary by program.
place: Chuncheon Puppet Theater and citywide venues

title: 5th Horror Hologram Festival
overview: An immersive horror festival staged inside the Iksan Prison Set — the disused prison film set where many Korean movies were shot. The main event fuses hologram technology from Jeonbuk's hologram industry with escape-room mechanics and live theatrical scares, backed by stage events, quiz shows, and food stalls. Free entry, evenings 18:00–22:00 — a genuinely unusual venue even by horror-attraction standards, worth the detour for genre fans.
sponsor: Ministry of Science and ICT · Jeonbuk · Iksan City · NIPA

title: Red Food Festival
overview: Jangsu is known for producing some of Korea’s finest Hanu (Korean beef) and apples. Launched in 2007 with these two local specialties at its heart, the festival reaches its 20th edition in 2026, making a long and distinguished history. It also holds the distinction of being Korea’s first Red Color Festival. Since 2024, the festival has expanded its focus from Hanu and apples to a broader range of Jangsu Red Foods, including omija and tomatoes. It now also features a growing selection of processed specialties such as apple beer, apple soju, apple bread, and omija wine. Having evolved from Korea’s first Red Color Festival into the country’s first Red Food Festival, the event continues to expand its scope and enhance its standing as one of Korea’s leading cultural tourism festivals.
place: Uiam Park area, Jangsu-eup, Jangsu-gun, Jeonbuk-do
sponsor: Jangsu Red Food Festival Promotion Committee

title: Gwangju ACE Fair
addr: 30 Sangmunuri-ro, Seo-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: Held at the Kimdaejung Convention Center, the 2026 Gwangju ACE Fair is a comprehensive cultural content festival where broadcasting, animation, characters, games, and webtoons converge. This dynamic event serves as both a professional business hub for industry networking and a vibrant playground for the public. While domestic and international companies showcase the latest trends in the exhibition halls, visitors can enjoy a rich array of participatory programs, including an illustration fair featuring unique artist goods, lively cosplay competitions, and stage events with popular creators. The festival also offers family-friendly entertainment such as a dedicated board game zone and bubble shows, alongside creative markets like the Juicy Festival and Semogwi Market for exclusive character merchandise.
fee: Free with advance online booking* Refer to the official website for details
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Gwangju Metropolitan City

title: Sinchon Global University Culture Festival
overview: Sinchon — Seoul's classic university district — fills Yonsei-ro with a festival built on its two identities: global culture and student culture. University students plan and run much of the program themselves: global culture-experience booths, world food stalls, and student-culture booths line the street, while the main stage cycles through student performances, global acts, and participatory events. Free, 11:00–21:00, and one of the easiest places to feel Korean campus energy without an invitation.

title: Yongsan Heritage Night Walk
overview: For a few evenings each year Hyochang Park — an ordinary neighbourhood park in central Seoul most of the time — is lit and staged as a memorial to the Korean independence movement. Eight independence activists are buried here, including Kim Gu, and the programme builds around them: illuminated grounds, performances, exhibitions, guided commentary and hands-on activities. It runs into the night deliberately, so that the park reads differently than it does by day. Local schools, universities, veterans' associations and arts organisations each contribute their own programme rather than a single organiser producing everything.

title: Myeongnyang Daecheop Festival
overview: A history festival commemorating the Battle of Myeongnyang (1597), when Admiral Yi Sun-sin's 13 ships defeated a vastly larger Japanese fleet in the roaring strait of Uldolmok. Jointly held by Jindo and Haenam counties on both shores of the actual strait, the festival's centerpiece is a multimedia naval-battle reenactment blending ICT effects with a marine parade, plus a departure parade, regional performances, nightscape lighting, and hands-on history programs. One of the most dramatic settings of any Korean festival — the tidal current that won the battle still races under the Jindo Bridge.
place: Uldolmok Strait (Usuyeong, Haenam and Nokjin, Jindo)

title: Cheongsong White Porcelain Festival
overview: Cheongsong baekja — white porcelain fired here for 500 years from local clay, water, and fire — gets its own festival at the pottery village near Juwangsan National Park. Under the slogan '500 years of history, 500 years of future', the festival mixes exhibitions, sales, wheel-throwing and other hands-on programs, and cultural performances that trace the craft's past and hand it to the next generation. Free entry (some workshops paid), 10:00–19:00. Combine with Juwangsan's rock spires — this is one of Korea's quietest, prettiest counties.

title: Seoul International Writers' Festival
overview: Seoul International Writers' Festival was founded in 2006 with aims to lay a foundation for connecting Korean literature and international literature. The festival provides the opportunity to get a deeper understanding of literature through programs such as meeting Korean and international authors and participating in writers' workshop.

title: Daejeon Jung-gu Heritage Night Tour
overview: A night festival threading together the modern-era heritage of Daejeon's original downtown — the former Chungcheongnam-do Provincial Office, Daeheung-dong Cathedral, and other early-20th-century buildings — with light installations, storytelling, performances, hands-on programs, and a night market through the old alleys. The point is to walk, listen, and participate rather than just look, discovering a district where the city's past and present coexist. Free (some programs paid), 18:00–22:00.

title: Chuncheon Sul Festa
overview: Chuncheon's traditional-liquor and local-food festival, celebrating the city's brewing culture. Local breweries pour takju, distilled soju, yakju, fruit wines, and craft beer for tasting, with bottles sold at fair prices, while local food brands and food trucks supply pairings. A busking stage and hands-on programs round out the evening at KT&G Sangsangmadang Chuncheon. Free entry; drinks purchased on site. An easy add-on to a Chuncheon day trip from Seoul on the ITX line.

title: Muchangpo Mystic Sea Road Festival
overview: Twice a month, the tide at Muchangpo Beach pulls back to expose a 1.5km sea road — and this Boryeong festival is timed to it. By day, walk the tidal flats when the sea parts, catch fish bare-handed, and watch open-air madanggeuk theater; after dark, the signature LED torch walk sends a line of lights out across the exposed seabed. A rare festival where the main event is a natural phenomenon, with the schedule set by the tide tables. Free entry; some programs paid.

title: Geoje Beer Festival
overview: Geoje Island's signature autumn festival: unlimited draft beer against the night sea of Jangseungpo Port. The waterfront park fills with local food and food trucks, while the stage cycles through EDM, K-pop, and retro hits with audience events between sets. The festival also runs tourism booths, photo zones, local makgeolli tastings, a barrier-free zone, and reusable-container operations. Ticketed entry; evenings 18:00–22:00.

title: Gwangmyeong Madanggeuk Festival
overview: A performing-arts festival devoted to madanggeuk — Korea's open-air folk theater of satire, humor, and audience participation — co-hosted with the national madanggeuk association. Now in its third year, it turns the Gwangmyeong Civic Stadium grounds into an open stage for madanggeuk, fusion gugak, circus, and street performance, with citizen-participation programs alongside. The form's defining trait is that the line between stage and audience disappears — expect to be pulled in. Free, 16:00–21:00.
sponsor: Gwangmyeong Cultural Foundation · Korea Madanggeuk Association

title: Samto Festival
overview: Wonju's harvest-season celebration of farming and rural culture. A direct farm market sells the region's produce at source prices, family programs cover rural crafts and games, and local arts groups fill the stage across the day. Less a tourist spectacle than a genuine regional fair — which is exactly its charm if you want to see how a Korean provincial city celebrates its farming roots. Free, 10:00–21:00 at the Wonju sports complex.

title: Namdo K-Garden Festival
overview: A 51-day night garden festival in Yeosu's old downtown under the theme 'A Night Garden Embracing Islands'. Around 40 gardens — showcase gardens, designer gardens, and citizen-made plots — line the Yeomun culture street and Yeoseo plaza, viewable day and night with evening lighting that ties into Yeosu's night-tourism circuit. Garden-interpretation walks, performances, and hands-on programs run throughout, 15:00–21:00, free. Runs September 11 to October 31, overlapping the city's peak autumn season.

title: Moonlight Music Festival
overview: The Moonlight Music Festival is a cultural and arts performance series designed to let people enjoy music on autumn nights from September through October in familiar, everyday settings across Daejeon’s five districts. As an open-air event free to all citizens, it will feature a total of five performances—one in each district. Against the backdrop of cool autumn nights, local artists performing a variety of genres will take the stage, alongside performances by popular singers. By adding music to the familiar and comfortable parks and riversides in the city center, the Moonlight Music Festival aims to provide special moments and experiences where families, couples, and friends can enjoy music together and share the joy of live performances as part of their daily lives.
place: Areas of Gapcheon Ecological Lake Park, Eungubi Park, Urideul Park, Dongchundang Park, Daedongcheon Stream

title: Goyang Food and Beer Festival
overview: Goyang's food-and-drink festival, now in its seventh year, held along the pedestrian street of La Festa in Ilsan. Craft beer and food stalls run alongside live music and hands-on activities, with a dedicated food-truck zone and beer zone. It is a city-centre street festival rather than a destination event — easy to reach from Seoul on Subway Line 3, and free to enter, with food and drink paid for individually.
fee: Free entry (food and drink charged separately)

title: Dalseong Daegu Contemporary Art Festival
overview: An open-air contemporary art festival at Gangjeong, by the sculptural ARC building on the Nakdong River. It inherits the spirit of the 1970s Daegu Contemporary Art Festival, when young artists challenged the rigidity of the art establishment — the 1977 edition at this very riverside drew some 200 artists in what is considered Korea's first collective art event. Free, open 11:00–22:00, and easy to combine with a riverside bike ride out of Daegu.

title: GXG 2026
overview: Korea's largest urban game-culture festival, held in Pangyo — the Silicon Valley of the Korean game industry. GXG (Game culture X Generation) treats games as culture rather than just play: the main program is GXG SOUND TRACK, a game-music competition, surrounded by concerts, exhibitions, and experience zones covering game music, video, and art. Free, on the plaza around Pangyo Station, 13:00–22:00 — an easy subway ride from Gangnam and a good window into Korean gaming culture.

title: Seocheon Heritage Night Tour
overview: A two-night heritage festival at Hansan Eupseong Fortress in Seocheon, themed 'The Lord of Hansan's Rowdy Incognito Outing'. The old fortress town — home of Korea's famous Hansan ramie fabric — hosts night performances, hands-on programs, and exhibitions that blend tradition with contemporary staging, September 11–12, 18:00–22:00, free. Part of Korea's national 'Heritage Night' series, which opens heritage sites after dark with food, light, and stories.

title: Michuhol Media Culture Festival
overview: Incheon's community media festival, running since 2004: VR and AR trials, one-person broadcasting workshops, photo and video editing, plus local performances, an art flea market, and kids' zones around the media center.
place: Incheon National University Jemulpo Campus plaza

title: Pyeongtaek Lake Light Festival
overview: Pyeongtaek's signature festival on the shores of Pyeongtaek Lake, built around the twin themes of water and light. The day runs family performances, hands-on programs, and food zones through the lakeside tourist complex; after dark the sky fills with the festival's headline fireworks show over the water. Local residents and artists carry much of the stage program, making it a friendly, low-key alternative to the megafestivals. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Daejeon Jung-gu Book Festival
titleFull: Daejeon Jung-gu Book Festival (대전 중구 북페스티벌)
overview: The Jung-gu Book Festival builds on the diverse reading cultures and voices discovered within Jung-gu, bringing them together to foster new connections throughout the district. Presenting the district as a place shaped by layers of stories accumulated over time, the festival traces the time embedded in its alleys, the memories preserved in the old downtown, the lives of its people, and the emotions held by the community. In doing so, it uncovers and connects the stories that already exist within Jung-gu in a different perspective.
fee: Free admission (certain programs may require a participation fee of 1,000 won to 5,000 won)

title: Pocheon Hantangang Garden Festa
overview: A large-scale garden-and-ecology festival at the Hantangang Eco Landscape Complex, inside the UNESCO Global Geopark of the Hantan River gorge. Seasonal flower fields spread beneath the park's 410m Y-shaped suspension bridge, with themed designer gardens, a Pororo-themed autumn camping photo zone, a river market of Pocheon farm produce and street food, and family e-bike rides along the gorge. Ticketed entry, 09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00). The geology alone — basalt cliffs carved by ancient lava — is worth the trip from Seoul.

title: Wonju Book Festival 2026: Books Met in the Street
overview: A weekend reading festival that deliberately spills out of the library and into the city — small neighbourhood libraries, independent bookshops and open-air reading rooms across Wonju. The programme includes talks by Korean authors Ye So-yeon, Baek Yu-yeon and Kim Geun-hee, a staged reading for children, and outdoor performances and workshops. Almost everything is in Korean, so the draw for a foreign visitor is the outdoor reading rooms and the atmosphere rather than the talks.

title: Wanju Sanggwan Water Pool Party
overview: A stay-style festival in Sanggwan, a valley township of Wanju county, linking its water, forests, hot springs, lodging, and food into one program. The daytime pool party and evening night market anchor the schedule, joined by cypress-forest activities ('Forest-tivity'), village and forest trekking walks, and lodging-linked stay packages. Free entry; the pool party and some programs are ticketed. Runs 10:00–22:00 at the Boem Spa & Resort area — an easy pairing with Jeonju, twenty minutes away.
fee: Free entry (pool party and some programs paid)
sponsor: Wanju County · Wanju Culture and Tourism Foundation

title: Glocal Culture in Namsan Festival
overview: A one-day neighborhood festival in Busan's Geumjeong district where global and local culture meet — powered by the international students of Busan University of Foreign Studies and the residents of Namsan-dong. The glocal food market serves fermented dishes made by the community fermentation school alongside local staples, with a flea market of local sellers and an evening citizens' concert. Namsan-ro becomes a cultural street for the day, 15:00–22:00, free.

title: Nowon Craft Beer Festival
overview: Thirty-four breweries from across Korea pour some 200 craft beers along the Gyeongchun Line Forest Trail at Hwarangdae Railroad Park — a disused rail line turned linear park in northeast Seoul. Traditional-market vendors and food trucks handle the pairings, while the stage hosts Korean and international acts in tandem with Seoul Music Week, plus experimental student art and children's programs. Free entry; pay per pour. One of the city's best-value beer events, in an unusually atmospheric venue.

title: Paju K-Culture Festival
overview: A K-culture festival at the former Paju English Village — now a shooting location for K-pop survival shows, music videos, and K-dramas. The program brings K-pop and cover-dance performances together with K-food, traditional Korean games, and around 30 hands-on K-culture booths, plus four-cut photo studios, stamp events, and traditional costume try-ons. Free, 10:00–17:00. For K-content fans, the venue itself — a purpose-built European-style village an hour from Seoul — is half the draw.
place: Gyeonggi Future Education Paju Campus (former Paju English Village)

title: 2026 DMZ Peace Festa
overview: A relay festival linking the tourism assets of the DMZ border region, long split between separate counties, into one program — this edition connecting Ganghwa Island and Cheorwon. Both legs build hands-on programs around three shared themes: nature and ecology, the lives and stories of border residents, and reflection and healing. Venues include the Hwagae Garden on Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and the history park in Cheorwon. Free; some programs need advance booking via the official site.
place: Hwagae Garden, Gyodong Island (Ganghwa) and History Park (Cheorwon)
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

title: Seoul Intangible Heritage Festival
overview: Seoul's intangible-heritage traditions gather in Namsangol Hanok Village for a weekend of performances, exhibitions, demonstrations, and tastings, organized into five themed courtyards: a spirited performance stage, a craft court where master artisans work within arm's reach, a taste court of traditional food and drink, an open participation court, and a heritage-collecting trail. Set among the village's relocated hanok houses under Namsan, it is one of the best-value traditional culture days in the city. Free (some programs paid).

title: Jeju Leisure Healing Festival
overview: Two days of leisure sports and wellness on Hamdeok Beach, one of Jeju's most beautiful white-sand bays. Headline concerts each evening (past lineups have drawn major Korean acts) bookend a daytime program of paddleboarding, flying disc, and trail running, balanced by wellness content: morning yoga on the sand, stargazing nights, and sketch-drawing sessions overlooking the water. Opens with a beach party performance and closes with a water-splash finale. Free, 07:00–22:00.

title: Yangju Heritage Night Tour
overview: The old government seat of Yangju-mok comes alive after dark under the theme 'Officials and people rejoicing together again'. The festival stages Yangju's remarkable roster of intangible heritage — the Byeolsandae mask dance, Sonori shamanic ox play, farming songs, and funeral bier songs — alongside a state-exam reenactment, traditional crafts, night walks, media exhibitions, and an old-style market with teahouse. Programs follow the classic '8 nights' structure of Korea's Heritage Night series (night views, night roads, night stories and more). Free, 17:00–22:00.

title: Cheoinseong Fortress Culture Festival
overview: In 1232, at the small earthen fortress of Cheoinseong, the monk-commander Kim Yun-hu and local villagers repelled the second Mongol invasion — killing the Mongol general Sartai in one of the great upsets of the era. Yongin's 35th festival in their honor stages a musical of the battle, mounted martial-arts shows, horseback riding, Goryeo costume try-ons, pottery and craft workshops, and guided history walks, closing with night performances and fireworks. Free entry, 10:00–22:00, with food trucks on site. A linked mission event connects it to October's Poeun Culture Festival.

title: Colorful Garden: Jaraseom Flower Festa
overview: Autumn flower fields blanket Jaraseom — the river island in Gapyeong best known for its jazz festival — from September 12 to October 5. Weekends add busking and local performances, plus balloon art and family programs, farm-produce booths, and snack stalls. Of the 7,000 won ticket, 5,000 won comes back as local currency to spend at booths and in town cafes and restaurants. Boats cruise the Bukhangang riverfront and an electric shuttle covers the walk in. Ticket holders get discounts at nearby attractions; Gapyeong residents enter free.
fee: 7,000 won (5,000 won returned as local currency)

title: Dongdaemun-gu Book Festival
overview: A reading festival for Korea's September 'Month of Reading', themed 'Open the book, move the body!'. The plaza at the Dongdaemun-gu Office hosts reading fitness sessions, folk tales turned into physical games, and an open-air library, while the auditorium runs library-network booths from a reading adventure squad to a mini sports day and a 'reading health check'. Children's musicals, a bubble show, and busking round it out. Free, aimed squarely at families, 12:00–17:00.
place: Dongdaemun-gu Office Future Plaza and auditorium

title: Seoro Market: Chuseok Edition
overview: A direct-from-the-farm market in Seoul Plaza in the run-up to Chuseok, where producers from across the country sell the ingredients people buy for the holiday. Beyond the stalls it runs as a cultural event: a hundred-cook Chuseok table demonstration with master artisans, a traditional mill where you can watch grain being pressed, a moonlight photo zone with hanbok, folk games, and a persimmon-tree capsule event. There is a parcel desk on site so you can ship what you buy rather than carry it. Free to enter, in the plaza outside Seoul City Hall.

title: Seoul Architecture Festival
overview:
The Architecture Festival aims to rediscover the unique architectural and urban charms of Seoul together with its citizens. Seoul generates creative potential based on “complex density”—a fusion of history, culture, and regional identity characteristic of a high-density city. Furthermore, amid rapid social change, the city has continuously adapted through “accelerated evolution,” which involves rapidly renewing its form based on its accumulated heritage. Moreover, through “glocality”—the intersection of local context and global trends—Seoul is expanding the unique urban experiences and values of contemporary K-architecture to the world.
The festival features a variety of participatory programs designed to allow citizens to experience Seoul’s architecture and urban landscape up close and engage with architectural culture in an accessible way. Through a diverse range of citizen-participatory content, the festival aims to create a space where citizens can discover Seoul’s architecture together and help shape K-Architecture culture.
place: Seoul Urban Architecture Exhibition Hall, B3, Bium Hall

title: 14th Busan International Port Conference
overview: The annual international conference of Busan Port — one of the world's busiest container hubs — gathering global port, shipping, and logistics leaders to share container-market outlooks and operating strategy. The 2026 agenda centers on the industry's defining shifts: digital transformation, decarbonization, and supply-chain realignment. Held at the Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center; free registration, with session times to be announced. An industry event rather than a festival — of interest mainly to maritime professionals.
place: Busan Port International Exhibition & Convention Center

title: Hampyeong Moaksan Red Spider Lily Festival
overview: In mid-September the woodland floor around Yongcheonsa Temple turns solid red as hundreds of thousands of spider lilies flower at once — leafless scarlet blooms on bare stems, a plant long associated with Buddhist temple grounds in Korea. The 27th edition leans towards quiet rather than spectacle: forest-therapy and meditation programmes along the Moaksan trails, walking routes through the flowering colonies, and local food. Free to enter. The bloom is short and weather-dependent, so check timing before travelling.

title: Literature Week 2026: Sideways Glance
overview: Korea's national literature festival, held every year since 2016 to widen the audience for Korean writing. The 2026 edition, themed 'Sideways Glance', looks at literature and everything just outside it, over five days of readings, talks, and programs around Marronnier Park in Daehangno — Seoul's theater district. Free; program times vary. Most events are in Korean, but the park itself buzzes for the week.

title: Korea National Contemporary Dance Company: Site and Fold — Yeongwol
overview: A mixed-reality dance performance by choreographer Song Ju-won, staged in a former mining-country gallery in Yeongwol. The work is built around mourning what has disappeared or is disappearing — human and non-human alike — and the audience moves through it wearing augmented- and virtual-reality equipment, becoming participants rather than spectators. Because the piece is largely movement and image rather than text, the language barrier is low. Admission is free, an open rehearsal runs at 19:00, and the last performance each day is followed by a talk with the artists.

title: 9th Jeonju International Short Film Festival
overview: A short-film festival in Jeonju's cinema street under the slogan 'New Frame, New Longtake' — this year expanding into vertical films shot for the phone screen while doubling down on short-form experimentation. The program combines screenings, audience talks with filmmakers, and a vertical-cinema forum at CGV Jeonju Gosa, in the heart of the city famous for its hanok village and food.

title: 8th Daejeon Special Visual Effects Film Festival
