overview: Korea's only film festival dedicated to VFX and special visual effects, built on Daejeon's visual-effects industry base. The program spans the DFX OTT Awards honoring effects work in Korean streaming content, DFX Screenings with director and cast talks, a DFX Tech Show on AI and VFX production trends, and DFX Pitch, which scouts feature-length effects-driven projects. Screenings spread across the DCC convention center and the city's independent cinemas. Free.
place: DCC Exhibition Hall 2 and cinemas across Daejeon

title: Eumseong Masterpiece Festival
overview: A farm-produce festival in Eumseong County, Chungbuk, showcasing and selling the region's agricultural goods and specialties. Expect produce exhibitions and direct sales, food booths, hands-on programs using local crops, and cultural performances — with growers and shoppers meeting face to face. A straightforward, local-flavored county fair rather than a tourist production.

title: 39th Donghae Mureung Festival
overview: Donghae's flagship traditional festival, four days at the Wellbeing Leports Town under the theme 'Citizens as one, Donghae leaping anew'. It opens with mountain-spirit and harvest rites, then runs generation-spanning concerts, a citizens' song contest, youth dance festival, navy band and honor-guard shows, special-forces martial-arts demonstrations, and folk performances including Mangsang nongak and the local bridge-treading play. Family zones cover folk games, craft workshops, and children's programs; a local-restaurant tasting vote and lantern-lit night tunnel round out the grounds. Free.

title: 2026 Gyeongbuk K-Story Festival
overview: A content-industry festival in Andong themed 'K-Story, where content begins', connecting the region's history and its creators' stories to webtoons, video, performance, and publishing. The program spans story-IP pitching sessions that link creators with buyers, keynote lectures and conferences, family experience zones, and exhibitions and performances at the Andong Culture & Arts Center. Free, 11:00–20:00 — and Andong itself, Korea's Confucian heartland and home of Hahoe Village, rewards the trip.

title: Gyeonggi Ceramics Biennale
overview: The Gyeonggi Ceramics Biennale features a range of exhibitions and educational events. The event takes place at various locations in Korea famous for ceramics, including Icheon, Yeoju, and Gwangju.
place: Area around Cerapia in Icheon, Gyeonggi-do / Gonjiam Ceramic Park In Gwangju Gyeonggi-do / Yeoju Dojasesang (Yeoju Ceramics Village) in Yeoju, Gyeonggi-d
fee: Combination ticket: On-site 11,000 won (Discount price 7,000) * Free admission for children under 6 years old and senior citizens over 65 years old

title: Yeonggwang Bulgapsan Red Spider Lily Festival
overview: Every September, millions of crimson spider lilies (sangsahwa) carpet the valley below Bulgapsa, a thousand-year-old temple on Bulgapsan Mountain. The 26th festival threads performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs along the flower paths, with soft night lighting turning the fields into a second, quieter spectacle after dark. The flower — whose leaves and blossoms never meet — symbolizes impossible love, giving the walk its bittersweet undertone. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Gamaksan Flower & Star Journey
overview: On the summit hill of Gamaksan in Geochang — the 'Star Wind Hill' — autumn wildflower fields bloom against one of southern Korea's best night skies. The sixth festival, themed 'a purple comma just for me', runs busking and sunset-hill concerts, a chrysanthemum-field walk, photo zones, a stamp tour, and a slow mailbox that delivers your letter before next year's festival. Local food tents serve bibimbap, gukbap, and jeon at village prices. Access by shuttle bus (3,000 won) or pre-booked private car.

title: Korea Youth Day Festival
overview: The 10th anniversary edition of Korea's official Youth Day festival, held on Gwangalli Beach in Busan. What began as an advocacy event became a legal commemoration day (third Saturday of September) in 2020, and the festival now spans youth policy, culture, careers, and entertainment: a K-pop concert, a college song contest, gala concert, youth film awards, the Korea cheerleading championship, and creator awards, all against the Gwangan Bridge backdrop. Free, 10:00–21:00.

title: Suseongmot Festival
overview: Daegu's lakeside arts festival at Suseongmot, the city's favorite evening hangout — twice ranked the city's best regional festival. The program floats between land and water: K-arts fantasy stages of Korean orchestral music, song, and dance, an on-the-water concert and 'wave' dance performance, street arts, a citywide youth dance competition, school music showcases, and an intangible-heritage stage. Music fireworks shows bookend the festival. Free, 13:00–22:00.

title: Anyang Dance Festival
overview: Anyang's citizen festival since 2000, drawing some 300,000 visitors a year and now one of Gyeonggi Province's flagship events. Under the slogan 'Walk, run, dance!', it treats any free movement of the body as dance, filling Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park with citizen performance teams, professional stages, and open dance floors over three days. Billed as Korea's only regional K-dance festival — and defiantly participatory: you will be invited to join.
place: Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park

title: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food Festival
overview: A festival built around Pyeongchang Dunjeonpyeong nongak — the region's designated intangible-heritage farmers' music — in the highland township of Yongpyeong. The drumming and dance performances anchor a thoroughly edible program: pot-barbecue and skewer grilling, market-style gukbap stew, and other mountain-village food, plus folk games, madanggeuk theater, and hands-on traditions. Free entry (food paid), 10:00–20:00. As unpretentious and warm as festivals get.
place: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food festival grounds

title: Busan Youth Week
overview: A three-day festival on Busan's Pier 1 marking Korea's Youth Day, programmed by young directors from the city under the theme 'The Faces of Busan'. The staging is immersive rather than a conventional stage-and-audience format, and the setting — a working port pier in the old town, close to Jagalchi and BIFF Square — is part of the appeal. Free, and open to anyone, not only Busan residents. Programmes are in Korean.

title: Aragaya Culture Festival
overview: Haman's festival of Aragaya — the ancient Gaya confederacy kingdom whose royal tombs crown the UNESCO-listed Marisan mounds. Reenactments bring the kingdom to life: a royal procession, gate-guard changing ceremony, and mounted-warrior experiences, alongside history trails, youth-produced performances, and a fireworks-backed theme show, 'Ara Red Lotus'. Held at the Haman Museum and tomb park, 09:00–21:00, free — one of the best windows into Korea's less-told Gaya history.

title: Jinan Red Ginseng Festival
overview:
Held in Jinan-gun, Korea’s only designated red ginseng special zone, the Jinan Red Ginseng Festival is a signature fall event where visitors can enjoy both healthy local specialties and festive fun. Jinan red ginseng, known for its rich aroma and high quality, can be sampled throughout the festival, alongside a variety of unique foods and hands-on activities that make red ginseng more approachable and enjoyable for visitors of all ages.
 Highlights include Red Ginseng Bingo, Red Ginseng Power Zone, Red Ginseng Barbecue, and an Outdoor Foot Bath Experience, as well as plenty of unique interactive programs found only at the festival. Traditional performances, guest singer concerts, and a variety of stage events add to the lively atmosphere. Visitors can also shop for Jinan red ginseng products certified under strict quality standards at reasonable prices. With healthy local foods, unique experiences, and plenty of entertainment, the festival offers a memorable way to enjoy fall in Jinan.

title: Seoul Autumn Festa Opening
overview: The opening night of Seoul Autumn Festa — the city's 73-day performing-arts season running September 18 to November 29, when roughly 260 theater, dance, music, and traditional-arts productions play across the city. The kickoff concert at the Ttukseom Hangang Park riverside stage doubles as Seoul's declaration of itself as a performing-arts city. Free, 19:00–21:00, on the river as the season's first cool evenings arrive.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government · Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Siheung Gaetgol Festival
overview: The Siheung Gaetgol Festival is an eco-festival held at Siheung Gaetgol Eco Park, the only inland tidal creek in Gyeonggi-do. Surrounded by wetlands and former salt fields, the festival offers a variety of ways to relax, learn, and have fun in nature. To help protect the park’s natural environment, it is held as a car-free event. A signature program is the salt-pan performance, "Memories of Salt, Dance of Water." Other performances include Concert in Gaetgol, Salt Warehouse Puppet Theater, Forest Music Festival, and the Gaetgol Senior Runway. Visitors can also enjoy a wide range of activities, including a Fantasy Hot-Air Balloon Experience, Gaetgol Adventure, Salt Play & Barefoot Salt Trail, SEA POOL Party, Insect Exploration Experience, Gaetgol Is My Playground for the Day, Salt Farm Experience, Slow Post Office, “Walk Siheung” Walking Festival, Siheung Salt Farm Ritual, Street Arts Festival, Gaetgol National Art Competition, Gaetgol Retro Photo Studio, and the Gaetgol Stamp Rally.

title: 11th Ulju Mountain Film Festival
overview: Asia's leading mountain-film festival, set at the welcome center of the Yeongnam Alps — the ridge country above Ulsan. The program spotlights how humans live with nature: trial and triumph, challenge and failure, conflict and coexistence, through international mountain films and documentaries that stretch the genre's boundaries. True to its setting, screenings include open-air bivouac and car-camping sessions running to midnight. Individual screenings 3,000 won; day pass 12,000 won.
fee: Screenings 3,000 won · Day ticket 12,000 won · UMFF pass 15,000 won · Bivouac screening 10,000 won

title: Gwacheon Performing Arts Festival (GPAF)
overview: Korea's first street-theater festival, running since 1997 and now drawing over 100,000 visitors each September. International and Korean companies stage outdoor and street productions across the plazas of Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, in a program mixing invited international works, Korean premieres, and commissioned pieces. Free and deliberately accessible — this is where Korean street theater made its name. 12:00–22:00.
place: Gwacheon Government Complex plaza and Citizens Hall area

title: Bucheon International Comics Festival
overview: Celebrating its 29th edition in 2026, the Bucheon International Comics Festival (BICOF) is one of Korea’s leading cultural tourism festivals devoted to comics and webtoons, offering something for everyone who loves the medium. This year’s festival, held under the theme “Comics & Webtoons: Easy to Love, Endless to Enjoy,” features a wide range of comic-related programs and cultural experiences designed to make the event more engaging and enjoyable for visitors. Highlights include curated and special exhibitions, meet-the-artist sessions for comics fans, the BICOF Playground and outdoor market booths offering a variety of hands-on experiences, and the International Cosplay Championship, which brings together cosplayers from 14 countries around the world.
place: Korea Manhwa Museum and Korea Manhwa Contents Agency area

title: Gyeongju Heritage Night Walk
overview: Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years, and this event opens its monuments after dark. The 2026 edition is subtitled 'Fragments — What We Have Kept, and What We Will Keep', and spreads across Woljeonggyo Bridge, Gyerim Forest, Gyochon Hanok Village and Gyeongju Eupseong Fortress. Expect illuminated architecture, performances and hands-on programmes at each site. Most of it is free; a few individual programmes charge. For a visitor this is the easiest way to see Gyeongju's heritage sites lit at night, when they are markedly less crowded than by day.
place: Woljeonggyo Bridge, Gyochon Hanok Village, Cheomseongdae and Gyeongju Eupseong Fortress
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Gyeongsangbuk-do · Gyeongju City

title: 67th Korean Folk Arts Festival
overview: Korea's longest-running festival, held since 1958 to preserve and pass on regional folk performing arts — the event that historically surfaced many of the country's now-designated heritage traditions. The 67th edition gathers folk troupes from every province in Pyeongchang, the 2018 Winter Olympics host, for open-air performances at the Jinbu sports park. Free, 09:00–18:00: two days of farmers' music, mask dance, ritual, and song you will rarely see assembled in one place.
sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gangwon · Pyeongchang

title: Geumcheon Science Festival (G-Science Festival)
overview: A district science festival for some 9,000 students and residents: motion simulators, an escape-room bus, robot dogs and humanoid robots, AI piano and AI-vs-human showdowns, 3D pens, science magic and bubble shows, and a coding hackathon across five zones around the district office.

title: Peace Nuri Picnic Festival
overview: An autumn picnic-and-concert festival on the great lawns of Imjingak Pyeonghwa Nuri (Peace Park) near the DMZ in Paju. Spread a mat under open sky for the Peace special stage and live sets by popular Korean artists spanning generations — daytime picnicking rolling into evening concerts. Entry is a token 3,000 won. The venue itself, wind-turbine hills within sight of the border, is among Korea's most evocative concert settings.

title: Ocean Village
overview: A local market event on the Jangseungpo waterfront in Geoje, gathering the island's fresh farm and sea produce, small-batch foods from local makers, lifestyle goods, family items, street food, and hands-on programs in one strollable seaside venue. Runs Friday–Saturday 11:00–20:00 and Sunday to 18:00. A good graze-and-browse stop if you are touring Geoje's coast.

title: Namhansanseong Culture Festival
overview: Three days marking the 400th anniversary of the fortress walls of Namhansanseong — the UNESCO-listed mountain fortress where a Joseon king withstood siege in 1636. Gwangju City's flagship festival mixes traditional and contemporary stage performances with history experience programs, participatory events, and a hands-on art market inside the provincial park. Free; the fortress wall walk itself, ringed with autumn forest, is reason enough to come.

title: Goyang Lake Arts Festival
overview: A street-arts festival held around Ilsan Lake Park, one of the largest artificial lake parks in Asia. Around 100 performances run across the park — circus, magic, aerial work and pieces that sit between genres — alongside hands-on programmes open to anyone. Fireworks over the lake and night-time programming close each evening. Free, and about 40 minutes from central Seoul on Subway Line 3.
place: Ilsan Lake Park and Ilsan Culture Plaza

title: Korean Confucian Culture Festival
overview: A festival translating Confucian values — loyalty, filial piety, propriety — into contemporary life, at the Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute in Nonsan, the heartland of Joseon's Confucian academies. Three days of performances, exhibitions, a humanities book concert, the K-Confucianism international forum, and family competitions and hands-on programs. Free entry (some programs paid). Pairs naturally with nearby Donam Seowon, a UNESCO World Heritage academy.
place: Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute and Noseong-myeon area

title: Busan International Performing Arts Festival (BPAF)
overview: A street performing-arts festival along the Oncheoncheon stream and the university district near Pusan National University, staging everyday urban space as theater. The 2026 theme, 'MOSAIC: many pieces, one picture', brings 28 selected Korean and international productions to outdoor stages, joined by participatory side programs and an art market. Free, 13:00–20:00 — catch it while browsing one of Busan's liveliest student quarters.
place: Oncheoncheon stream and PNU university street

title: Gwimong at Jeju Shinhwa World
overview: An outdoor horror night at Jeju Shinhwa World's theme park: a fright course through real darkened terrain, b-boy and horror-musical performances, ghost-edition rides (spinning coaster, carousel), and a 'gwimong market' of spooky pubs, makeup shops, and food. 30,000 won, gates from 19:00.
place: Shinhwa Theme Park, Jeju Shinhwa World

title: Suwon Jazz Festival
overview: An evening of jazz on the shores of Gwanggyo Lake Park — regularly ranked among Korea's best urban landscapes. Korean and international artists cover the spectrum from straight-ahead jazz to blues and funky crossover, aimed as much at casual listeners as aficionados. Free, outdoors, 17:30–21:30: bring a mat and settle in as the lake lights come on.

title: Mullae Arts Festival
overview: Mullae-dong is Seoul's strangest cultural ecosystem: precision metal workshops and artists' studios sharing the same alleys. Its festival opens that world up through three programs — 'Mullae Hyperlink' exhibitions linking the district's galleries, open studios where artists show work and process in place, and a street festival of performances, media facades, DJ sets, and markets in the alleys between lathes. Some programs need advance sign-up via the Yeongdeungpo foundation site. 12:00–19:00.

title: GES 2026: Game & Esports Seoul
overview: A global game and esports festival at Dongdaemun Design Plaza, hosted by the Seoul city government. Around 100 game and esports companies exhibit across indie and major-studio showcases, with esports tournaments (including a PUBG club match and the Seoul Cup), competitions, and networking programs drawing some 20,000 visitors. Free entry, 10:00–18:00 — three days of Korean gaming culture in one landmark venue.

title: Soesokkak Festival
overview: A two-day festival at Soesokkak, the jade-green lava-cliff estuary on Jeju's south coast, in its 21st year. Free traditional raft, kayak, and jet-boat rides anchor the program, with a youth rock festival, local performances, and fireworks over Hahyo Port.

title: Daegu Maker Festa
overview: A maker festival at the Samsung Creative Campus in Daegu — a complex built inside the company's original 1930s factory site — running under the slogan 'Beyond imagination, make it together'. Exhibits and hands-on booths cover making, science, technology, art and starting a business, with schools, makerspaces, companies and institutions all setting up. Open to anyone; much of it is aimed at school-age visitors but the fabrication demonstrations are worth a look regardless. Free.
sponsor: Daegu Metropolitan City · Daegu Office of Education

title: Incheon Reading Festival
overview: Incheon's book festival at the Incheon Art Platform — a cluster of restored early-1900s port warehouses in the open-port district. Under the slogan 'Read Incheon, connect hearts', the outdoor plaza hosts picture-book performances, busking, a book market of local bookstores and publishers, photo zones, and a book-themed escape game, while indoor sessions run author meetings, book talks, and forums. Free, 11:00–17:00 — and the surrounding Incheon open-port streets and Chinatown make a full day of it.

title: Suwon Hwaseong Media Art
overview:
Suwon Hwaseong Media Art is a nighttime festival held against the backdrop of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Since its launch in 2021, the event has presented large-scale media art inspired by the fortress and its history. Beginning in 2026, the festival has been newly reimagined under the theme “Saebit Dongrak: Suwon Hwaseong Blossoming in Light,” inviting visitors to experience the site through light and shared enjoyment.

The festival brings together light, video, and performance to create immersive media art installations that trace the stories of people from the construction of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress to the present. Centered around the Hwahongmun Gate and Jangan Park areas, it features a wide range of experiential and interactive works, offering visitors a dynamic mix of visual spectacles and engaging activities throughout the event period.
place: Area of Hwaseomun Gate, Janganmun Gate, and Jangan Park

title: Mungyeong Eco-Camping Festival
overview: Camping, environment, and music meet on the banks of the Yeonggang River in Mungyeong. The program pairs the Yeonggang River Run with upcycling and recycling workshops that make resource circulation hands-on, plus family side events through the day. The closer is a headline hip-hop double bill — Dynamic Duo and Mighty Mouth — heating up the riverside autumn night. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Hanam Iseongsanseong Fortress Festival
overview: Excavations at Iseongsanseong, a hilltop fortress above Hanam, turned up a yogo — an hourglass drum, and the oldest percussion instrument found in Korea. The 2026 festival takes that drumbeat as its theme, 'Hanam's history, drumming toward the future', and links two sites: the fortress itself and Misa Lake Park down in the city where people actually spend their weekends. The programme is built for taking part rather than looking at — drumming, making, performances into the evening. Free.
place: Misa Lake Park lawn and Iseongsanseong Fortress

title: Gijang Pet Culture Festival
overview: A companion-animal festival in Busan's Gijang County themed 'happy coexistence with pets' — its third edition. New this year: a walk-together event for pets and owners, and 'K-Pet Got Talent', a national showcase for gifted dogs and cats. Experience, education, and participation programs run throughout, aimed at both pet owners and the pet-curious, with responsible pet culture and animal welfare as the through-line. Free, 09:00–18:00 at Jeonggwan Central Park.

title: Gyeongju Golden Carnival
overview: A music festival with no main stage. Under the concept 'OFF THE STAGE', Gyeongju's old downtown — a shuttered cinema, empty storefronts, cafes, and alleys around the Hwangnidan and Geumnidan streets — becomes a constellation of small live venues, and the audience discovers performances rather than arriving at them. Local food and drink pace the wandering between sets. A one-ticket (55,000 won) experiment in using an ancient city's modern quarter as an instrument. 11:00–22:00.

title: Gwangmyeong Book Festival
overview: Gwangmyeong's reading-culture festival on the lawn of the civic gymnasium, slogan: 'The start of infinite exploration, a friendly book journey!'. The grounds fill with hands-on programs, performances, author book concerts, and all-ages reading events designed to make books a shared outing rather than a solitary habit. Free, 10:00–17:00; program details on the city library website.

title: Alien Festival
overview: Korea's only alien-themed festival, run by the Miryang Arirang Space Observatory — the country's observatory specializing in the search for extraterrestrial life. The 7th edition is styled as an 'alien sports day': Meteor Run races, laser tag, and a costume contest get families running rather than watching, with space-science content woven through for the educational payoff. Free, 10:00–18:00 at the Miryang stadium grounds.

title: Suwon Nammun Market Night Market 'Bulchwimugwi'
overview: 'No going home sober!' — King Jeongjo's famous toast lends its name to this night market at the Paldalmun gate markets in Suwon, held September 5 and 19. Built on the history of the market Jeongjo opened for his people, it fills the streets with food trucks, merchant stalls, and an art market, wrapped in a light story-world: duel the wandering taoist character, hunt hidden talismans, break magical seals. Eat, walk, and photograph your way through a market district that has been trading since the 18th century.
place: Paldalmun plaza and Jidonggyo Bridge area

title: Youth Coffee Festival
overview: A coffee-and-culture festival on the plazas beneath Lotte World Tower, themed 'the perfect blend to wake today's me'. Korean and international coffee and dessert brands pour tastings, surrounded by photo zones and participatory programs, while the stage runs artist performances, youth talk concerts, auditions, classic screenings, and the 29-second film festival awards. Free, 13:00–18:00 — a caffeinated afternoon in Jamsil aimed at Seoul's twenty-somethings but open to all.
place: Lotte World Tower Arena Plaza and lawn

title: Cheongchun-daero Youth Street Festival
overview: A day-long street festival on the open-air stage at Seoul Children's Grand Park, run by Gwangjin-gu and programmed largely by students from nearby Konkuk and Sejong universities. Club performances, busking, a talk show and headline acts run through the afternoon, with a flea market and craft stalls from young local makers. Free, and easy to combine with the park itself, which is one of the largest green spaces in eastern Seoul.
place: Open Stage, Seoul Children's Grand Park

title: U-Plef Youth Festival, Namyangju
overview: A one-day youth festival on the Han River at Sampae, Namyangju. Hands-on booths run by young organisers open at 13:00, a local talent stage follows in the late afternoon, and the evening closes with performances by rapper Gaogaii and singer Kim Na-young. Food trucks, a flea market and a non-alcoholic beer bar run alongside. Free, on the riverside about 40 minutes east of central Seoul.
place: Sampae District Water Park, Han River Park

title: Tuntun Pet Festa
overview: A two-day pet festival at Dongtan Yeoul Park in Hwaseong — a park already built for dogs, with its own pet playground. The fifth edition runs craft programs (walk bottle-bags, photo mugs), plus practical counseling corners: pet legal advice, health-check consultations, and behavior consultations, backed by the agriculture ministry and the Korea Kennel Association. Free entry, 10:00–18:00; bring the dog.

title: Seokgye Station Moonlight Night Market
overview: A neighborhood night market at the culture park by Seokgye Station in northeast Seoul, run to boost the local alley economy. Food booths, craft beer and makgeolli, retro games, photo zones, and a flea market fill the park, with busking stages and headline performances (past editions have drawn well-known Korean singers). Booth prices vary; open 14:00–22:00. A low-key, genuinely local slice of Seoul night-market culture.

title: Moonlight Workout Busan Challenge
overview: An outdoor fitness event held on autumn evenings across three Busan parks — Busan Citizens Park, the North Port waterfront and Hwamyeong Ecological Park. Sessions are led by well-known fitness instructors and cover gymnastics, yoga, circuit training, zumba and children's classes, interspersed with taekwondo and cheerleading displays, busking and comedy. There are also fitness-test booths, archery, basketball, bowling and golf try-outs, and a random-play dance challenge. Free, informal, and one of the more unusual things to do in Busan after dark.
place: Busan Citizens Park · North Port Waterfront Park · Hwamyeong Ecological Park

title: Ulju Drone Festival
overview: A day of drones at Jakcheonjeong plaza in Ulju: balloon-popping and obstacle-racing drone games, drone basketball, plus AI baduk robots, an AI painter, quadruped robots, 3D printing, and a disaster-safety experience hall. Stages feature Chae Yeon, Lee Ji-hoon, Sleepy, and local crews. The finale is the point: a 1,300-drone light show choreographed to music over the autumn night sky — one of the larger drone shows on the Korean festival circuit. Free, 14:00–21:00.

title: Han River Walk
overview: The Han River Walk is a walking event that takes place at various locations along the Hangang River. Participants can expect to enjoy light exercise in beautiful natural settings, as well as earn a completion medal. In addition to walking, the festival dates will feature a range of additional events for a lively environment.

title: Seoul Street Arts Festival
overview: Seoul Street Arts Festival is held in Ttukseom Hangang Park and Seoul Forest. This year's festival presents international performances from France, Lithuania, Chile and more, in addition to local performances.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government, Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Haksan Madanggeuk Nollae Festival
overview: A citizen-created theater festival in Incheon's Michuhol district, running since 2014. Residents write and stage their own madanggeuk — open-air folk theater — drawing on neighborhood issues and life stories, in forms ranging from percussion drama and mask dance to puppet, music, and staged-reading theater. Performed outdoors by the artificial waterfall in Subong Park, it is community art in the most literal sense: the neighbors are the cast. Free, 17:00–21:00.

title: Uiwang Baekun Lake Festival
overview: Uiwang's autumn festival on the lawn plaza of Baekun Lake, a reservoir ringed by wooded hills just south of Seoul. Headline music performances share the bill with busking, free and paid hands-on programs, food courts, and events by local artists and residents — a community festival first, with the lake path there for strolling between acts. Free, 10:00–22:00.

title: Ansan Daebu Grape Festival
overview: Daebudo Island's sea-breeze vineyards produce unusually sweet, aromatic grapes, and this festival — running since 1995 — is their annual showcase. A direct-sale market cuts out the middleman for freshly picked bunches, while the signature grape-stomping event, concerts, the Daebu Haesol-gil walking festival, and the Ansan marathon fill the weekend at the Daebu Sea Fragrance Theme Park. Free, 09:00–18:00; an easy island day trip on Seoul's doorstep.

title: Bibliotheca Busan
overview: Bibliotheca Busan, set against the stunning backdrop of the sea in Busan, is an outdoor festival that blends books, culture, and art. Visitors can enjoy reading as well as cultural programs organized in collaboration with public libraries, bookstores, publishers, and cultural institutions in Busan.
hours: 14:00-21:00* Subject to change depending on weather conditions

title: Seoripul Music Festival
overview: For one weekend a year, Seoul closes the ten-lane Banpo-daero boulevard and turns it into a concert ground — the signature move of this Seocho district festival, which has drawn a cumulative 1.34 million visitors since 2015. The 2026 edition, 'Seocho is the Music', caps a month-long borough-wide music journey with two days of multi-genre stages and citizen programs on the open avenue. Free (market and food booths excepted).

title: Seoul Philharmonic Park Concert
overview: The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra under music director Jaap van Zweden plays a free open-air evening at the Forest Stage of Seoul Children's Grand Park, joined by top-flight guest soloists. No reservation needed — just arrive and sit — and the concert streams live on the Seoul city and orchestra YouTube channels. 19:00–20:30. One of the easiest ways to hear a world-class orchestra for free.
place: Forest Stage, Seoul Children's Grand Park

title: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish Fulfillment Festival
overview: Gatbawi is a 9th-century stone Buddha near the summit of Palgongsan, wearing a flat slab on its head that looks like a traditional Korean hat — hence the name. It has drawn people praying for a single wish to be granted for over a thousand years, and this festival, now in its 25th year, is built around that. The two days include a yadanbeopseok gathering mixing rock bands, Buddhist chant, Wonhyo's muae dance and sound meditation; an opening bibimbap offering shared among the crowd; a healing concert with gugak singer Nam Sang-il; and an orchestral wish concert with baritone Kim Dong-gyu and soprano Kang Hye-jung. A temple run along the Gatbawi wish trail and a templestay at Seonbonsa run on advance registration, and there are temple-food demonstrations and wish-paper hanging at the main site. Free.

title: Yongsan Youth Festival: Fancy a Rest?
overview: A one-day festival for young residents of Yongsan-gu built around the idea of rest — the programme is framed as emptying the mind, refilling energy and heading back out into the world. It runs in the former officers' quarters at Yongsan Park, the site handed back after more than a century of military use and now one of central Seoul's most unusual public spaces. The stage bill mixes dance crews, a gugak ensemble, magic and pop acts. Free.

title: Seven Bridges Tour 2026
overview: A 77 km cycling event across Busan's sea bridges — the only day of the year these spans open to bicycles. The route starts on Gwangan Bridge and links Busan Harbour Bridge, Namhang Bridge and Eulsukdo Bridge, riding above the water on roads normally closed to anything but cars. For non-cyclists there is a separate Gwangan Bridge walking programme, plus wellness activities and a food lounge around Yongho Byeolbit Park. Paid entry, and Busan residents get 50 per cent off.
place: Across Busan — major sea bridges and the city centre
fee: Seven Bridges Tour 100,000 won (early bird 80,000 won) · Good Morning Bridge Walking 10,000 won · 50% off for Busan residents

title: Seomjin River International Experimental Art Festival 2025 (SIEAF)
overview: An experimental and performance art festival held along the Seomjingang, the river running through Gokseong in the south of the country. The 2025 theme was 'Seomjingang Byeolgok' — byeolgok being a form of folk song that carried private stories of ordinary lives — reworked so that the lives and legends along the river are told in the language of contemporary art. Around 100 artists from Korea and abroad took part, with work staged outdoors at the Amnok riverside recreation area. Free; times varied by programme.

title: Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo
overview: Goseong is one of the world's three great dinosaur-footprint fossil sites, and its expo — running since 2006, now in its 10th edition and 20th year — is Korea's flagship dinosaur event. The Danghangpo venue combines a dinosaur theme zone and an Admiral Yi Sun-sin zone with coastal walks, trails, and fossil-footprint paths. The 2026 theme is 'an exciting adventure with dinosaurs', with exhibitions, hands-on programs, and shows aimed squarely at families. Adults 19,000 won, children 13,000 won; open to 22:00 on night-opening days.

title: Andong Maskdance Festival
overview: The Andong Maskdance Festival is a global celebration where the memories carried by masks come to life through dance. Visitors can experience Korea’s mask dance traditions, inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list, alongside mask dances from around the world. A wide range of performances, parades, the Tallori Daedongnanjang community celebrations, and the World Maskplay Competition create opportunities for people to come together and share in the festival experience. The 2026 Andong Maskdance Festival seeks to connect the stories preserved in masks with contemporary life. As children and seniors, local residents and international visitors gather in the same place to laugh, applaud, and share the rhythm of the festival, the memories carried by masks become a living culture. Shaped by the participation of all who take part, the festival becomes a true “dance for everyone,” celebrating the power of community and the joy of coming together.
place: Jungang Line 1942 Andong Station, Mask Dance Park, and Andong Old Downtown
sponsor: Korea Foundation for Cultures and Ethics

title: Inje Autumn Flower Festival
overview: An autumn garden festival in the mountains of Inje, near the Yongdae tourist area at the foot of Seoraksan. The 2026 edition marks the centenary of Park In-hwan, a leading poet of Korean modernism who was born here, and the planting is arranged along four themed paths named after his lines — a romantic garden and lookout, a wildflower garden and chrysanthemum bonsai display, a lakeside walk with a slow postbox, and a forest section with a tree-climbing course, treehouse and children's woodland. There is a market selling local produce and chrysanthemums, food trucks, performances, and a stamp trail. Free, with some activities charged.

title: EX-Pumpkin Night: Magic Kingdom
overview: Gyeongju Expo Park's Halloween tradition, in its fifth year: the Hwarang forest becomes a pumpkin kingdom complete with Halloween-styled fire stations, police, and broadcast studios where kids role-play jobs among the night lights.

title: Changgyeonggung Palace Night Banquet
overview: A family-friendly night banquet at Changgyeonggung Palace, reinterpreting the feast Crown Prince Hyomyeong held for his father King Sunjo. Participants dress in court attire as Joseon officials and noblewomen, taste royal confections, watch traditional performances, and join palace experience programs around Munjeongjeon Hall. The autumn run spans late September through early October — including the Chuseok holiday — making it a natural family outing for the season. Sessions 17:00–20:30.
sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

title: 2026 Korea Urban & Regional Innovation Expo
overview: Korea's largest urban-innovation expo, gathering government ministries, local governments, and companies around urban regeneration and regional innovation — exhibitions, seminars, and results-sharing sessions across four days at Osong Convention Center (OSCO) in Cheongju. Held annually since 2019 as a public-private-industry-academia forum. Free entry, 10:00–17:00 (to 15:00 Friday). A policy-and-industry event rather than a festival.
sponsor: MOLIT · Chungcheongbuk-do · Cheongju City · Yonhap News

title: Dobong Hangeul Festival
overview: A Hangeul Day festival in the district where key figures of the alphabet's history rest — King Sejong's daughter Princess Jeongui, collector Jeon Hyeong-pil who saved the Hunminjeongeum manuscript, and poet Kim Su-yeong. The 14th edition marks 579 years since Hangeul's promulgation with exhibitions and family programs at Wondangsaem Park.

title: Jeongseon Arirang Festival
overview: The Jeongseon Arirang Festival is Jeongseon County’s signature cultural tourism festival created to preserve and carry forward the history, cultural value, and traditions of Jeongseon Arirang, one of Korea’s best-known folk songs. Celebrating Arirang, which is inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, the festival brings together performances that blend tradition with contemporary elements, parades, hands-on programs, exhibitions, and various cultural and artistic events for visitors of all ages. The festival is also shaped by the local community, with residents taking on an active role in its planning and operation. Programs connecting Jeongseon’s cultural and tourism resources help boost the local economy and attract more visitors to the region. Building on the cultural legacy of Arirang and the unique traditions of Jeongseon, the festival seeks to establish itself as Korea’s leading Arirang celebration and grow into a global cultural tourism festival that people around the world can enjoy and relate to.

title: Gimje Horizon Festival
overview: The Gimje Horizon Festival is Korea’s only Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival dedicated to traditional farming culture, as designated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. Centered around Byeokgolje Reservoir, Korea’s oldest and largest irrigation facility, the festival celebrates the nation's rich farming heritage. Set against the region's expansive horizon, the festival features the Presidential Cup National Nongak Competition, along with hands-on agricultural experiences such as cooking rice over a traditional wood-fired stove, catching grasshoppers, and harvesting rice. Visitors can also take part in traditional events, including the Byeokgolje Twin Dragon Play, inspired by a local legend, and the Ipseok Tug-of-War for a bountiful harvest.

title: Ground Forces Festival
overview: Korea's largest military culture festival, hosted by the ROK Army on the runway of Gyeryongdae — the tri-service headquarters. Five days of the latest Korean and US combat equipment on display (much of it climbable), Army TIGER and drone-bot demonstrations, AI-based combat systems at the army policy hall, and a full slate of military pageantry: military band and honor guard shows, taekwondo demonstrations, military police motorcycle drills, and road parades. Free, 09:00–17:00 over the Chuseok holiday window.

title: Busan International Performing Arts Market (BPAM)
overview: A festival-style performing-arts market in Busan, now in its fourth year: artists, producers, and presenters from Korea and abroad showcase productions, build networks, and negotiate distribution — but unlike a pure trade fair, the showcases are open for ordinary audiences to enjoy. Venues center on Dongseo University's Centum campus and the Haeundae Culture Center. Fees vary by program; 10:00–22:00.
place: Dongseo University Centum Campus and Haeundae Culture Center

title: Cheonan World Dance Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Cheonan World Dance Festival is a global event that brings everyone together through dance, transcending nationalities and language barriers. Dancers from all over the world gather in Cheonan to participate in various festival programs. The National Dance Competition is the highlight of the festival, with a total prize of about 100 million won. There is also the Street Dance Parade across the city center and the International Dance Competition in which dance teams from across the globe participate. Other shows include the energetic performances of the National University Cheerleading Competition and the exciting “Improv Dance Battle,” where everyone can join in on the fun.
sponsor: Cheonan Foundation for Arts and Culture

title: Gyeryong Military Culture Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The 2025 Gyeryong Military Culture Festival will take place from September 17 (Wed.) to 21 (Sun.) at the Gyeryongdae Runway and venues across the city under the slogan “Gyeryong’s Dream, K-Military Culture Taking Flight to the World!” Recognized as one of Korea’s leading festivals, the event will offer a wide range of performances and activities for visitors of all ages. Highlights include the opening celebration, Military Culture Festa concerts featuring rock, trot, K-pop, and other genres, guest performances by military bands and honor guards, and road parade. Visitors can also enjoy hands-on activities and special programs including Extreme Special Experiences, all designed to raise the profile of military culture. This year’s festival will also feature a special Wellness Life Exhibition that brings together military culture and lifestyle in a new festival experience.
place: Gyeryongdae Runway and various locations across Gyeryong-si

title: Geumsan World K-Insam Festival
overview: Held in Geumsan, Chungcheongnam-do, long known as the home of ginseng with a history spanning more than 1,500 years, the Geumsan World K-Insam Festival invites visitors of all ages to experience ginseng in every form. The festival features hands-on programs such as ginseng digging, red ginseng facial mask treatments, red ginseng foot baths, traditional ginseng culture experiences, and the International Ginseng Trade Fair, along with opportunities to shop for ginseng products at reasonable prices. Across the festival grounds, visitors can also enjoy healthy dishes made with ginseng and medicinal herbs. Held annually since 1981, the festival has become one of Korea’s leading industry-based festivals. It has been named one of Korea’s Top Cultural Tourism Festivals by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism 10 times and was selected as an Asian Specialty Festival by IFEA World in 2024. Today, the Geumsan World K-Insam Festival continues to grow as a global festival enjoyed by visitors from Korea and beyond.

title: Yeoncheon Goryeo Ginseng Festival
overview: Yeoncheon sits on the 38th parallel with the latitude, climate, and soil rated ideal for six-year ginseng — the gold standard of Korean insam. Its festival, in the plaza by Yeoncheon Station, showcases the county's Gaeseong-lineage Goryeo ginseng with exhibitions, direct farm sales, tastings, and hands-on programs, putting growers and buyers face to face. Free, 10:00–17:00. Good for stocking up at source prices on Korea's most famous health root.

title: Uiryeong Rich Rich Festival
overview: In the middle of the Nam River at Uiryeong stands Solbawi, the 'cauldron rock', with a legend: great fortunes will be born within 20 ri of it. The founders of Samsung, LG, and Hyosung were all born nearby — and the county has run with it. The fifth Rich Rich Festival invites visitors to soak up the rock's money-luck through wealth-themed experiences, performances, and family programs around town. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–22:00. Unapologetically fun feng-shui tourism.

title: Soraepogu Festival
overview: Soraepogu Festival, a maritime ecology festival, has been held annually since 2001. Sorae Port has become a popular attraction, visited by over 7 million domestic and international tourists each year. During the festival, visitors can enjoy Sorae Marsh Eco Park, Shrimp Tower, and Haeoreumhosu Lake. Festival programs include seafood-catching events like shrimp and crab catching, various cultural performances, and engaging events.
fee: Free (separate charge may apply to activities)

title: Daejeon Hyo Culture Roots Festival
overview: Hyo — filial devotion to one's parents and ancestors — is the organising idea of this festival, held in Ppuri Park, a hillside park in Daejeon planted with sculpted stones representing the origin of Korean family clans. Visitors can trace the history of a surname and its clan lineage, and the programme wraps that in traditional performances and hands-on activities aimed at getting several generations of a family taking part together. Free.

title: Bongsan Mask Dance
place: Uijeongbu Historic Site Plaza (Gwanghwamun), 45 Jongno-1 gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul

title: Anadream Safety Festival
overview: Gyeongbuk's largest safety-experience event, held since 2021 in the 'thousand-year forest' by the provincial office in Andong. Some 40 agencies run 70-plus hands-on safety programs — fire-engine and rescue-equipment displays, rescue-dog training demos, drone demonstrations, a firefighting parade, and a kids' safety school — leavened with magic and bubble shows, stamp tours, and treasure hunts. Free, 10:00–17:00, and genuinely useful for families with children.

title: Seorak Cultural Festival
overview: Sokcho's oldest festival, running since 1966 and now in its 61st year, held beneath Seoraksan at the start of the autumn foliage season. The 2026 theme is 'Seorak, Turning Colour Together'. At its heart is Seorak Sosa, a mountain rite performed at the very first festival and still held today — now with narration and storytelling added so that visitors can follow what is happening. The programme also includes a climb up Dalmabong, a trail otherwise closed to the public, a mountain concert, and a street parade led by residents, schools and local arts groups rather than professional performers. Free.
place: Sokcho Expo Lawn Plaza and the Seorak Rodeo Street area
sponsor: Sokcho City · Sokcho Culture and Tourism Foundation

title: Bupyeong Pungmul Festival
overview: Celebrating its 30th edition, the Bupyeong Pungmul Festival brings rhythm, excitement, and community spirit to the heart of the city. Since its launch in 1997, the festival has grown into one of Korea’s leading traditional cultural and performing arts festivals. For nearly three decades, it has filled the urban landscape with the vibrant sounds of Korean pungmul, creating a dynamic space where citizens and artists come together. At the heart of the festival are the pungmul troupes from Bupyeong’s 22 neighborhoods, whose lively rhythms have long served as a powerful force for community unity. Held for three days from October 2 to 4, 2026, the 30th Bupyeong Pungmul Festival carries special significance as it reflects on the traditions built over the past three decades while celebrating a new chapter for the future. This year’s edition will be bigger and more colorful than ever, expanding into the Gulpocheon Stream area, an iconic symbol of Bupyeong’s urban regeneration, and presenting an even wider variety of programs and experiences.

title: Goseong Pollack Festival
overview: Goseong on Gangwon's north coast was Korea's pollack capital, and this festival reworks that heritage on the beach at Geojin: a pollack gourmet zone with live chef cooking and cook-it-yourself sessions, fish crafts and games, bare-hand fish catching, a beach playground, and a silent-DJ party on the sand. Residents, soldiers, and students run much of the program themselves. Distributed stages and shuttles keep the beachfront lively all day. Free entry, 11:00–19:00.

title: Anheung Steamed Bun Festival
overview: Anheung's jjinppang — soft steamed buns with red-bean filling — made this Hoengseong village famous, and its 18th festival celebrates them with a full weekend: the bun-and-dokkaebi (goblin) themed main festival drawing on local folklore, the retro 'Saturday Saturday is a Singer' 90s-music stage, roaming goblin performance squads, bun-themed events, and a closing residents' singing contest. Free, 10:00–20:00, in the aptly named 'steaming bun village'. Come hungry.

title: Wanju Wild & Local Food Festival
overview: Wanju — the county that pioneered Korea's local-food movement — throws its flagship festival in the Gosan recreational forest under the 2026 slogan 'burning wild'. Fire is the theme: open-fire oven roasting, local bushcraft, potato pit-steaming, and large fire events, alongside stream water play, straw-bale slides, a 'local table' cooked by the women's associations of all 13 townships, a farm-produce market, and a wild EDM party after dark. Free, 10:00–22:00.

title: Busan International Rock Festival
overview: First held in 2000, the Busan International Rock Festival is Korea’s first and longest-running international rock festival. In 2026, the 27th edition will take place over three days, from Friday, October 2 to Sunday, October 4, at Samnak Eco Park, featuring a diverse lineup of Korean and international artists. Stages set throughout the park will showcase everything from emerging talent to world-renowned headliners. Beyond the performances, visitors can also enjoy a variety of festival attractions, including interactive games, food court lounges, camping zones, and other special side events.

title: Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival
titleFull: Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival (포항 해뜨면 국수축제)
overview: The  Pohang Sunrise Noodle Festival is a grand culinary festival held at Ara Plaza in Guryongpo on the Homi Peninsula. The festival’s name intuitively captures the symbolic significance of the Homi Peninsula—where the sun rises first in South Korea. Visitors can sample everything from Pohang’s best noodle restaurants to representative noodles from across the country, global noodles, and recipes by star chefs—all in one place. The festival also offers plenty of entertainment for all ages, including a music festival, cooking competitions, and retro experiences. Equipped with an eco-friendly system featuring smart QR ordering and reusable containers, the festival offers a unique culinary journey exclusive to Pohang—where the flavors and excitement are first awakened amidst the vibrant energy of the East Sea.
place: The area around Guryongpo Ara Plaza

title: Gunsan Time Travel Festival
overview: Gunsan preserves one of Korea's densest concentrations of Japanese colonial-era architecture, and its signature festival turns that district into a stage for time travel. Large flash-mob performances recreate the era's global currents, the 'March 5th' event fills the streets with the cry of the 1919 independence movement, and a time-currency system converts participation into souvenirs and discounts. Retro 7080 games and food round out a festival that manages to be both a history lesson and a proper day out. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–21:00.
place: Old city hall plaza and Time Travel Village

title: Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival
titleFull: Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival (안성맞춤 남사당 바우덕이축제)
overview: The Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival is centered on Namsadang Nori, which is inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It preserves and builds on the artistic legacy of Baudeogi, the first female kkokdusoe (troupe leader) of the Joseon era, and the vibrant traditions of Anseong’s Namsadang troupe. The festival offers a rich mix of programs for all ages, from traditional cultural experiences and performances by Korean and international artists to folk performances from around the world. Visitors can also explore the Anseong Old Market, which recreates the lively atmosphere of one of the three major marketplaces in Korea during the Joseon period. Highlights include jultagi (tightrope walking) and Namsadang Nori, giving visitors a close-up look at some of Korea’s most dynamic traditional performing arts. Performances that blend traditional and contemporary elements make the festival an engaging way to experience the energy and appeal of Korean culture. Bringing together history, culture, performance, and tourism, the Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival has established itself as a cultural tourism festival enjoyed by visitors from Korea and abroad, and continues to grow as one of Korea’s leading festivals celebrating traditional culture.
place: Anseong Matchum Land & Anseongcheon Stream area

title: Sancheong Medicinal Herb Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Sancheong Herbal Medicinal Festival is a celebration for those interested in traditional herbal medicine. Donguibogam (Principles and Practice of Eastern Medicine) and its author, Heo Jun, are highly regarded in Korean medicine. Sancheong, where Heo Jun studied, is home to Jirisan Mountain, which is often seen as a treasure trove by Korean medicine doctors due to being a habitat of over 1,000 species of medicinal herbs. The festival features Korean medicine clinics offering treatments like acupuncture, while the festival square is transformed into an herbal garden with photo zones, tea drinking spots, spaces for making herbal flower pots, and exhibitions and sales of herbal flower pot goods. Visitors can also participate in making herbal sweet rice puffs, nostalgic herbal dalgona candy, herbal cocktails, and herbal tea brewed in a large decoction pot.◎ Dongui bogamDongui bogam is a medical encyclopedia completed in 1610, written by Heo Jun after a meticulous study and observation of medical books and practices of China and Joseon. It is considered the best medical encyclopedia in the East and was registered as a UNESCO Memory of the World in 2009.

title: Jeonju Heritage Night Tour
overview: 'A night stroll through a thousand-year capital': Jeonju's hanok village, Gyeonggijeon shrine, the Confucian school, Pungnammun gate, and the restored provincial office light up for two June nights of performances, tours, and experiences led by eight themed 'masters'.
place: Jeonju Hanok Village and heritage sites

title: Cheongwon Life Festival
overview: Cheongju's eco-agriculture festival, running since 2008 around the Cheongwon Life brand of premium local produce. The rural theme park in Ochang fills with themed exhibitions, hands-on farm programs, cultural performances, and a direct farmers' market connecting growers and consumers — with a strong education angle for children on where food comes from. Entry 5,000 won; children, teens, pregnant women, and seniors free. 10:00–20:00.
fee: 5,000 won (children, youth, pregnant women, seniors free)

title: Yeongju Punggi Ginseng Festival
overview: Punggi is one of Korea's most storied ginseng regions, and its festival lands in October when the root's nutrients peak. The program leans into health: ginseng-cuisine tastings, ginseng-peeling contests, and wellness exhibitions, plus ritual reenactments — the founding-site rite, Governor Ju Se-bung's procession (the 16th-century official credited with starting cultivation here), and the great ginseng ceremony. Fresh roots, red ginseng, and processed goods sell at grower prices. Free entry, 10:00–20:00.
place: Namwoncheon stream and Punggi Ginseng Park

title: Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*The Jinju Namgang Yudeung Festival is an event that continues the practice of making wishes by floating colorful lanterns down the Namgang River. This practice of over 400 years originated from the Siege of Jinju in 1592. The festival begins at sunset when lanterns of various shapes and sizes are lit on the Namgang River. World Pungmul lanterns, wish lanterns, traditional lanterns, religious lanterns, and customized lanterns embroider the night with colorful lights. Fireworks and lighting shows are held against the backdrop of this beautiful night view, along with various cultural shows. The festival operates food trucks where visitors can enjoy delicious foods from around the world. ◎ The Siege of Jinju and YudeungDuring the Japanese invasion of Korea in 1592, yudeung (oil lanterns) were lit in the battle at Jinjuseong Fortress to stop the Japanese army from crossing the Namgang River. The lanterns were also used as a means of contacting families outside the fortress.
place: Areas of Jinjuseong Fortress and Namgang River

title: Gangnam Festival
overview: Gangnam Festival, the largest urban festival unfolding across the entire city center, begins with a spectacular street parade to mark the opening. The festival transforms the entirety of Gangnam into one massive festival space featuring K-POP concerts, family concerts for the whole family to enjoy, a Fashion & Beauty Festa combining K-fashion and performance, and a Beer & Food Festa offering diverse culinary experiences. As a global K-Culture festival combining the city's energy with Hallyu content, the Gangnam Festival is a representative cultural tourism event that promotes the charms of Gangnam to the world.
place: Areas of Dosandaero Avenue, Gaepo-dong Maru Park, and Bongeunsa Temple

title: Baekje Cultural Festival
overview: Baekje Cultural Festival first started in 1955 and aims to bring the history and culture of the Baekje era to life, taking place at UNESCO-recognized sites throughout Gongju and Buyeo. The festival operates as an open event where the history and culture of Baekje, local businesses, and the daily lives of residents harmonize, and is expected to provide visitors with a special cultural experience where the past and present coexist.
place: Buyeo historic sites (Jeongnimsaji Temple Site, Seoktap-ro, Gwanbuk-ri)

title: Yeongju Punggi Insam Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Ginseng is a well-known traditional Korean medicinal herb. High quality ginseng in Korea is mostly produced in Punggi, a region in Yeongju, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and the place where the Punggi Ginseng Festival takes place. The festival features health-related exhibits and offers opportunities to taste healthy ginseng dishes at the ginseng cooking exhibition. Visitors can also participate in Punggi ginseng-related interesting activities such as making Punggi ginseng wine and peeling ginseng in the traditional Korean way. The festival offers a variety of ginseng products, including fresh ginseng, original ginseng, red ginseng, and ginseng processed foods, which are all grown by local farmers in Yeongju and sold at reasonable prices. Additionally, the festival showcases local specialties and symbols such as ginseng and Yeongju apples through oil lantern displays along Namwoncheon Stream. With so many attractions, visitors are sure to have a great time at the festival.
sponsor: Yeongju  Punggi Insam Festival Organizing Committee

title: Yeongju Museom Single-Log Bridge Festival
overview: Museom is a riverside heritage village wrapped in a bend of the Naeseongcheon stream, reached for centuries by a narrow single-log bridge over the water and white sand. The festival reenacts the village's life rites — a traditional wedding procession arriving by palanquin, a funeral bier procession departing — alongside bridge-crossing performances, barefoot sand walking, parade games, rope experiences, a poetry contest, a national photo contest, and a stamp tour. Free, 10:00–18:00. One of the most photogenic festivals in the country.

title: Chuncheon Ani-Toy Festival
overview: A three-day subculture fair at the Animation Museum in Chuncheon, gathering animation, characters, art toys, figures, goods, and creator content in one place. Brand and artist booths, industry experience programs, and sales floors run side by side, bringing companies, creators, fans, and collectors together — with plenty for families in between the collector stalls. Free, 11:00–17:00 over the early-October holiday weekend.

title: Yongin Youth Festival
overview: A space-themed Youth Day festival planned by young residents themselves, joined by city mascot Joayong: UFO wish-making, perfume and patch workshops, quiz olympics, and youth policy zones at Yongin Mir Stadium.

title: Donggang Doomchit
overview: A one-day outdoor lifestyle festival on the banks of the Donggang River in Yeongwol, run by and for the county's young residents. There is an outdoor reading garden, a market of young Yeongwol brands, a food club built around local produce, and a live radio programme broadcasting listeners' stories and interviews from the riverbank. Birdwatching, mindfulness sessions, hula dancing and caricature drawing run through the day, with evening sets from Korean indie acts including Yozoh, Soran and Seoul Bossa Society. Free.

title: Guardians of Jinju Mission Tour
overview: A web-based mystery mission game through Jinjuseong Fortress at night: three story series — a historical narrative, a three-character whodunit, and a fantasy edition in Korean and English — played by collecting clues among the lantern-lit fortress grounds, no app needed, souvenirs on completion.

title: King Jeongjo Filial Piety Festival
overview: Hwaseong's flagship history festival at Jeongjo Hyo Park, honoring the king whose devotion to his father shaped the region. The centerpiece reenacts the relocation of Crown Prince Sado's tomb to Yungneung — considered Joseon's finest burial site — and on October 4 the great royal procession of 1795 sets out from Dongtan Central Park in full period costume, one of Korea's grandest parade reenactments. Traditional performances and family programs fill the park throughout. Free, 10:00–18:00.

title: Dongdaemun Festival
overview: For one day, 700 meters of Janghan-ro go car-free under the theme 'a new gallop of culture' — a nod to the street's history, from the Joseon military horse pastures of Janghanpyeong to the modern used-car district. Performances, hands-on programs, and citizen events run the length of the road, including a pop-up roller rink and 'my car becomes a shop', where residents' own vehicles turn into market stalls. Free, 11:00–22:00.
place: Janghan-ro (700m, Woori Bank crossing to Jangan crossing)

title: Dangjin Haenaru Sweet Potato Festival
overview: Dangjin's sweet potatoes grow in yellow-ochre soil under sea wind from the west coast, which the region credits for their sweetness and dry, floury texture. The ninth edition of this harvest festival sells them direct from the growers below market price, alongside food stalls doing sweet potato fritters, dig-your-own plots for children, craft workshops, a regional produce market and stage performances. Free to enter, with some programmes charged.

title: Yongin Cyber Science Festival
overview: The 26th edition of Yongin's science festival, held over two days at Yongin Mir Stadium. Four themed zones cover future technology, a hands-on workshop, the future city and young scientists — with robot-arm demonstrations, humanoid robots and drones to pilot, future mobility to ride, and VR simulators. There are carbon-neutral energy experiments, making gadgets with Arduino and 3D pens, and a care robot to try. Samsung Electronics and other local companies show current work alongside school science clubs, a drone soccer class and character-based science kits. Free, with a materials charge on some activities.

title: Gwacheon Youth Festival (Eopstival)
overview: A one-day youth festival built on a joke with teeth: 'everything Gwacheon does not have' — pop-up cinema, board-game cafe, arcade, and pocha street appear in Central Park for a single day, with performances, policy booths, and food trucks.

title: Festival Gwangmyeong
overview: Gwangmyeong closes an eight-lane road beside Cheolsan Station and turns it into a street festival for two days. The GM Live main stage runs eleven acts: singer-songwriter 10cm headlines the first night with Daybreak, Jack Kingkong, Asrai and Asadal, and Korean rock veteran Kim Jong-seo the second, with Romantic Punch, Bulnabang Star Sausage Club and others. On the closed road itself there is a random-play dance, street karaoke, a bubble show and stilt performers, plus a civic parade, youth busking and market stalls run by local social enterprises. Free.
place: The eight-lane road at Cheolsan Station

title: Suwon Hwaseong Festival
overview: The Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival reimagines, through a contemporary lens, the most magnificent moments of King Jeongjo’s eight-day royal procession to Hwaseong in 1795. Historic scenes recorded in the Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe come vividly to life through high-quality cultural programs. Visitors can also take part in the King Jeongjo Royal Parade, the largest royal procession reenactment in Korea, where citizens and guests from around the world become part of the spectacle. As a leading global festival, the Suwon Hwaseong Festival offers a unique opportunity to experience the joy of a celebration that transcends time and space while bringing people together in the historic setting of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress.
sponsor: Suwon-si, Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival Organizing Committee, Suwon Cultural Foundation

title: Gumcheon Siheung Haenggung Cultural Festival
overview: The 'Geumcheon Siheung Palace Cultural Festival' is a representative historical and cultural festival of Geumcheon-gu that embodies the district's historical identity and cultural artistic significance. The festival offers diverse programs for all residents to enjoy together.

title: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade
titleFull: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade (정조대왕 능행차 공동재현)
overview: King Jeongjo's Royal Parade to Hwaseong Fortress recreates one of the most remarkable events of the Joseon dynasty. In 1795, King Jeongjo traveled from Seoul to Suwon to celebrate the 60th birthday of his mother, Queen Heonui, sharing the eight-day journey with the people along the route. Based on records from the "Wonhaeng Eulmyo Jeongni Uigwe," the festival faithfully reenacts the royal procession with traditional costumes, performances, and ceremonial displays. Held through the cooperation of Seoul, Gyeonggi-do, Suwon, and Hwaseong, the event offers visitors a chance to experience the grandeur and spirit of a historic royal celebration.
sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government, Gyeonggi Province, Suwon Special City, Hwaseong Special City

title: Creative X Seongsu
overview: A culture-and-creative-industry festival spread across Seongsu-dong — Seoul's converted-factory district often compared to Brooklyn. Anchored at the S-Factory, the program mixes themed exhibitions by culture-tech companies, conferences and pitches, 'Play Seongsu' turning the whole district into a game theme park, gallery exhibitions, a craft flea market, an outdoor fashion show, and an urban music festival. Fees and hours vary by program — check before you go, then let the neighborhood's cafes fill the gaps.

title: Gwangju Busking World Cup
overview: An international street-music competition staged across downtown Gwangju, centered on the May 18 Democracy Plaza. Buskers from Korea and abroad — vocalists, bands, acoustic acts, performers — battle through preliminaries and finals judged by a professional panel, turning the city's streets into open stages for days. Free, 13:00–22:00; the finals nights draw the biggest crowds.

title: Hamyang Wild Ginseng Festival
overview: Hamyang's mountain-grown ginseng — raised above 500m in germanium-rich soil, dense-fleshed and high in saponin — is billed as Korea's premium sansam, backed by the country's first wild-ginseng traceability system. The festival unfolds in Sangnim Park, a 1,100-year-old planted forest and Natural Monument, with programs reviving the culture of the simmani (wild-ginseng hunters), local-produce markets, and forest-and-culture events. Free, 10:00–21:00; the ancient forest alone justifies the visit.

title: Royal Culture Festival
overview: Korea's biggest heritage festival: nine days each spring and autumn across all five Seoul palaces and Jongmyo shrine — performances, rite reenactments, night openings, and experiences. The 12th edition, 'Palaces Awaken Art', opens with a night spectacle at Gyeongbokgung's Heungnyemun plaza. THE event to plan a spring Seoul trip around.
place: Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Deoksugung, Changgyeonggung, Gyeonghuigung, Jongmyo

title: Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection
titleFull: Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection (광주 추억의 충장축제)
addr: 226-22, Geumnam-ro, Dong-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City
overview: The Chungjang Street Festival of Recollection is Gwangju’s largest signature festival, originating on Chungjang-ro in Dong-gu. Built around the universal theme of memories, it is Korea’s first festival of its kind, bringing together people of all generations and backgrounds. Geumnam-ro and May 18 Democracy Square, the festival’s main venues, hold profound significance in the history of democracy. They symbolize not only remembrance of the past but also Gwangju’s journey toward a hopeful future. Recognized for its excellence, the festival has been designated by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as both a Cultural Tourism Festival and an Honorary Cultural Tourism Festival. It has also gained international recognition through consecutive honors at the Asia’s Pinnacle Awards and Gwangju’s designation as a World Festival City. Looking ahead, the festival aims to grow into a truly international event through collaboration with the Asia Culture Center, embracing the cultures and shared memories of Asia. In doing so, it strengthens Gwangju's role as a leading cultural city of Asia and provides a meaningful platform for communication and harmony through culture.
place: Geumnam-ro, Chungjang-ro, May 18 Democracy Square, and Art Street
sponsor: Gwangju Dong-gu, Dong-gu Culture & Tourism Foundation, Chungjang Festival Organizing Committee

title: Hoengseong Hanu Festival
overview: Hoengseong Hanu Festival is the biggest hanu (Korean cattle) festival in Korea. Visitors can buy hanu and local agricultural products at a discounted price. The festival consists of various programs across three themes: food, culture and arts, and experiences.
fee: Free (separate charge may apply to activities)

title: Naju Yeongsangang River Festival
overview: Naju's five-day autumn festival in the Yeongsangang Garden, where the wide river meets landscaped grounds. Days bring garden strolls, family programs, and Naju food (the city is famous for its beef-broth gukbap and pears); nights turn to illuminated riverscapes and headline performances. A stay-all-day festival that doubles as an introduction to one of Jeolla's oldest river towns. Free, 11:00–21:00.

title: Hongcheon Ginseng & Hanwoo Festival
overview: Hongcheon's flagship harvest festival pairing its six-year ginseng with local hanwoo beef: direct farm sales, grill zones, folk games with residents and the local army garrison, and full days of stages in the Tori Forest.

title: Jeungpyeong Insamgol Festival
overview: Jeungpyeong grows about two-thirds of Chungbuk's ginseng, and its harvest festival has grown into a full-spectrum event: the 'In-Maek Party' pairing ginseng with beer and EDM, an international youth festival, a national song contest, a national busking festival, and nightly fireworks. Family and health experience zones, on-site produce auctions, and traditional ssireum wrestling round it out. Free, 10:00–20:00 along the Bogangcheon sports park.

title: Jangseong Hwangryonggang Autumn Flower Festival
titleFull: Jangseong Hwangryonggang Autumn Flower Festival (장성 황룡강 가을꽃축제)
overview: The Jangseong Hwangryonggang River Autumn Flower Festival is set against the backdrop of the 3.2-kilometer-long Hwangryonggang River. The festival features gardens where visitors can admire a variety of autumn flowers, such as cosmos and zinnias. This festival allows visitors to observe the changing seasons up close as they stroll through the gardens along the riverside and admire the flowers within them. It also features hands-on activities for visitors to participate in, as well as performances by local artists and invited singers, making it a festival that welcomes people of all ages. With rest areas and amenities provided throughout the festival grounds, along with displays of local agricultural specialties and food, this festival allows visitors to experience all that Jangseong has to offer in one place.

title: Jeongeup Gujeolcho Flower Festival
overview: Every October, 150,000 square meters of white gujeolcho (Korean chrysanthemum) bloom beneath a pine forest along a clear mountain stream in Jeongeup — the largest such garden in the East, and one of Korea's most beloved photography spots, whether in dawn mist or afternoon light. Walking paths thread the pine-scented flower hills, joined by local-heritage experience programs and farm-produce markets. Ticketed entry, 08:30–17:30.

title: Gokseong Simcheong Children's Festival
overview: A children's festival at the Gokseong Train Village — the steam-train theme park on the Seomjin River — built on the filial-daughter folktale of Simcheong: character shows, musicals, magic, and mission adventures through the rose garden.

title: Imsil N Cheese Festival
overview: *The information below is based on the 2025 festivals. Details for the 2026 festivals will be updated as they become available.*Imsil N Cheese Festival is held every fall in Imsil, the birthplace of cheese production in Korea, at Imsil Cheese Theme Park and Imsil Cheese Village, which are proud symbols of the region. Visitors are greeted by the aroma of delicious cheese as they wander through the beautiful chrysanthemum flower garden with millions of blooms. The festival features more than 10 main themes and 70 programs centered around cheese, offering a rich and diverse experience. Events include Imsil N Busking, kids’ concerts, various craft experiences, and a stamp rally tour, ensuring plenty of fun for everyone.◎ TipIt is recommended to bring a tripod or an extra battery pack to take many pictures of the quaint buildings and flower gardens at the festival.
place: Imsil Cheese Theme Park, Imsil Cheese Village, and the Imsil-eup area

title: Gunsan Jjamppong Festival
overview: A noodle festival for Gunsan's claim to fame: jjamppong, the spicy seafood noodle soup that evolved here from the Chinese-Korean chomamyeon of the port's overseas-Chinese community. Chinese-restaurant booths, jjamppong-themed programs, and stages fill the Baeknyeon Plaza.

title: Siheung Wolgot Port Festival
overview: A harbor festival at Wolgot, the fishing port folded into the city on Gyeonggi's west coast. The draws are hands-on: fishing-boat rides, bare-hand fish catching, and king-prawn catching, plus surprise seafood auctions, a dried-seafood wholesale market, and salted-shrimp making. Evenings bring the Moonlight Concert and opening and closing fireworks over the water. Free, 10:00–22:00 — Seoul's nearest taste of working-port festival culture.

title: Daejeon Donggu-dongnak Festival
overview: A festival behind Daejeon Station, spreading through the east plaza and along the Daedongcheon stream — the gateway to Soje-dong's retro cafe alley and the old railway officials' village. World-food theme booths, all-ages game zones, a streamside 'booknic' of books and rest, a bakery competition (this is the city of bakeries), and chef cooking shows give it an urban, food-forward flavor distinct from Korea's rural festivals. Free, 11:00–22:00.
place: Soje-dong east plaza and Daedongcheon stream

title: Sejong and Paik: Hangeul Culture Special Exhibition 2026
overview: An exhibition pairing two Korean innovators five centuries apart: King Sejong, who created the Hangeul alphabet in the 1440s, and Nam June Paik, who invented video art in the 1960s. The argument is that both remade how people communicate. It runs from 9 October — Hangeul Day — to 8 November at the Biennale Hall in Sejong City, the administrative capital named after the king. Free, with volunteer-led tours at 14:00 and 16:00, Tuesday to Sunday. Tours are in Korean.

title: Silla Culture Festival
overview: Gyeongju's flagship festival since 1962, now in its 53rd edition, staged among the city's actual Silla monuments. The Hwabaek ceremony reenacts royal history against Woljeonggyo Bridge; a street-arts festival and Silk Road Festa fill the historic quarter; and the Hwarang Hip-hop Festa puts Korea's top hip-hop acts on stage in front of ancient burial mounds — a collision of eras you will only see here. The Moonlight Market adds local food into the night. Free, 15:00–24:00.

title: Damyang Heritage Night Walk
overview: Damyang after dark, staged around Gwanbangjerim — a riverside forest planted in the 1600s to hold back floods and now a national monument — plus the stone flagpole supports at Gaeksa-ri and the five-storey pagoda at Namsan-ri. The programme tells the stories of people Damyang produced: a street play about the magistrate who built the forest, a madang changgeuk honouring Yi Nal-chi, the great Joseon pansori singer born here, a talk concert with piano beneath the flagpole supports, and a family mission built on the Taoist trickster Jeon U-chi, who is said to have trained at Damyang's Yeondongsa Temple. Free, with some market stalls and activities charged.
sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Jeonnam-Gwangju · Damyang County

title: Incheon Open Port Heritage Night Tour
overview: The 11th night festival in Incheon's open-port quarter — the district of 1880s customs houses, banks, and warehouses where modern Korea first met the world. The classic '8 nights' program (night views, night roads, night history, night food, night market and more) threads performances, exhibitions, and food through three evenings of specially opened heritage buildings, with lodging promotions for those who stay. Free, 18:00–22:00; Chinatown and Songwol-dong's fairytale village are next door.
